title: Full audit of mhfe with independent verification of every finding

reviewer.name: Claude Code coordinator with 162 sub-agents (8 scoped reviewers, finding skeptics, a completeness critic and 5 gap reviewers) and 8 record writers

snapshot.workingTree: HEAD plus uncommitted changes: Codex's AUD-021 host-protection fixes (src/bin/mhfe/made_password.rs, protect.rs, settings.rs, terminal.rs), the self-test label change (src/bin/mhfe/main.rs, self_test.rs), docs/releases/unreleased.md, docs/audits/README.md and the uncommitted AUD-020, AUD-021 and AUD-022 records
snapshot.manifestRule: SHA-256 of the path-sorted 'sha256  path' rows of every tracked or untracked, not ignored file outside docs/audits/

scope.repository: mhfe (library, command-line tool, WebAssembly browser package)
scope.specification: mhfe_spec README.md and docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md at its working tree
excluded: Full-cost vector replays (about an hour each), excluded by the owner
macOS and Windows execution beyond the exact-commit CI logs
A foreign host's application (the multi-chain Deriver)
environment: emcc (Emscripten gcc/clang-like replacement + linker emulating GNU ld) 6.0.12 (5488e0871d46d19a3209988190fa6a653126256f)

entries.check: CHECK-SEC-001 Threat model and secret ownership (native: phrase, password, passphrase, round key, state)
entries.method: Traced every secret from input to consumer in the library and CLI: memory.rs, password.rs, feistel.rs, phrase.rs, mhfe.rs, container.rs, rekey.rs, hidden.rs, new_password.rs, wallet_check.rs, rehearsal.rs, check_word.rs, word_hints.rs, word_wishes.rs, wallet.rs (seed/keys), then the CLI readers and displays (terminal.rs, hidden_input.rs, typed_line.rs, choice.rs, check_word.rs, made_password.rs, diceware.rs, encrypt/decrypt/rekey/new_wallet/wallets/check/chosen_words). Checked Debug/Display, Clone, field privacy, copies, reveal/export paths and private-screen guards. Live: a release-binary encrypt run read from /proc at its first secret prompt; a pseudo-terminal probe of `mhfe password`; heap probes of hint rows and check-word labels.
entries.evidence: Library secret types keep private LockedText/LockedBytes/Zeroizing fields, implement no Display, and only redacting Debug (Password password.rs:88-92, LockedBytes memory.rs:143-147, WordWishes word_wishes.rs:96-100). AUD-012-SEC002 is fixed in source (RecoveredPhrase keeps a private LockedText, mhfe.rs:97-104). AUD-014-SEC002 is fixed in source (word_wishes.rs:84-100). CLI secrets are read into locked buffers of fixed capacity (terminal.rs:424-442, hidden_input.rs:394-418). Phrases are shown only on private screens, and new, wallets, made passwords and the rekey owner comparison refuse without one. Two Low findings: hint rows copy typed phrase and password words into unwiped strings; `mhfe password` prints on the main screen without a private screen. Both AUD-020 fixes are present; their file hashes equal AUD-021's after-hashes.
entries.limits: Windows and macOS runtimes were not executed. Dependency internals were not audited line by line. Same-user and root attackers are bounded by the documented threat model.

entries.scope: gap:Secret lifecycle in the browser package (WebAssembly, workers and the Emscripten Argon2 heap)
entries.check: CHECK-SEC-001 (browser half: secret ownership from page to WebAssembly, workers and the Emscripten Argon2 heap)
entries.method: Read every file of the gap scope in full. web/runtime.js, web/client.js, web/worker-runtime.js, web/worker-start.js, web/core-worker.js and the wallet, passwords and repair worker tables: encodeSecret, the transfer lists, wipeSecrets on the page and in the worker, and the answers of asks. target/wasm-bindgen/mhfe.js: Vec<u8> arguments are copied by passArray8ToWasm0, and secret results are decoded from linear memory by __wbindgen_string_new, so the JS side makes no copy. src/wasm_api/mod.rs SecretText and secret_json. Every export and session of src/wasm_api/core.rs. The wasm32 branches of src/memory.rs. src/engine/browser.rs and web/argon2-engine.js: the slices are views, and the C-heap copies are wiped and freed in finally. src/hidden.rs. The vendored reference argon2.c, from argon2id_hash_raw through argon2_hash and argon2_ctx, and core.c: initialize, finalize, free_memory, secure_wipe_memory and the wipes in blake2b.c. Then measured: the real dist/runtime/worker.js runs in Node with a stand-in self and the real argon2-st build at reduced round cost (256 KiB, 1 pass; known answers unchanged). Linear memory and the Emscripten HEAPU8 were scanned for the synthetic passwords and passphrase, phrase text, entropy, BIP39 seeds, BIP32 master keys and chain codes, Argon2 round keys and salts, and H0 (this construction was checked against RFC 9106 section 5.3). Copies that a fresh instance already holds were excluded.
entries.evidence: Intended holders confirmed: a hidden session holds the main passphrase and each used password (1 heap copy each). A rekey owner wait holds the old and new password and the phrase. A check noLength wait holds the entropy. After free() or the end of an operation these are at 0. The Emscripten heap of both builds holds 0 copies of the password, H0, salt or key after a derive and at session waits: argon2-builds.log shows 2475 non-zero bytes (single-threaded) and 13026 (threaded) out of 16 MiB; h0.log and run1.log agree. Round keys: 0 in either heap. The drawn phrase's entropy and random fills: 0 (probe2.log case I). Residue left by compiler and dependency copies on the shadow stack (offsets below 1 MiB): BIP32 master key and chain code, BIP39 seeds, the entropy, and the passphrase in bip39's PBKDF2 salt block (see the DOC finding and observation O1). Probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/gap-browser-secret-lifecycle/probe.mjs (sha256 9ec4bbd0...984a); log run1.log (sha256 2cfd7551...1ef4); inputs dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm cdd9e5e4...f9c, dist/runtime/worker.js 50526ef1...b27b, dist/core/argon2-st.js 1780eced...512, target/wasm-bindgen/mhfe.js 3161c2d9...22f.
entries.limits: Node/V8 only, not Chromium or Firefox. JavaScript heap strings were not scanned; they are documented as unwipeable. Argon2 rounds ran at reduced cost. The threaded build was measured through the bridge only, not inside a worker session. Browser process memory, swap and crash dumps are out of reach. The probes live in the tmp scratch folder and are not committed.

entries.check: CHECK-SEC-002 Sandbox and transport (native isolation, serve exemption)
entries.method: Read protect.rs isolate/seccomp/Landlock/namespace/probes/IsolationCheck, main.rs prepare order, menu.rs command threads, startup.rs, serve.rs. Reviewed the baseline-check.log runtime tests. Live /proc read-back of a running `mhfe encrypt` (release binary sha256 cec75011…) at its first prompt.
entries.evidence: The BPF filter refuses foreign arch, x32, socket, socketpair and io_uring_setup/enter/register with EACCES (protect.rs:617-698). Landlock handles every file-system-changing right for each ABI, plus TCP bind/connect from ABI 4 (protect.rs:740-805). The namespace is entered single-threaded, before the startup threads (main.rs:289-291, protect.rs:570-604). Probes downgrade claims, and the summary states only confirmed boundaries (protect.rs:310-417, settings.rs:353-374). Live: Seccomp 2, Seccomp_filters 1, NoNewPrivs 1, summary 'isolated network, no new sockets or file writes (kernel-enforced)' (readback/probe.log sha256 2484550974f9…). Baseline passes: an_isolated_thread_cannot_open_a_socket_or_write_a_file, landlock_refuses_opening_dev_null_for_writing, a_process_with_one_thread_gets_an_empty_network, the_empty_network_is_entered_before_the_startup_checks_start_threads, and PTY 'isolation: a command started directly runs with an empty network'. serve: 127.0.0.1:0, exact Host, GET/HEAD '/', 16 connections, 16 KiB head, 10 s deadlines, page checked by SHA-256 and held in RAM, no secret (serve.rs:41-60, 219-265, 287-345, 400-436).
entries.limits: Inherited descriptors and threads created before isolation (the menu thread, the ctrlc thread in the menu) are not covered, by documented design. macOS and Windows have no sandbox (documented). The menu path was not run live by this reviewer.

entries.scope: gap:The fast-mode serving path (mhfe serve and the Python launcher) was never run with a real browser
entries.check: CHECK-SEC-002 (transport of the fast-mode server: headers, Host check, header CSP combined with the page's meta CSP, cross-origin isolation)
entries.method: Real-browser runs on loopback. I built a fresh browser-check page from the current dist/ (buildId 4f5000f4290fa5eb). I used a scratch copy of scripts/build-browser-check.mjs that writes into the probe folder, so nothing was written to the repository. I served the page through target/release/mhfe serve (SHA-256 cec75011...0746, current with the working tree) and through packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py (byte-identical to dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py). Each was opened at #check, the full self-check of all four classes, in Playwright 1.64.0 Chromium and Firefox. The script recorded response headers, crossOriginIsolated, client.mode(), the threaded Argon2 part, every request and page errors. It also requested http://localhost:PORT/, /index.html and /favicon.ico. The same page over file:// served as the contrast.
entries.evidence: run-launchers.log (sha256 bb82ffca...667e): Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Firefox 157.0, via both mhfe serve and mhfe-fast-mode.py. Every run gave status 200 and all seven SECURITY_HEADERS (COOP same-origin, COEP require-corp, CSP frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, no-referrer, no-store). Every run showed crossOriginIsolated true, SharedArrayBuffer function, "mode: fast" and "Argon2id at 64 and 256 MiB, threaded build: passed". MhfeClient, MhfeRepair, MhfePasswords and MhfeWallet each passed fullCheck(): 54 component lines, none failed; SUMMARY: PASS in 2.7-3.2 s. No request other than the page and blob: workers, and no page error. localhost:PORT gave 403 "403 Forbidden", so the browser's own Host 127.0.0.1:PORT is accepted and any other host is refused. /index.html and /favicon.ico gave 404. file:// gave crossOriginIsolated false, "mode: standard" and the threaded part "notRun (the page is not cross-origin isolated)". The response header frame-ancestors combined with the page's meta CSP blocked nothing the page needs. The menu route showed the same: menu-route.log (sha256 acadb8a4...0aaf).
entries.limits: Linux, headless Playwright builds only. No WebKit or Safari (the docs make no claim for them), no Windows or macOS launcher run. Python 3.14.4 only; the Python 3.8 claim was checked against the 3.8 grammar only. DNS rebinding was shown through the Host value (localhost), not with a real rebinding domain. The full-cost #all and #selftest pages were not opened (2 GiB).

entries.check: CHECK-SEC-003 Network egress and secret guards
entries.method: Searched src for std::net, sockets, HTTP clients and Command spawns. Reviewed how error and refusal messages are built, the summary records, and the serve path.
entries.evidence: Network and process code exist only in serve.rs (TcpListener on loopback, xdg-open/open/cmd start of a generated http://127.0.0.1:port/ URL) and in tests. Secret commands cannot create sockets (seccomp EACCES read back live and by IsolationCheck). Library errors carry positions and counts, never input text (phrase.rs:40-70, wallet.rs:330-340, mhfe.rs:419-429, repair.rs:402-406). Failure messages are MhfeError Display (exit.rs). Summary records name counts and kinds only (check_word.rs:44-55, choice.rs:239-241, check.rs:557-606: the reference is recorded only once parsed, AUD-015-SEC001 fix present).
entries.limits: No fuzzing of error paths. The guard is not a defence against arbitrary malicious code inside the process.

entries.method: Static trace of every production random source and of the encryption parameters against the specification, plus independent reviewer probes without Argon2. Randomness: src/random.rs (RandomSource, check_source, uniform_below), src/random/health.rs (check_spread, ScriptedSource), src/bin/mhfe/system_random.rs (getrandom::fill), src/wasm_api/mod.rs:270-292 with web/worker-runtime.js:60-62 (crypto.getRandomValues filling a view of module memory), src/wallet_check.rs try_draws/draw/read_back and src/wallet_check/threads.rs, src/new_password.rs make/characters_from. Encryption: src/engine/{mod,native,ffi,browser}.rs (Argon2id type 2, version 0x13, 4 lanes on 4 threads, 16-byte salt, 32-byte tag, empty secret and associated data, m(MEM)/t(PIM), key-written guard), src/suite.rs, src/feistel.rs, src/password.rs, src/mhfe.rs.
entries.evidence: ScriptedSource and lcg_source are referenced only from known_answers modules and #[cfg(test)] code (grep); production sources are getrandom (CLI) and crypto.getRandomValues (browser), both probed by check_source (two 32-byte probes, all-zero/equal refused) before a draw; uniform_below uses 1 or 2 bytes with rejection above values/n*n (n=57: 228; n=7776: 62,208). Argon2 call: ffi.rs:140-165 maps passes, memory_kib, lanes=threads=4, version 0x13, ARGON2_ID=2 (argon2.h Argon2_id = 2); m(21)=3*2^30 KiB fits u32 (suite.rs:242-245); NativeEngine refuses memory the OS does not report free and 32-bit builds; browser refuses levels above 0. Password rule probe (probes/core-crypto/assigned_table.py): the pinned unicode-normalization 0.1.25 is_public_assigned table plus src/password.rs Private Use ranges agrees with unicodedata2 17.0.0 General_Category != Cn on all 1,112,064 scalar values (0 mismatches); Cc count 65 + U+2028/2029 = 67, as src/password.rs:151-160 asserts. Oracle `independent-suite3.py passwords`: all 33 password cases reproduced with Unicode 17.0.0. Salts are derived per round from the unchanged half (no stored salt, no nonce by design); no authentication by design (spec Security Considerations); a wrong password yields a valid phrase labelled not verified; invalid words, checksums, counts and suite/length mismatches are refused before any Argon2 call (mhfe.rs:995-1102 tests; oracle `independent-suite4.py validation`: 63 refusals consistent); decryption errors carry no reading (VerifierMismatch, LengthDiffers, AmbiguousLength carry lengths only).
entries.limits: No full-cost Argon2 or vector replay was run (audit resource rule); Argon2 known answers and RFC 9106 binding were taken from the coordinator's baseline-check.log (344 library tests passed). The live browser random source was not exercised by this reviewer (baseline-browsers.log covers the package). Gordian Envelope, permits, recipients and nonce uniqueness are not-applicable: MHFE has no permits and is deterministic by design.

entries.scope: gap:Tracked source files that no reviewer read in full
entries.check: CHECK-SEC-004 (randomness evidence for the chosen-word draw: src/word_wishes/statistics.rs)
entries.method: Read statistics.rs (569 lines), src/word_wishes.rs (541 lines) and PhraseDraw::try_draws/draw (wallet_check.rs:165-268) in full. Re-derived each probability model: bit marginals with one excluded word, adjacent-bit and cross-word joints, the birthday repeat rate, the 'anywhere' multiplicity conditioned on at least one occurrence, and the Laurent-Massart chi-square bound. Checked that every statistic has a deliberately faulty control that it refuses. Confirmed that the deterministic streams cannot reach production.
entries.evidence: The tests drive the production rejection loop `PhraseDraw::unchecked().with_wishes(..).try_draws(source, ..)` (statistics.rs:149-163), not a copy of it. The controls are: clobbered bit and counter pattern for the balance check (:488-502); excluded word drawn (:491-493); identical draws for the repeat check (:503-504); copied bit for the correlation check (:507-513); opposite per-position biases that cancel when pooled (:517-536); fixed placement and random-position insertion for the anywhere checks (:539-568). All 9 statistics tests passed on this tree (baseline-check.log:333-365; statistics.rs SHA-256 f0823ff5… matches the initial manifest). SplitMix64 exists only under cfg(test) (word_wishes.rs:29-30). xorshift32 is private to the word-wishes self-check (known_answers.rs:97, used only at :125). Production phrases come from getrandom (src/bin/mhfe/system_random.rs:11), behind check_source (random.rs:52-64) in PhraseDraw::draw (wallet_check.rs:259).
entries.limits: These are fixed-seed regression tests of the wish logic, not evidence about source quality; statistics.rs:11-12 says so. They cannot detect a uniform-looking but low-entropy source, which is the Milk Sad case (a 32-bit-seeded PRNG). Draws with the wallet check and the multi-thread draw_on_every_core path are not sampled. Tracing the production RNG source belongs to the core-crypto reviewer.

entries.check: CHECK-SEC-005 Secret lifecycle and exceptional paths (zeroize, mlock, DONTDUMP, core dumps, signals, panics, private screen, swap warning)
entries.method: Read memory.rs, ffi.rs, native.rs, engine/mod.rs, argon2_simd.c, build.rs and the vendored core.c/opt.c/ref.c wipe calls. Read feistel.rs, protect.rs, terminal.rs, hidden_input.rs, startup.rs panic hook and Cargo.toml profile. Ran allocator-hook and /proc/self/mem heap-residue probes, with and without hints and with positive controls. Ran a live encrypt at its prompt and sent Ctrl+C. Read the PTY harness results in baseline-check.log.
entries.evidence: LockedText/LockedBytes reserve, lock, fill, then wipe before unlocking, with field order (memory.rs:18-141). Pages shared by guards are counted (memory.rs:274-348). The work area is wiped by the C code (FLAG_clear_internal_memory, test reuses_one_work_area_and_leaves_it_wiped) and by Rust on a failed call (ffi.rs:181-189), and is MADV_DONTDUMP (ffi.rs:286-298). The round key is marked unwritten and checked (engine/mod.rs:41-64), and RoundValues is ZeroizeOnDrop (feistel.rs:195-205). Release builds use panic=abort (Cargo.toml). Live: core limit 0/0, environ and mem of the process denied to the same user (non-dumpable), Ctrl+C exit 130 with the alternate screen left. SIGTERM/SIGHUP (ctrlc termination) and Ctrl+\/Ctrl+Z (protect.rs:55-87, terminal.rs:334-344) are covered by baseline PTY cases. The AUD-020-SEC001 fix is verified in source and tests. Two Low findings: hint rows hold phrase words unwiped (heap probe: 7 of 12 words left, 0 of 12 without hints), and a zram swap device with a writeback backing device is exempt from the swap warning. Observations cover allocator-level residue of check-word labels, unwiped hash/MAC dependency states, Argon2 thread-stack residue and the std stdin buffer.
entries.limits: Exit after Ctrl+C deliberately skips wiping (documented). No forced paging, hibernation or zram-writeback host was available. Windows and macOS were not run. The heap residue measured depends on glibc's allocator.

entries.scope: gap:Secret lifecycle in the browser package (WebAssembly, workers and the Emscripten Argon2 heap)
entries.check: CHECK-SEC-005 (browser half: exceptional paths, Rust panic/abort, WASM linear-memory residuals)
entries.method: Cargo.toml has panic=abort and src/ installs no panic hook, so a panic becomes an 'unreachable' trap with no text. The trap path of each operation was traced through core-worker.js, worker-runtime.js, the wasm-bindgen glue and the wasm-bindgen 0.2.129 free and borrow codegen in the cargo registry. Real traps were then forced inside operations. Before the operation, memory.grow takes the core's memory to its maximum. In the middle of a round, the core's allocator is then exhausted, and the next Rust allocation aborts. This ran for a hidden-wallet open (E), a rekey recovery (F) and a decrypt (G), and once more behind the page's real WorkerJob from dist/runtime/runtime.js with a stand-in Worker (E2). Residue was measured at every wait and after every end: cases A to D and I.
entries.evidence: A trap is posted as an error, the page's WorkerJob stops, and the worker is terminated (E2: job ended, worker terminated, 0 messages sent afterwards). After a trap the session's Drop never runs: case E leaves 3 heap copies of the second password plus the passphrase and first password in linear memory, freed only by termination. The worker's finally still wipes the JS request copies. The worker does call the trapped instance again: the glue's __wbindgen_add_to_stack_pointer, session free() and, in rekey, ownerLengths(). wasm-bindgen's ownership and borrow guards refuse these calls with thrown errors, and the free() error masks the trap (finding API, low). Shadow-stack residues are recorded in observation O1 and the DOC finding.
entries.limits: Allocation failure is the trap trigger here; no reachable Rust panic was found in the scope (capacity bounds in password.rs, check_word.rs and wallet.rs hold). Tab switching, blur, hidden document and reload belong to the embedding page, the multi-chain Deriver, and are not in this package; not-applicable here for that reason.

coverage.group: Browser injection, persistence and sensitive APIs

entries.method: Searched web/*.js and the built dist/*/*.js (worker.js, argon2-mt.js, argon2-st.js, runtime.js, client.js, wallet.js) for DOM sinks, storage, console, eval/new Function/importScripts/dynamic import, network APIs; reviewed Blob URL revocation, postMessage targets, crypto.getRandomValues use, error texts for echoed input (library messages of address/fingerprint/path/coin/word-wish refusals), and the CSP the browser test applies (no 'unsafe-eval', 'wasm-unsafe-eval', connect-src 'none', worker-src blob:).
entries.evidence: No localStorage/sessionStorage/indexedDB/document/innerHTML/console/eval/new Function in web/*.js; eval/new Function/importScripts/import( count 0 in every dist script; 'fetch' only in comments (runtime.js:8, client.js:7, worker.js:1994); Emscripten built with -sDYNAMIC_EXECUTION=0 (scripts/build-argon2-wasm.sh:51); the only new Worker() in argon2-mt.js takes the Blob passed as mainScriptUrlOrBlob; WorkerJob revokes its Blob URL on terminate (runtime.js:206-213); verify-browsers.mjs:4430-4438 policy and stray-request check (4498-4523) passed in both browsers.
entries.limits: Generated glue reviewed lexically. No static gate counts dynamic code in the package scripts (observation).

entries.check: CHECK-SEC-007 Read-only guarantees and availability bounds
entries.method: Read every bounded input and allocation path, the free-memory and cgroup checks, the LockedText::build capacity callers, the serve limits and the Landlock write refusal.
entries.evidence: Typed and script lines are at most 8192 bytes in fixed locked buffers, and longer ones are refused (terminal.rs:28-31, 418-442; hidden_input.rs:486-495; tests a_longer_line_is_refused, a_line_over_the_capacity_or_invalid_utf8_is_refused). A password is at most 1024 bytes after NFKD (password.rs:22, 56-71). The passphrase NFKD buffer is sized at 11 times the input (wallet.rs:1047-1068, U+FDFA bound). Every LockedText/LockedBytes::build capacity is the final size (phrase.rs:107, check_word.rs:334/356, new_password.rs:172/212, feistel.rs:232/272, packing.rs:69, password.rs:56, terminal.rs:427, hidden_input.rs:403) and is asserted. Settings are checked before secrets: memory level and MemAvailable/cgroup room (native.rs:155-211, ffi.rs:385-406, cgroup.rs) and a clean MemoryAllocation refusal (ffi.rs:223-236). serve limits are as above. Secret commands cannot write files (Landlock, read back). There is no transaction or spend capability.
entries.limits: No load, fuzz or stress run. On systems that report no free-memory figure, an oversize level relies on the allocation itself (documented).

entries.scope: gap:The fast-mode serving path (mhfe serve and the Python launcher) was never run with a real browser
entries.check: CHECK-SEC-007 (availability bounds of both launchers; supplementary to the assigned checks)
entries.method: Probed the connection cap and the request deadline of the release program, and the Python response deadline. Fed the Python serve loop a stand-in listener whose accept() raises ConnectionAbortedError.
entries.evidence: The cap and the deadlines hold in both launchers (probe-limits-a.txt, probe-limits-bcd.txt). The Python serve() returns after a single accept error, and main() then reports success (finding 5).
entries.limits: The accept error was injected; it was not provoked from a real socket on Linux.

entries.method: Read src/phrase.rs, src/packing.rs, src/detection.rs, src/phrase/known_answers.rs, src/wallet_check.rs and wallet::bip39_seed; compared word reading, checksum, entropy widths, byte/bit order and the separation of entropy, packed state, BIP39 seed and passphrase with the specification; recomputed all published vectors from the specification text with an own Python script using only the recorded Argon2id outputs.
entries.evidence: phrase.rs:40-71 accepts 12/15/18/21/24 words only, any whitespace and ASCII case, exact word first then a unique prefix of >= 4 letters (complete_word :154-167), rejects everything else with positions only; bip39 3.0.0 checks the checksum. src/phrase/known_answers.rs uses BIP-0039 vectors including all-0x00, 0x7f, 0x80 and all-0xff entropies at 12/18/24 words. Packing (packing.rs:247-283) writes X = E || Trunc_r(SHA-256(E)) in digest byte order; detection tests all four layouts (detection.rs:25-31). Probe probes/core-crypto/feistel_recorded_keys.py recomputed packing, every round's salt input/salt/mask input/mask/states in both directions, the container words and the recovery readings under the length rules for all 17 suite 3 and 10 suite 4 vectors: all reproduced. The BIP39 seed and the 16-bit check use NFKD of the passphrase separately from the MHFE password (wallet.rs:1055-1068); probe wallet_check.py reproduced both published digests and the three failing variants. The Keep list names the BIP39 passphrase separately from the container (operation.rs:136-167).
entries.limits: Full-cost Argon2 not run; the probe trusts the recorded Argon2id outputs, which the project's independent-verification.json records as reproduced with OpenSSL.

entries.method: I read every file in scope line by line: src/wallet.rs, src/wallet/known_answers.rs, src/rehearsal.rs and its known answers, src/search.rs and its known answers, src/wasm_api/wallet.rs, the reference parsing in src/wasm_api/core.rs, src/bin/mhfe/check.rs and container_search.rs, and src/wallet_check.rs. I checked the code against BIP32, BIP39, BIP44/49/84/86, BIP173/350, BIP341, EIP-55, CashAddr, SLIP-44 and DIP17/18, and against the specification's rehearsal and re-encryption rules (mhfe_spec/README.md lines 465-532). I recomputed every known answer with a pure-Python implementation that does not import mhfe: secp256k1, BIP32, PBKDF2 from hashlib, Keccak-256, Bech32/Bech32m, Base58Check, CashAddr, EIP-55 and the BIP86 tweak. The Rust tables were parsed straight from the source. I also ran an exhaustive scan of NFKD byte growth over every code point. For test results I read the coordinator's baseline-check.log and baseline-browsers.log.
entries.evidence: probes/wallet-derivation/independent-rerun.log: 104 PASS, 0 failures. The run used the current tree; the SHA-256 of src/wallet.rs, wallet/known_answers.rs, search.rs, search/known_answers.rs, rehearsal.rs and rehearsal/known_answers.rs equals initial-manifest.txt. It covers: 24 Trezor English seeds with "TREZOR"; the NFKD bytes of the Unicode passphrase (43616665cc81…) and its seed (d0d474bd…); master fingerprints 73c5da0a and b4e3f5ed; BIP32 vector 1 (key, chain code, public key, fingerprint 3442193e); BIP32 vector 3, the leading-zero master key (00ddb80b…) and m/0H; vector 4 (leading zero in a hardened child) as an independent cross-check; all 43 address rows at their paths, every coin and profile (Bitcoin 44/49/84/86 receive and change, mainnet and testnet, account 3/change/index 7, the TREZOR-passphrase row, Ethereum, XRP, Tron, Zcash, Dogecoin, Bitcoin Cash in both forms and both roots, Litecoin L/M/ltc1q, Ethereum Classic on both roots, Cosmos, Injective, Dash X, Dash DIP17 classes 0'/1'); the search answer bc1q4du7… at m/84'/0'/2'/1/19; the three Dash Desktop tdash1 vectors at m/9'/1'/17'/0'/0'/i; the 9 damaged addresses, each one character from a table row; the wallet-hash digests; the four wallet-check vectors. search_answers-rerun.log: candidates of zero-12 with word 3 missing (7, first 'bubble', real at 7) and word 24 missing (8, 'brave', real at 6); decoy fingerprint 487a156e. The DIP17 mainnet rows equal multi-chain-wallet-tools packages/coin-protocols/tests/dash-platform.test.ts (official DIP17/18 vectors). Under Unicode 16 the largest NFKD growth is U+FDFA, 3 to 33 bytes, which is exactly NFKD_MAX_GROWTH = 11 at src/wallet.rs:1048. Code review confirmed: (1) the path parser is strict (m prefix, ' or h, index < 2^31, no empty steps, signs, spaces or 'H'), and src/wallet.rs:694-705 accepts leading zeros ('m/007'' reads as m/7'), which is harmless. (2) SearchLimits accept 1..=2^31 (wallet.rs:740-752). (3) Master key zero or ≥ n, IL ≥ n and a zero child are refused, not skipped (wallet.rs:1084-1090, 1126-1136). (4) Keys are fixed 32-byte arrays, so leading zeros are kept. (5) The Taproot tweak takes P with even y, and t ≥ n or Q = infinity is refused (1015-1034). (6) The Bech32/Bech32m variant follows the witness version through bech32::segwit. (7) Cosmos accounts must use Bech32 with exactly 32 groups (AUD-007-FUN001/FUN003 still fixed). (8) DIP18 payloads must be 34 groups with zero padding (AUD-008-FUN001 still fixed). (9) EIP-55 is enforced only on mixed case. (10) CashAddr checks case, polymod and padding. The phrase input is &str and is never changed. baseline-check.log: 344 library tests passed, including every wallet::, search:: and rehearsal:: test and the wallet.rs doc-test. baseline-browsers.log: the MhfeWallet startup check passed in 131 ms; address, fingerprint, passphrase, path and refusal cases passed in Chromium and Firefox.

entries.method: Mapped every MUST/SHOULD/MAY of mhfe_spec/README.md:465-567 (Application requirements), plus the application text of Creating (365-393), Recovering (395-438), Work factor (453-463), suite 4 (602-671), MHFE-WALLET-CHECK-SEED-1 (675-708), MHFE-REPAIR-1 (744-806) and MHFE-PASSWORD-CHECK-1 (845-863), to the library module that enforces it, the CLI module that shows it and the browser binding or BROWSER-PACKAGE.md duty. Two reduced-cost probes: the rehearsal outcome through the built package's CheckSession on the published ambiguous-12-21 phrase and the library's public wallet-check test phrase with TREZOR; the CLI rekey warning in a pty, cancelled before any Argon2 work.
entries.evidence: Requirement map (library / CLI / browser). Distinct workflow: no word-count guessing outside the spec's recovery workflow, containerFingerprint derived openly and labelled 'not the wallet' (client.d.ts:128-129). SHOULD keep the original backup until a receiving address matches is in README.md:221-224 but missing from BROWSER-PACKAGE.md (F3). Checking the finished backup: encrypt.rs:172-179, new_wallet.rs:155-161 'rehearse with mhfe check from the backup you wrote'; BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:939-943. Rehearsal MUST NOT display/export/persist: RecoveredForCheck in LockedBytes, only CheckEvidence leaves (rehearsal.rs:256-273); CLI prints outcome lines only (check.rs:326-376); browser CheckSession.compare returns {matches,path,evidence} (core.rs:527-550). Outcome categories 'not verified' and 'the lengths that match' are missing (F2; probe rehearsal_outcomes.out). Stating the bounded search first: check.rs:398-414; MhfeWallet.describeAddress. 'Reference SHOULD NOT be stored next to the container' is in README.md:236 but not in the browser guidance (F3). Re-encryption: (1) confirm the source MUST: Rekey takes a Confirmation in every path (src/rekey.rs:146-243). (2) when the verifier is enough: Confirmation::refuse_for (rehearsal.rs:430-441) plus RecoveredForRekey::confirm, which returns LengthDiffers, AmbiguousLength or VerifierMismatch (rehearsal.rs:533-579); tests at src/rekey.rs:627-705 and 770-797; the same library serves the CLI (bin rekey.rs:200-254) and the browser (core.rs:970-1012). (3) reading without a verifier: the owner's explicit yes is needed, since seal refuses awaits_owner (src/rekey.rs:259-262); the CLI asks with no default (bin rekey.rs:509-544); the browser accepts only the value true (core.rs:1057-1072). (4) complete creation procedure: seal runs Encryption::run with check_new_container (operation.rs:205-235). (5) replacement rehearsal reference before creation: CLI bin rekey.rs:298-313. The browser leaves it to the page (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:269-272), which is the concurrent ARC finding. Preserving derived wallets: the CLI warns before the container is read (bin rekey.rs:147-151; probe rekey_warning.out), asks nothing, and states non-revocation (bin rekey.rs:353-358). The browser has no API for this (F1). Resources: the CLI's Ctrl+C ends the process at any moment (terminal.rs:330-363), and free memory is checked before secrets (settings.rs:444-448). The browser's cancel() terminates the worker, and its memory limits are documented (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:739-749). The level>0 reminder is partial (O6). Parallel lanes MUST: the native engine runs four lanes on four threads (engine/native.rs:24,146-147). The browser's fast mode is threaded, and the standard-mode warning is a page duty (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:937-938). Passwords: encrypt.rs:465 'Letter case and spaces count', the weak warning at encrypt.rs:506-516, README.md:172-210; BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:788-804. Work factor: the CLI shows 'PIM 0 and memory level 0' (settings.rs:188-206), and both front ends get the keep list from the library's Keep (operation.rs:140-167). The browser guidance never asks for defaults shown as 0 or empty (F3). Suite 4: chosen only on request (encrypt.rs:280-300; sameLength defaults to false), suite id shown after creation, consequences shown (length_choice.rs:116-125, partial wording in O6). Wallet-check profile MUST explain: the CLI explains under '?' (new_wallet.rs:199-222; O5), and the browser guidance is incomplete (F3). Repair profile MUSTs: checksum and bound enforced in repair.rs:394-432, changes shown before use. The SHOULDs on card numbering, keeping it apart and guarding it are met by the CLI (container_repair.rs:647-677) and absent from the browser guidance (F3). Check word: repairs only on an explicit choice, passwordRepair defaults to asTyped.
entries.limits: Read-only mapping. Probes ran at reduced Argon2 cost (256 KiB, 1 pass), so no full-cost run. Sensitive-memory and no-network requirements (spec 556-567) are covered by other reviewers and were not re-run. entries.check: CHECK-FUN-006 (published round table that the cipher-rounds self-check replays)
entries.method: Read scripts/generate-published-rounds.py (161 lines) in full, src/mhfe/published_rounds.rs (1,857 lines: structure, all 27 headers with their same_length/startup/pim/memory_level flags, sampled rounds), and src/mhfe/known_answers.rs (1,224 lines) in full. Ran the generator in --check mode. Checked the fixture SHA256SUMS. Compared the fixture bytes with mhfe_spec/vectors. Traced how the startup set is chosen (STARTUP list, then the `startup` flag, then the filter at known_answers.rs:549-553).
entries.evidence: `python3 scripts/generate-published-rounds.py --check` exited 0. `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` passed in both tests/fixtures/suite3-vectors and suite4-vectors. All 27 vector JSON files are byte-identical to mhfe_spec/vectors/suite3 and suite4; the only differences are the mhfe-local independent-verification.json records and where validation-cases.json is kept, which is identical too (92ced6ea…, 541826d4…). The startup flags in the table are exactly the generator's STARTUP list of 10 names (generate-published-rounds.py:27-38): ambiguous-12-21, nonzero-15, unicode-password, zero-12-pim-1-memory-level-1, zero-12, zero-24, same-length-nonzero-21, same-length-unicode-password, same-length-zero-12, same-length-zero-18. Three things guard the table. `published_round_table_equals_the_fixtures` (known_answers.rs:768-953) compares every value, including the decryption salts as a subset; it passed (baseline-check.log:101). `hex()` is a const fn that rejects wrong lengths at compile time (self_check.rs:453-466). The `rounds: [PublishedRound; crate::ROUNDS]` type stops the generator's ROUNDS=12 copy from drifting silently. PublishedRoundKeys is used only by the known_answers modules (grep). On startup coverage: the cipher-rounds startup set encrypts suite 3 at 12, 15 and 24 words and suite 4 at 12, 15, 18 and 21. The startup `formats` check packs 12, 15, 18, 21 and 24 words against known states (validation-cases.json length_detection packed-12..24), and the 21-word reading is recovered from ambiguous-12-21. So the generator's comment 'every phrase length's packing in either suite' holds across the two startup checks together.
entries.limits: The table's Argon2 keys are trusted as recorded; only the release-time full-cost vector replays and the independent scripts recompute them, and I did not run those, as the rules required. The Rust test pins only the size of the startup set (:952), not its names. See the observation on this.

entries.method: Only part of this check applies: the offline, bounded address search that the rehearsal check, rekey confirmation and the missing-word search use. entries.evidence: The search covers accounts 0..accounts-1 (hardened), both chains (0/1, or hardened 0'/1' for DIP17 key classes) and indexes 0..indexes-1 under each root. The roots come from AddressType::purpose and Coin::coin_types; testnet uses coin type 1, and Bitcoin Cash and Ethereum Classic each have two roots (src/wallet.rs:306-321, 961-986). Bounds are 1..=2^31 with a u128 count (AUD-013-API001 still fixed, tested at 2^64). An explicit --path or path compares one key only, also at m/…/2147483647 and m alone. The scope is stated before the work: check.rs:398-414 and the browser's describeAddress both call AddressSearch::describe_within, and the address-search self-check compares the statements. For two missing words the decoy search narrows to first_account(gap), default DECOY_SCAN_GAP = 20. The JS copy in web/client.js:65 is gated by requireSameLimits (client.js:968-980). A cancel is asked before each address (wallet.rs:974), and native workers abort comparisons already under way (search.rs:288-330). The tests a_stopped_search_ends_at_once and a_cancel_ends_the_comparisons_under_way pass (AUD-016-API001 still fixed). The lowest-index match wins deterministically. No network code exists: serve.rs is the loopback fast-mode page server.
entries.limits: Not applicable: providers, proofs, balances, accounting, Platform/Orchard scanning, since MHFE does no public lookups. I did not measure timings of large scan gaps.

entries.method: Read WorkerJob (start timer, loaded flag, deferred terminate of a loading worker, ask/answer, callPage), OperationSlot (requireIdle, after(), hold(), cancel), PackageCheck.require/startup caching, the hidden-wallet handle (pendingOpen/nextRequest/closing), the rekey confirmAgain loop (core-worker.js recoverConfirmed and the Rust RekeyStep machine), and the multi-worker draw (#startDraws). entries.evidence: RekeySession refuses every call out of order (core.rs:1224-1232) and ends on any non-retryable failure; ownerLengths is null unless step==Refused (core.rs:1020-1022); confirmAgain re-judges walletHasPassphrase via Rekey::confirm (rekey.rs:233). Hidden session: BUSY during open, SESSION_CLOSED after end, close() during open terminates, close() while waiting frees in Rust. Browser log: cancel before round 1, in round 2, while a rekey awaits the owner, during an open and between wallets; BUSY; CALLBACK_FAILED for throwing/rejecting callbacks; slot freed after failures, in Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Firefox 157.0, both modes. handshake.out: mismatched ready -> PACKAGE_MISMATCH.

entries.scope: gap:Secret lifecycle in the browser package (WebAssembly, workers and the Emscripten Argon2 heap)
entries.check: CHECK-API-002 (browser half: cancel, close or late completion after a secret was cleared; long-lived session workers)
entries.method: Traced WorkerJob (run/send/stop/#receive/#answer), OperationSlot, openHiddenWallets (waitForPage/sendRequest/answerOpen/closeSession), rekey and check answers (answerConfirmAgain, answerNoLength), and the worker side of hiddenWallets, check and recoverConfirmed. These cases were executed with the real worker and the real page runtime: close while the session waits (A5); the owner answering no and yes (B2); a stop while a session waits followed by a late page answer (H); a trap in a session with the page's WorkerJob (E2).
entries.evidence: A5: close() frees the session. Passwords and passphrase go to 0 in linear memory, the worker's request.mainPassphrase is wiped, and a result is posted. B2: the JS copies are wiped on both answers, and the Rust copies after free(). H: after stop the worker is terminated; the late answer is wiped on the page (WorkerJob.send on an ended job) and never delivered. The page copy of mainPassphrase is detached by the transfer. The Rust and JS copies in the worker are not overwritten but are freed with the worker, as BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:974-976 documents. No path lets a late reply restore a secret or settle a newer request: #receive ignores and terminates an ended job, pendingOpen is cleared before stop, and open() refuses SESSION_CLOSED or BUSY before it encodes anything. AUD-010's client-lifecycle harness already covers the page-side copies.
entries.limits: Single-threaded Node event loop. A close in the middle of an open cannot interleave with the synchronous WebAssembly call here, so that case is covered by code reading. Idle timeouts of sessions are left to the embedding page by design (SECURITY.md).

entries.method: Read every writer to standard output in src/bin/mhfe (println!/print_phrase/print_card/print_result/check result/diceware/test-benchmark JSON). Compared each --stdin help text and the README "For scripts" list (README.md:503-575) line by line with the code paths (encrypt: phrase, password, password again, then container plus optional card line; decrypt: container, [card with --repair], password, [passphrase with --passphrase-used yes and a 24-word reading], then "<words> <verified|unverified> <phrase>" per reading; check: container, [card], password, reference + passphrase, or the passphrase for --words auto, then matches/does not match with exit 0/3; repair: container, card, then the repaired container or nothing; repair-words: container, then the words). Probed output failures: a closed pipe and /dev/full. Reused the baseline parity run.
entries.evidence: Script formats and stdout/stderr separation match the README; prompts are not written in script mode; mhfe self-test writes nothing to stdout. Two defects: F6 (anstream println! ignores BrokenPipe, so a closed pipe gives exit 0 and a "✓"; other write errors panic and abort with exit 134), and F8 (encrypt --help says standard output holds the container alone, but --repair-words adds a second line). baseline-check.log: "The command-line tool and the browser package give the same results."
entries.limits: No monetary, CSV or XLSX export exists, so those parts are not applicable. Full-cost encrypt, decrypt and check outputs (2 GiB Argon2) were not run. The test-vectors JSON writer was only read.

entries.method: probes/gap-module-isolation/scan2.py reads the string and byte-string literals of every known-answer file (test modules excluded) and keeps the vectors among them, by the rule of verify-browser-package.mjs: 8 or more characters with a digit and no space, or 12 or more words. Hex literals are also searched as the bytes self_check::hex() makes of them. The fixture sections are attributed to the parts that read them. Each literal is assigned to its check parts, wallet/known_answers.rs split so that address_search counts on its own, and each build's expected parts come from sets.rs. The scan searches every bound .wasm and glue and records which parts' literals appear outside the build's set. Hits outside the set are judged generic when they are: a production literal, part of a dependency alphabet, consecutive bytes, zeros, a substring of the build's own literals, or a short case name. Self-check labels are counted per build. Control: the full `wasm` build carries every literal any single build carries (0 missing), and all 24 labels. Startup self-test applicability: compared each binding's computed parts with its set, then damaged the BIP32 master-key HMAC key "Bitcoin seed" → "Bitcoin seeE" in copies of the WebAssembly (fingerprint-gap.mjs).
entries.evidence: scan3.out (sha256 b5b7c345…3178). Non-generic literals of parts outside the set: browser-core 0, browser-repair 0 (one hit '0102030405060708' is serde's two-digit table, shown in context), browser-wallet 0. browser-passwords: 48, all from the formats check's fixture sections. The whole tests/fixtures/validation-cases.json (10987 B, sha256 92ced6ea…0fecd) is embedded byte for byte in the passwords build: `fixture in wasm` is True for browser-passwords, browser-core and wasm, and False for repair and wallet. No build carries the label of a part outside its set, and every build carries the labels of its own set. fingerprint-gap.out (sha256 68b07c43…1590): with the damaged key, MhfeRepair's startupCheck still passes (it runs bip39-words and repair-words only), on the single-module build and on the full build alike. Its repairContainer then returns containerFingerprint 04963134 instead of 487a156e. The same damage fails MhfeWallet (bip39-seed, bip32, addresses) and MhfeClient (container-search, bip39-seed, bip32, addresses, rehearsal). These are findings 1 and 2.
entries.limits: The vector rule is a heuristic, as in the package verifier. Text built at run time, or constants stored in another encoding, would escape it. Two-module and three-module combinations were not linked or scanned; their cfg gates are unions (`any(...)`), so they carry the union of their modules' parts. Data only; no disassembly of code paths.

Each run used three worker scripts built from the shipped worker sources: (a) shipped-start: glue + worker-runtime.js + <module>-worker.js + worker-start.js; (b) recipe: the scripts/build-wasm.sh order with every table; (c) own-start: a one-line start for that module only. A stand-in Worker runs the worker script in-process with structuredClone messaging.
entries.evidence: build.out: all four single-module builds and `wasm` linked and bound with no warnings. Bound sizes: browser-core 1190949 B, browser-repair 413638 B, browser-passwords 519386 B, browser-wallet 715473 B, wasm 1329756 B. Raw repair, passwords and wallet .wasm are byte-identical to the skeptic's probes/skeptic-arc-cycle builds, e.g. repair 33792d3f…c42b. Each glue exports only its own module's API plus packageVersion (wordHints too for passwords and wallet). browser-repair exports inspectContainer, repairContainer, repairParameters, repairWords and selfCheckRepair; browser-core exports no repair, password or wallet function. Run results (run-results.json sha256 55f95595…6571): (b) and (c) pass startupCheck for all four modules. (a), the shipped web/worker-start.js, fails for every single module with WORKER_FAILED: ReferenceError: CORE_OPERATIONS is not defined (REPAIR_OPERATIONS is not defined for the core). This is finding 3. The passwords build's embedded fixture is finding 1.
entries.limits: Covers only the isolation aspect of ARC-001. Import cycles and the other seams belong to the architecture reviewer. entries.check: CHECK-ARC-003 (can each self-check and generated table fail; production-path fidelity of tests)
entries.method: Went through every damaged-case and meta-test, one by one, in src/mhfe/known_answers.rs, src/container/known_answers.rs, src/operation/known_answers.rs, src/password/known_answers.rs and src/word_wishes/known_answers.rs, and every test in src/validation_cases.rs. For each one I traced the order of Findings (Findings::each/one stop at the first failure, self_check.rs:324-355) to find which comparison the asserted failure actually comes from. Reproduced the six word-wish known answers independently.
entries.evidence: Nineteen of the twenty meta-tests in scope assert the exact failure string, which pins the comparison that fails. They are: a_wrong_hash_or_digest_fails, a_corrupted_container_or_round_key_fails, a_wrong_password_encoding_or_recovery_fails, the_full_tier_replays_every_vector, a_damaged_fixture_or_a_wrong_expectation_fails_the_formats, the_suite_4_refusals_run_in_the_full_tier, a_wrong_fact_fails (3 cases), a_list_with_a_default_setting_fails (2 cases), corrupted_bytes_or_a_wrong_refusal_fail (3 cases), a_damaged_case_fails, a_case_taken_from_another_draw_fails, a_wrong_bit_oracle_answer_is_refused and a_damaged_reader_fixture_is_refused. The exception is mhfe::known_answers::tests::a_refusal_that_is_accepted_fails (:1141-1155): it asserts only `is_failure()`, and it passes because refusal 1 cannot find zero-24, not for the reason its comment gives (finding 1). My independent oracle (probes/gap-generated-tables/oracle.py, using a BIP39 list whose SHA-256 is 2f5eed53…) reproduced all six word-wish phrases with their draw counts 1, 2, 1, 770, 10 and 192. It confirmed 'primary' = 1365 = 0b10101010101. Two of the phrases also appear in the Deriver's packages/crypto-core/src/bip39-chosen-words.ts:248,256, as the module claims.
entries.limits: I did not edit the repository to run mutated tests (the review was read-only), so finding 1 rests on a traced execution order that any reader can repeat. No meta-test exists for length_rules, entropy_separation, refusals 2 and 3, the word-wish filters, or the count of refused password scalars. Those checks compare exact outputs and would fail on a wrong library result; only the proof that they can fail is missing.

findings.title: Word-hint rows copy the list words that match a typed seed phrase or password into ordinary, unwiped strings.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Reading the residue needs privileged memory access (root or the kernel), a swap device or a hibernation image, with no remote or same-user path, and the project has rated this class Low and non-blocking before (AUD-005-SEC001, AUD-008-SEC002, AUD-014-SEC002, AUD-015-SEC006, AUD-017-SEC001).
findings.affected: Native mhfe command-line binary, interactive input on the private (alternate) screen at a terminal. Files (reviewed tree: HEAD e8dca53 plus its uncommitted changes; SHA-256 given in the evidence): src/bin/mhfe/typed_line.rs:132-150 (LineScreen::hint builds and writes the rows), 161-178 (rows_of), 182-198 (word_rows, lines 190-191), 203-206 (hint_row, line 205); src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:53-57 (paint and its public-text-only contract); src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:65-78 (Content::hints: passwords get EFF hints, seed phrases and chosen words get list hints), 95-113 (read_line builds a LineScreen with hints only when the line is shown), 588-595 (show_hint after every character, removal and Tab); src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:379-387 (a secret is shown, and therefore hinted, while PRIVATE_SCREEN_ACTIVE); src/word_hints.rs:25 (LIST_FROM_LETTERS = 2), 102-115 (Hint for a prefix), 139-144 (starting_with), 158-187 (TypedWord, the library's own wiped copy); SECURITY.md:39-41 and 68-74. typed_line.rs is byte-identical at tag v0.6.0 (same SHA-256), so the released v0.6.0 binary is affected as well; this is not a regression. The measurements cover Linux with glibc 2.43 malloc only; the evidence covers the native command line only.

findings.reproduction: Static: (1) Read src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:588-595 and src/bin/mhfe/typed_line.rs:132-150: after every edit of a shown secret line, LineScreen::hint calls rows_of and writes the returned rows. (2) Read typed_line.rs:182-206: word_rows formats each candidate word with format! into a Vec<String> (line 190), joins them with concat() (line 191), and hint_row returns format!("{INDENT}{}", paint(style, shown)) (line 205). None of these Strings is Zeroizing or reserved at its final size. (3) Read src/word_hints.rs:102-115: from two typed letters on, Hint::Words lists every list word that begins with the typed prefix; when the prefix is unique and shorter than the word, the row is that one word. Dynamic, reviewer probe (scratch, outside the repository): in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/secrets-native/paint-probe run `cargo +1.99.0 build --offline --release --bin hints && ./target/release/hints nohints && ./target/release/hints` under the heavy-job wrapper (flock on heavy.lock plus systemd-run with MemoryMax=3G). The probe mirrors typed_line.rs:183-206 at 80 columns and the word_hints rule, types the public Trezor vector 'legal winner thank year wave sausage worth useful legal winner thank yellow' letter by letter into a Zeroizing 8192-byte buffer, drops every row, and scans its own rw heap and anonymous memory through /proc/self/mem with masked patterns. Compare '0 of 12' (no hints) with '7 of 12' (hints). Dynamic, skeptic probe (independent): in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-hint-rows, which compiles the real src/bin/mhfe/typed_line.rs and cell_widths.rs through #[path] against the real mhfe library (only paint, MUTED, WARNING and LINE_CAPACITY are stubbed, copied verbatim), run `cargo +1.99.0 build --offline --release` under the same wrapper, then `./target/release/skeptic-hint-rows nohints`, `./target/release/skeptic-hint-rows` and `./target/release/skeptic-hint-rows context` to dump the context of each surviving copy.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:39-41: 'Every buffer the program owns that holds a password, phrase, passphrase, entropy, state, Argon2 key or mask is wiped when it is dropped'; the copies that are wiped but not locked are listed at SECURITY.md:68-74, and hint rows are not among them. style.rs:53-54 restricts paint to public text: 'For public text only: the result is an ordinary string, which is not wiped. Secret words are painted by [`boxed_words`]' (boxed_words, style.rs:452-482, builds Zeroizing lines reserved at a fixed capacity). The library itself treats the typed prefix as secret (word_hints.rs:158-160: the last word is kept 'in a buffer that is wiped when dropped: it may be part of a password or a seed phrase'). The project's no-growth rule (src/phrase.rs:95-97) says every growth of an unwiped string 'would leave an unwiped copy of the first words in freed memory'. The workspace rule for Rust programs (AGENTS.md, 'Secrets in memory') requires secret values to live in types that wipe them on drop.
findings.observed: While a seed phrase, chosen word or password is typed on the private screen, every character, removal and Tab redraws the hint (hidden_input.rs:588-595). The rows are built as plain Strings: one per candidate word (typed_line.rs:190), their concatenation (line 191), the painted text returned by paint (style.rs:55-57) and the indented row (line 205). They are freed without being wiped. From two letters on (LIST_FROM_LETTERS = 2) the rows list the BIP39 words (for a phrase) or EFF words (for a password) that begin with the typed prefix, so successive rows follow the order of the typed prefixes; once a prefix is unique, the row built is exactly the secret word (word_hints.rs:111 suppresses the hint only when the typed letters already equal the word). An allocator-hook probe showed that drawing one single-word hint row frees 4 heap blocks that still hold the word at the moment they are freed. In the heap scans, the 12-word public test phrase typed with hints left copies of its words at 7 of 12 positions (per word [4, 5, 0, 0, 2, 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 0, 0] in the reviewer's probe; [4, 5, 0, 0, 2, 0, 1, 4, 4, 5, 0, 0], stable over three runs, in the skeptic's probe of the real code), against 0 of 12 when typed without hints. The surviving copies were multi-candidate rows for 2- and 3-letter prefixes; no exact single-word row survived (0 for all 12 words), because glibc overwrites the first 16 bytes of a small freed chunk with its free-list bookkeeping and those rows are shorter than that.
findings.impact: Fragments derived from a seed phrase typed on the private screen, and by the same code path the EFF words of a typed password, stay in unlocked, unwiped freed heap memory until the allocator reuses those chunks. In the probe, 5 of the 9 distinct words of the test phrase (legal, winner, wave, worth, useful) left a trace and 4 (thank, year, sausage, yellow) left none; 'legal' and 'winner' occur twice, which gives 7 of 12 positions. The traces narrow some words to 3-5 candidates (for example 'used useful useless usual') but do not give them exactly, so the claim that the phrase can be largely reconstructed is not supported by this evidence. Reading the memory needs root or the kernel, a swap device or a hibernation image: the heap is not locked, and the unencrypted-swap warning applies. Another process of the same user cannot read it on Linux (PR_SET_DUMPABLE 0, read back) and no core dump is written (RLIMIT_CORE 0). The password (EFF) path was established statically only; only the BIP39 phrase path was measured. Allocators other than glibc 2.43 (macOS, Windows) were not measured. The defect breaks the paint contract (style.rs:53-54), the wiping promise of SECURITY.md:39-41 and its list at SECURITY.md:68-74, and the project's no-growth rule (phrase.rs:95-97).
findings.recommendedFix: Write hint rows straight to the terminal writer (indent, style, each padded word, reset) without building intermediate Strings, and keep only the row count that hint() needs to move the cursor back (typed_line.rs:145-147). Alternatively, build each row in one Zeroizing buffer reserved at its final size (bounded by the terminal width plus the colour codes), as style::boxed_words does (style.rs:452-482). Apply the same treatment to the EFF password path. Until the fix lands, name hint rows among the wiped-but-unlocked or unwiped copies in SECURITY.md:68-74.
findings.requiredVerification: A regression test that types a public phrase (for example the Trezor vector above) and a synthetic EFF-word password with hints enabled and asserts that no word of either survives in freed memory, for example with a counting or inspecting global allocator in a test binary, as the reviewer's allocator-hook probe does; the test must fail against the current typed_line.rs (4 freed unwiped blocks per single-word row). Re-running both probes must report 'freed-unwiped=0' for a hint row and '0 of 12' with hints. The existing typed_line.rs row tests (around lines 436 and 471) must keep their behaviour, adapted to the new writer if rows_of no longer returns Strings, and scripts/verify-hidden-input.py must still pass for the drawn hints.

findings.title: A zram swap device with a writeback backing device is treated as in-memory, so no swap warning is given.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: It needs an uncommon zram writeback setup by root, an actual writeback while mhfe runs and later access to that disk, the same class and conditions as AUD-020-SEC001, which was rated Low.
findings.affected: Native mhfe command-line binary on Linux only (on macOS and Windows unprotected_swap returns an empty inventory without inspecting swap, protect.rs:828-833). Hosts whose kernel has CONFIG_ZRAM_WRITEBACK and where root has set /sys/block/zramN/backing_dev. Files (reviewed tree: HEAD e8dca53 plus its uncommitted changes): src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:909-914 (encrypted: the zram shortcut at lines 912-914), 825-827 (doc of unprotected_swap: 'An area in memory (zram) is safe'), 862-863 (swap_inventory drops an area that encrypted() accepts), 1003-1014 (test dm_crypt_and_zram_are_protected, zram0 without a backing device only); src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:136-158 (warn_about_swap and swap_warning); SECURITY.md:78-81. The same shortcut is in the released v0.6.0 (protect.rs:900 at that tag).
findings.evidence: Source hashes (SHA-256, reviewed tree): src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs 94c103f1057bd5901564d506a4895c3b767baae35d00b6a5e69d6d4de2794e0f; src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs e7600572c563eb2c7bec2641051b4f47a3306b4bf006d994c5e4ff14a2f5399f; SECURITY.md f01c5bfcf2788f9ca6daf17bbd094e6aade96befa07be5927939c2bf6c99a46b. Code quotes: protect.rs:911-914 `fn encrypted(root: &Path, device: &str, depth: usize) -> bool { if device.starts_with("zram") { return true; }`, followed at line 915 by `let sysfs = root.join("sys/class/block").join(device);`, which is never reached for zram; protect.rs:863 `Some(device) if encrypted(root, &device, 0) => None,`; settings.rs:156-158 `if areas.is_empty() { return None; }`; protect.rs:1004-1013 test `dm_crypt_and_zram_are_protected` with `system.device("zram0", None, &[]);` and `assert_eq!(system.unprotected(), []);`. SECURITY.md:78-81: 'The Argon2 work area, gigabytes in size, cannot be locked, and from its blocks a password guess can be tested cheaply. On Linux the tool therefore warns, before any secret is typed, when a swap area is not encrypted with dm-crypt, directly or under LVM, or when it cannot tell; swap in memory (zram) is safe.' At tag v0.6.0 the same `if device.starts_with("zram")` is at protect.rs:900. Probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/secrets-native/zram/probe.rs (SHA-256 f43999d316de3cfb103ac95fc91c27d9d9c8654ca9779393da3160a3bf7b2e85) printed, and printed again when re-run while writing this record: 'zram0 with backing_dev=/dev/sda5 -> Available([])' and 'sda5 directly -> Available([SwapArea { name: "/dev/sda5", unknown: false }])'. Host kernel configuration: `grep CONFIG_ZRAM_WRITEBACK /boot/config-$(uname -r)` gives 'CONFIG_ZRAM_WRITEBACK=y'; /proc/swaps lists only '/swap.img file'. Live readback (/home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/secrets-native/readback/probe.log, SHA-256 2484550974f985d955c4da153c31624754e96d29d94b2e89ea1bbc4005d99fab): 'swap warning shown: False' for that encrypted host. A grep of docs/audits for zram, backing_dev and writeback finds only mentions of the existing test name in AUD-020, AUD-021 and AUD-022; AUD-020-SEC001 covered an unreadable /proc/swaps, and AUD-020/021 only required the existing zram test to keep its result. No earlier finding covers zram writeback.
findings.reproduction: Static trace: take a Linux host with zram0 as its only swap and /sys/block/zram0/backing_dev naming a plain partition such as /dev/sda5. unprotected_swap() reads /proc/swaps, resolves /dev/zram0 to 'zram0' (device_of_node, protect.rs:879-883) and calls encrypted(root, "zram0", 0), which returns true at protect.rs:912-913 before reading anything under /sys/class/block/zram0; swap_inventory drops the area (line 863) and returns SwapInventory::Available(vec![]); settings::swap_warning returns None for an empty list (settings.rs:156-157), so warn_about_swap prints nothing. Synthetic-sysfs probe (scratch, outside the repository): /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/secrets-native/zram/probe.rs copies protect.rs lines 808-823, 836-883 and 906-934 unchanged (only device_of_file, which partitions do not use, is stubbed). It builds a temporary root with proc/swaps listing '/dev/zram0 partition 1024 0 100', sys/class/block/zram0/backing_dev = '/dev/sda5', sys/class/block/sda5 with an empty slaves directory, and dev/zram0 and dev/sda5; as a control it then lists /dev/sda5 itself as swap. Compile it with rustc (it was built under the heavy-job wrapper, flock on heavy.lock plus systemd-run) and run ./probe. An equivalent FakeSystem test in protect.rs (system.device for zram0 plus a backing_dev file) would show the same.
findings.expected: SECURITY.md:78-81: the Argon2 work area 'cannot be locked', so 'On Linux the tool therefore warns, before any secret is typed, when a swap area is not encrypted with dm-crypt, directly or under LVM, or when it cannot tell'. protect.rs:825 documents unprotected_swap as returning 'The swap areas that are not encrypted by dm-crypt, or whose encryption cannot be told'. The workspace rules for Rust programs (AGENTS.md, 'New Rust programs and ports to Rust') require that 'The program warns when swap is not encrypted' and that 'A protection the system refuses is reported, never assumed'. A zram device is in memory only while it has no backing device: with CONFIG_ZRAM_WRITEBACK, an administrator can set one (`echo /dev/sdX > /sys/block/zram0/backing_dev`) and have idle or incompressible pages written to it (Linux Documentation/admin-guide/blockdev/zram.rst, 'writeback'); those pages are not encrypted unless that device is itself dm-crypt.
findings.observed: encrypted() classifies every device whose name starts with 'zram' as safe without looking at its backing_dev attribute. A zram swap area backed by a plaintext partition is therefore dropped from the inventory and no warning is printed, while the same plaintext partition used directly as swap is reported as unprotected (unknown: false). The only zram test (dm_crypt_and_zram_are_protected) covers zram0 without a backing device, and no test has a zram device with one. SECURITY.md:80-81 states unconditionally that 'swap in memory (zram) is safe'. Not reproduced on a real host with zram writeback: the audit host has no zram (its swap is a swap file, /swap.img, on LVM over LUKS) and is correctly not warned in a live encrypt run.
findings.impact: On a host with zram writeback configured, pages of the Argon2 work area (gigabytes in size, not lockable, and a source from whose blocks a password guess can be tested cheaply, SECURITY.md:78-79) and other heap pages can be written to a plaintext backing device without the warning SECURITY.md promises, so the person is not told to use encrypted swap or a live system. Argon2 blocks are pseudo-random and therefore incompressible, so zram stores them as 'huge' slots, the class that `echo huge > /sys/block/zramN/writeback` sends to the backing device. Prerequisites: root has set a backing device, writeback is triggered (mainline does not trigger it on its own), pages of the work area or heap go out while mhfe runs, and someone later reads that disk. The setup is possible on stock kernels (CONFIG_ZRAM_WRITEBACK=y in the audit host's distribution kernel; systemd's zram-generator has a writeback-device option) but uncommon. Evidence is a static trace plus a synthetic-sysfs probe of the unchanged source; no real writeback was observed.
findings.recommendedFix: In protect.rs, treat a zram device as in memory only when /sys/class/block/zramN/backing_dev is absent or reads 'none'. Otherwise resolve the named backing device through device_of_node and classify it through the same encrypted() path (dm-crypt UUID, slaves), reporting the area as unknown when the backing device cannot be resolved or read, so that swap_warning names it. backing_dev is a world-readable sysfs attribute, so no extra privilege is needed. Update the doc comments at protect.rs:825-826 and 909-910 and the sentence at SECURITY.md:80-81 to say that zram is safe only without a plaintext writeback device.
findings.requiredVerification: New FakeSystem tests in protect.rs: zram without a backing device (no area reported; dm_crypt_and_zram_are_protected keeps its result), zram with backing_dev 'none' (no area), zram with a plaintext backing partition (one SwapArea with unknown: false; this test must fail against the current code), zram with a dm-crypt backing device (no area), and zram whose backing device cannot be resolved (one SwapArea with unknown: true). A settings.rs test that swap_warning returns a warning naming /dev/zram0 for the plaintext case. Re-running the synthetic-sysfs probe against the fixed functions must report /dev/zram0 instead of Available([]). Targeted run: `cargo test` for the protect and settings modules of the mhfe binary.

findings.title: A result that cannot be written to standard output is reported as success on a closed pipe, and on any other write error the command-line tool aborts with a Rust panic
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Only a failing output channel is affected, a full disk still ends with a non-zero exit code, and no secret, integrity or offline boundary is involved.
findings.affected:
Native command-line binary `mhfe` built with the release profile (`panic = "abort"`, Cargo.toml:101), on every platform. The browser package does not write to standard output and is not affected. Reviewed tree: HEAD e8dca53 plus the uncommitted changes recorded in the AUD-023 initial manifest (src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs is among the changed files; its line numbers are those of the reviewed tree).

The result writers all use anstream's `println!` (Cargo.toml:46 pins `anstream = "=1.0.0"`):
- src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:247-253: the container at :250 and the repair card at :252.
- src/bin/mhfe/decrypt.rs:369-380 (`print_result`): the script result at :376.
- src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:327-337 and :354: "matches" / "does not match" at :329, :331, :336 and :354.
- src/bin/mhfe/container_repair.rs:646-678 (`print_card`): script words at :649, card rows at :675.
- src/bin/mhfe/diceware.rs:209-216 (`show`): the new password at :212 and :215.
- src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:457-467 (`print_phrase`): :459, :463 and :466.

Related code:
- src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs:122-126: the existing `From<std::io::Error> for Failure` mapping, which the output path never uses.
- src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:135-160: the panic hook.
- README.md:559-568: the exit-code table.

Commands concerned: encrypt, decrypt, check, repair, repair-words and password.
findings.evidence:
Code:
- anstream 1.0.0, `src/_macros.rs` in the Cargo registry: `println!` is defined at :130. Lines 143-147 read: `match ::std::writeln!(&mut stream, $($arg)*) { Err(e) if e.kind() != ::std::io::ErrorKind::BrokenPipe => { ::std::panic!("failed printing to stdout: {e}"); } Err(_) | Ok(_) => {} }`.
- Cargo.toml:46 is `anstream = "=1.0.0"`. Cargo.toml:101 is `panic = "abort"`.
- The result writers import the macro: encrypt.rs:6, decrypt.rs:3, check.rs:8, container_repair.rs:6, diceware.rs:7 and terminal.rs:13 all have `use anstream::{… println}`.
- startup.rs:139-160 is the only panic hook. It handles a panic only while a startup check is running. Otherwise `let Some(part) = part else { before(info); return; };` hands the panic to the previous (default) hook, and the process aborts.
- exit.rs:122-126 already has `impl From<std::io::Error> for Failure { … Self::internal(format!("Input or output failed: {error}")) }` (exit 1), but no output path uses it.
- `grep -rniE "broken ?pipe|EPIPE|/dev/full|SIGPIPE"` over README.md, docs/ (audits excluded), tests/, scripts/ and src/ finds no handling and no test.

Executed by the verifier with the release binary, built after the newest source change, under `systemd-run MemoryMax=300M` (peak RSS about 7.8 MB; no Argon2 beyond the startup tier):
1. `NO_COLOR=1 mhfe password > /dev/full`: exit 134, "Command terminated by signal 6". Standard error: "thread 'main' (138299) panicked at src/bin/mhfe/diceware.rs:215:9: failed printing to stdout: No space left on device (os error 28)".
2. `printf '<abandon x23 art>\n' | NO_COLOR=1 mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 4 > /dev/full`: exit 134 and "Aborted". Standard error: "thread 'main' (146956) panicked at src/bin/mhfe/container_repair.rs:649:9: failed printing to stdout: No space left on device (os error 28)". The same command to a regular file: exit 0, output "letter wealth borrow cable".
3. pipe_probe.py, with `restore_signals` True and False: `password` exits 0 and prints "✓ 5 words from the EFF list, about 64.6 bits." and "Shown only once and not stored…" to standard error; `repair-words --stdin --count 4` exits 0.

The reviewer's probe cli-ux/broken_pipe.py gave the same exit-0 results.

Retained local outputs: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-broken-pipe/ (pw_full.err, rw_full.err, rw_ok.out, pipe_probe.py).

Not run: full-cost `encrypt --stdin > /dev/full`, which is not allowed under the audit rules.

No earlier mhfe audit (AUD-001 to AUD-022) reports this.
findings.reproduction:
Use public data only. These are cheap commands: no Argon2 runs beyond the startup tier. Run them under a memory cap, for example `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=300M -p MemorySwapMax=0 ...`.
1. Build the release binary with `cargo build --release --locked`.
2. Full device: `NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe password > /dev/full; echo $?` prints 134.
3. Full device with a container on standard input: `printf '%s\n' "$(printf 'abandon %.0s' $(seq 23))art" | NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 4 > /dev/full; echo $?` prints 134. The input is the public BIP39 phrase of 23 times "abandon" then "art". The same command with output to a regular file exits 0 and writes one line.
4. Closed pipe: run `python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/cli-ux/broken_pipe.py`, or `probes/skeptic-broken-pipe/pipe_probe.py`, which also runs each case with `restore_signals` True and False. Each script creates a pipe, closes its read end, then starts `mhfe password` and `mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 4` with standard output on the write end. Both commands exit 0.
5. Not run, because full-cost Argon2 at 2 GiB is not allowed by the audit rules: `mhfe encrypt --stdin > /dev/full`. It reaches the same `println!` at encrypt.rs:250 on the same code path.
findings.expected:
The tool should report a failed write of a result as a documented error:
- The workspace AGENTS.md (Terminal output) requires every error to be one red "✗ Error:" line.
- README.md:559-568 documents exit codes 0-4 and 130 only.
- src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs:122-126 already maps every other I/O error to "✗ Error: Input or output failed: …" with exit 1 (INTERNAL_ERROR).

Some results exist only once: a new container, a recovered phrase, a password "Shown only once and not stored". When such a result reaches no reader, the command should not end with exit 0.
findings.observed:
Full device (ENOSPC): the process prints a raw Rust panic to standard error, aborts with SIGABRT and exits with code 134.
- `password` prints "thread 'main' (138299) panicked at src/bin/mhfe/diceware.rs:215:9: failed printing to stdout: No space left on device (os error 28)".
- `repair-words` prints "thread 'main' (146956) panicked at src/bin/mhfe/container_repair.rs:649:9: failed printing to stdout: No space left on device (os error 28)", then "Aborted".

Closed pipe (EPIPE): the write error is swallowed and the command exits 0.
- `password` still prints "✓ 5 words from the EFF list, about 64.6 bits." and "Shown only once and not stored…" on standard error.
- `repair-words --stdin --count 4` exits 0 with no message.
findings.impact:
On a full disk, `mhfe encrypt --stdin > container.txt` ends with the undocumented code 134 and a Rust panic text. It should end with "✗ Error: Input or output failed: …" and exit 1.

When the consumer of a pipeline exits early, mhfe exits 0 although the container, the recovered phrase or the new password reached nobody. `set -o pipefail` cannot detect this, because mhfe itself reports success. The "✓" that `password` prints is its strength line, not a delivery confirmation; the misleading success is the exit code.

Limits of the evidence:
- Only a failing output channel is affected, and a full disk still gives a non-zero code.
- No secret leaks: core dumps are disabled, so the abort writes nothing.
- The abort cannot leave the terminal on the private (alternate) screen. A private screen or step flow needs standard output to be a terminal (terminal.rs:607-632), and a terminal does not return ENOSPC.
- The closed-pipe half is the weaker part of the finding. Exit 0 on EPIPE is anstream's documented behaviour and is common among Rust command-line tools, for example ripgrep.
findings.recommendedFix:
Write every result through one function in the command-line front end that returns `io::Result`: `writeln!` to a locked standard output, for example `anstream::stdout().lock()` so that colour adaptation is kept, then `flush`.

Map every error, BrokenPipe included, to `Failure::from(io::Error)`, which gives exit 1 and "✗ Error: Input or output failed: …".

Replace the `anstream::println!` calls listed above with that function, so that no output path can panic. If a different exit code is chosen for an undelivered result, document it in README.md's exit-code table.

findings.evidence:
This record merges two reports of the same defect: the core-crypto reviewer and the specification-parity reviewer.

Severity: the core-crypto reviewer rated it medium and the parity reviewer low. Two of three verifiers rated it low: a bounded label and conformance defect, with mitigated interactive paths and a safe failure direction, and with precedents AUD-019-DOC001 and mhfe_spec AUD-006-FUN004, both low. One verifier kept medium, as an API-contract defect in supported behaviour. All three agreed it is real, reproduced and not release blocking.

Specification text:

findings.reproduction:
1. Browser, executed in the AUD-023 baseline (`node scripts/verify-browsers.mjs`; Chromium 156.0.8078.4 and Firefox 157.0, standard and fast mode). `made.checked` is the suite 3 container of CHECKED_PHRASE ("abandon" x21 "above proof fatigue", verify-browsers.mjs:67), made at :905-910 with the correct PASSWORD.
