- Release run 38057244146: Firefox standard 325 s and fast 332 s; browser step about 17 minutes.
- Run 38161783972: Firefox 209 s and 166 s.
- The failing step took about 18.5 minutes.

Local probe (probe.log), under the heavy lock with MemoryMax=3G and taskset -c 0-3, on the COOP/COEP-served reduced-cost page built by the baseline:
- Run 1: finished after 110.7 s, 52 reports.
- Run 2: finished after 262.3 s, 120 reports; the drawings took about 129 s and 112 s.
- Run 3: finished after 58.9 s, 4 reports.
- 0 failures, about 950 draws/s.

The local baseline (docs/audits/AUD-023-evidence/baseline-browsers.command.json) has exit code 0 for all four pages on 16 CPUs. No AUD-001 to AUD-022 finding covers PAGE_TIMEOUT or browser-page timeouts.
findings.reproduction:
1. Read-only: `gh api repos/hobby-eng/mhfe/actions/jobs/115528543243/logs` and search for 'mode:' and 'TimeoutError'.
2. Compare the page durations of the earlier runs' logs (jobs 114223463000, 114228126731 and 114536111425).
3. Locally, under the heavy-job lock and memory cap, run the skeptic's /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-ci-firefox/firefox-fast-probe.mjs. It runs the reduced-cost page in Firefox fast mode with hardwareConcurrency 4 on 4 CPUs (`taskset -c 0-3`) and records the time of each drawing.
findings.expected: A mandatory CI check should give the same result for unchanged code, size its time budget for the runner it uses, and on failure leave enough evidence to tell a product hang from a slow run (CHECK-BLD-005: "failure artifact retention"). The comment at verify-browsers.mjs:57-62 claims that ten minutes are exceeded by two drawings "about once in 500,000 pages ... so a page that times out has stopped, not drawn long".
findings.observed:
In CI run 38464712912, job check (115528543243), step "Check the browser package in Chromium and Firefox", the Chromium standard (20:52:41Z), Chromium fast (20:53:31Z) and Firefox standard (20:57:38Z) pages printed only ok lines (0 FAIL lines). The Firefox fast page then failed at 21:07:39Z with "page.waitForFunction: Timeout 600000ms exceeded. at checkPage (scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:4505:27) ... log: [], name: 'TimeoutError'", and the step ended with exit code 1.

What the timeout leaves behind: the exception leaves checkPage through finally blocks only. Nothing reports the page's partial results, its console messages or the check that was running, and no trace or screenshot is uploaded.

Why the budget is likely too small:
- The comment sizes the budget for eight workers at half a minute per drawing. On CI, hardwareConcurrency is 4 ("drawn on the default 4 workers"), and the second drawing uses 3.
- The step's 20-minute timeout is less than four pages of 600 s, so the last page (Firefox fast) gets less than its full budget.
findings.impact:
The failure is either an intermittent hang of fast mode in Firefox (a product defect) or a CI-only stall or slow run. The retained log cannot tell which, and the next occurrence will again leave nothing to decide it.

The skeptic's data point to a timeout budget that is too small for 4-worker runners, not to a hang:
- Pages took up to 511 s in passing runs.
- The local probe finished 3 of 3 runs.
- At the measured rates, one page has an estimated 0.5-5% chance of passing 600 s, depending on CI's slowdown, not the 1 in 500,000 the comment claims.

No product hang is shown. The release workflow inherits the failure and can fail at random until the budget is fixed.
findings.recommendedFix:
1. Give each drawing its own timeout, sized from the actual worker count, or keep the test's duration from depending on unbounded random drawings. Correct the comment's eight-worker assumption.
2. On a timeout, print the page's last progress, its partial results, its console messages (register page.on("console")) and the check that was running.
3. Upload a short-retention trace or console artifact on failure.
4. Make the step timeout cover all four pages.
5. Run the Firefox fast page repeatedly, locally and on CI, to establish whether the product can hang.
findings.requiredVerification:
1. A forced short timeout in a test mode shows the running check, the partial results and the console output in the log and in the uploaded artifact.
2. Repeated Firefox fast-mode runs with 4 workers on 4 CPUs (for example 20 local runs, CPU-limited) all finish within the new per-drawing budgets.
3. The browser step passes on the next CI run without a rerun.

findings.title: Pull requests from branches of the repository, including Dependabot's, run CI and the RustSec audit twice for the same commit, once for the push and once for the pull request
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Runner time and workspace policy only: it does not change any check's result or any artifact.
findings.affected: .github/workflows/ci.yml:5-7 (`push: branches: ["**"]` and `pull_request`), :15-17 (`group: ci-${{ github.ref }}`, `cancel-in-progress: true`), :85 (the windows-2025 and macos-15 matrix). .github/workflows/audit.yml:5-15 (push on all branches and pull_request, same path filters), :20-22 (`group: rustsec-${{ github.ref }}`). .github/dependabot.yml:1-15 (weekly cargo and github-actions updates). Affects every pull request opened from a branch of the repository itself, in practice Dependabot's.
findings.evidence:
- Files read: ci.yml:5-7, :15-17 and :84-86; audit.yml:5-15 and :20-22; dependabot.yml:3-15.
- Run pairs from `gh run list` as listed under observed behaviour. `gh run view 37456206908` (pull_request) and `gh run view 37456201490` (push) each ran check, canonical-build, portable (macos-15) and portable (windows-2025) to success.
- `gh repo view hobby-eng/mhfe --json visibility` gives {"isPrivate":false,"visibility":"PUBLIC"}.
- `gh pr list --state all` gives PRs 1-12, all by app/dependabot, the latest on 2026-10-06.
- Commit 717265c ("CI: superseded runs cancel themselves; a release tag starts no duplicates") added the concurrency groups and dealt with tag pushes and force pushes, but left the push plus pull_request pair alone.
- release.yml and vectors.yml do not affect CI or audit triggers.
- No AUD-001 to AUD-022 report records this.
findings.reproduction: Read-only: `gh run list --repo hobby-eng/mhfe --limit 100 --json workflowName,event,headBranch,headSha,databaseId,conclusion`, grouped by (workflowName, headSha). Each Dependabot head SHA appears once with event push and once with event pull_request, for both CI and RustSec audit. `gh run view <id>` on both CI runs of one SHA shows that each ran every job.
findings.expected: The workspace AGENTS.md (Commits section) says: "GitHub Actions runs are not free. When a push makes a run pointless (a force-push, a moved tag, a newer commit on the same branch, a second run of the same commit for the same purpose), cancel that run at once ... Workflows cancel superseded runs themselves with a concurrency group and cancel-in-progress: true". A commit pushed to a branch and opened as a pull request should be checked once per workflow.
findings.observed:
The concurrency group `ci-${{ github.ref }}` resolves to refs/heads/<branch> for the push run and to refs/pull/<n>/merge for the pull-request run. The two never share a group, so neither cancels the other; audit.yml has the same shape. Run history for 2026-10-06T11:24Z:
- eb1e8bad (dependabot/cargo/cc-1.6.0): CI push 37456201490 and pull_request 37456206908, both success; RustSec push 37456201538 and pull_request 37456206847.
- 4bea94a8 (bitcoin_hashes-1.2.0): CI push 37456194539 and pull_request 37456201745, both failure; RustSec 37456194624 and 37456201524.
- ff2c4692 (libc-0.2.190): CI push 37456184488 and pull_request 37456189655, both failure; RustSec 37456184434 and 37456189719.
None was cancelled. For eb1e8bad, both CI runs ran check, canonical-build, portable (windows-2025) and portable (macos-15) in full. For example, macos-15 ran 11:25:56 to 11:27:03 in one run and 11:24:45 to 11:26:18 in the other.
findings.impact:
Every same-repository pull request doubles the runner time of CI, including its macOS and Windows jobs, and of the RustSec audit. It also takes concurrent-job slots (the macOS limit is small), lengthens queues and duplicates entries in the run history. It breaks the owner's written rule, which names a second run of the same commit for the same purpose as a pointless run.

Correction to the reviewer's wording: `gh repo view` reports the repository as PUBLIC, and standard GitHub-hosted runners cost nothing on public repositories, so "doubles the paid minutes" overstates the cost.

Frequency is limited: 12 Dependabot pull requests in all, the latest on 2026-10-06, and the owner pushes to main directly. Strictly, the pull-request run checks the merge ref, not the head commit; for a fresh Dependabot pull request the trees are identical and both runs report the same headSha.
findings.recommendedFix:
In both ci.yml and audit.yml, do one of the following:
- Run push only for main, since pull requests cover branches.
- Skip push runs for branches that open pull requests, for example `branches-ignore: ["dependabot/**"]` on push.
- Key the concurrency group on the head commit (the pull request's head SHA or github.sha), so that the second run cancels the first.
Keep the weekly schedule and workflow_dispatch of audit.yml, and keep release.yml's call of ci.yml working.
findings.requiredVerification:
- A static review and a workflow lint of the changed triggers.
- On the next Dependabot pull request, `gh run list --json workflowName,event,headSha` shows exactly one CI run and one RustSec audit run per head SHA.
- A push to main still starts both workflows.
- No extra runs are dispatched only to test the change.

findings.title: The release job whose archives are attested runs a cargo-audit binary built from unlocked dependencies (restored from the default-branch cache, or installed unlocked on a cache miss) on the same runner before the canonical build
findings.releaseBlockingReason: No compromise is demonstrated. docs/RELEASING.md:20-23 has the maintainer compare the four canonical archives with independent local Docker outputs before signing, while the draft stays private, so this is a hardening gap.
findings.affected: .github/workflows/release.yml:19-53 (job canonical: the RustSec step at :39-42 runs before scripts/build-reproducible.sh at :45-48, and the archives are uploaded at :49-53). :120-132 (publish: a transfer check against canonical.sha256, written on the same runner after the build, then actions/attest over release/*). actions-rust-lang/audit@72c09e02f132669d52284a3323acdb503cfc1a24 (v1.2.7), action.yml lines 41-53. .github/workflows/audit.yml:4-17 and :35 (branch pushes and the weekly cron keep the default-branch cargo-audit cache alive). Artifacts: the four canonical archives of every tag release (linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, windows-x86_64, browser) and their build-provenance attestations. The macOS archives are built in other jobs.
findings.evidence:
- release.yml:39-42: `uses: actions-rust-lang/audit@72c09e02f132669d52284a3323acdb503cfc1a24 # v1.2.7` inside job canonical.
- release.yml:45-48: `scripts/build-reproducible.sh canonical-output` and `cp canonical-output/release/SHA256SUMS canonical-output/release/canonical.sha256`.
- release.yml:129-132: `uses: actions/attest@... with: subject-path: "release/*"`.
- action.yml at the pinned SHA: line 41 `uses: actions/cache@9255dc7a...`, line 48 `key: cargo-audit-v0.22.0`, line 51 `if: steps.cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'`, line 53 `run: cargo +stable install cargo-audit --vers 0.22.0 --no-default-features`.
- `cargo help install`: "By default, the Cargo.lock file that is included with the package will be ignored. This means that Cargo will recompute which versions of dependencies to use, possibly using newer versions".
- AUD-019 evidence, remote-release-canonical.log: line 230 "Cache hit for: cargo-audit-v0.22.0", line 234 "Cache restored successfully", line 238 "Install cargo-audit ... outcome=skipped".
- audit.yml:4-17: branch pushes and cron "17 4 * * 1"; :35 uses the same action.
- For comparison, the project's own pinning: packaging/Dockerfile.reproducible:14 and :20 (digest-pinned bases), :63 (sha256 --check of rustup-init) and :69 (`--locked`); ci.yml:61 (`--locked`).
- AUD-002 noted only that the audit action is pinned by SHA, and AUD-019 noted cargo-audit 0.22.0 and denyWarnings=false. Neither raised the unlocked build or the shared job.
- Noted separately by the skeptic, not part of this finding: release.yml:74 runs `brew install gnu-tar` unpinned in the macOS jobs that pack and later attest the macOS archives, which the local Docker comparison does not cover.
findings.reproduction:
1. Read release.yml:39-48.
2. Read-only: `gh api 'repos/actions-rust-lang/audit/contents/action.yml?ref=72c09e02f132669d52284a3323acdb503cfc1a24' --jq .content | base64 -d`, lines 41-54.
3. `cargo help install`, for its statement on the package's Cargo.lock.
4. In AUD-019's retained local evidence, docs/audits/AUD-019-evidence/remote-release-canonical.log lines 230-238 (the v0.6.0 tag run).
findings.observed:
The pinned action's action.yml restores `~/.cargo/bin/cargo-audit*` through actions/cache (line 41) under the key cargo-audit-v0.22.0 (line 48). On a cache miss (line 51) it runs `cargo +stable install cargo-audit --vers 0.22.0 --no-default-features` (line 53): no --locked, and a floating stable toolchain. Per `cargo help install`, the package's Cargo.lock is then ignored and newer dependency versions may be used, and the dependencies' build scripts run on the runner during the install.

In the v0.6.0 tag run the job did not install anything: it restored a cached binary, which had been built from unlocked dependencies in an earlier run on main. A tag run can restore a cache from the default branch, and audit.yml keeps that cache alive with the same action. So the reviewer's title ("first installs") overstates a cache hit; the risk is the same kind, at a different time.

Code running in that step can rewrite scripts/build-reproducible.sh or the sources before the build. The SOURCE_STATE marker (build-reproducible.sh:32-36) is no defence, because the same code can rewrite the script that sets it. Publish's check at :120-127 proves only that the bytes did not change between jobs.
findings.impact:
A malicious or broken crate published within cargo-audit's dependency ranges when the cache is filled (or during a tag run with a cache miss) could alter the checkout or the Docker build before the canonical archives are built, and the GitHub attestation would then vouch for the altered bytes.

Mitigations:
- docs/RELEASING.md:20-23 has the maintainer verify "the four canonical archives against the independent local Docker outputs before signing", and the draft stays private until then, so altered canonical bytes would be caught before publication.
- The macOS archives are not built in this job.

No compromise is demonstrated, and exploitation needs a compromised crate in range at the right moment.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the RustSec step out of the canonical job, into a job of its own that publish also needs, or call audit.yml through workflow_call. The canonical job then runs only the checkout, the pinned toolchain, the tag checks and the pinned Docker recipe. If cargo-audit is installed in that separate job, install it with --locked and a pinned toolchain.
findings.requiredVerification:
- A static review of release.yml shows that the canonical job has no step besides checkout, toolchain, tag and notes checks, the Docker build and the upload.
- The RustSec job is in publish's `needs`, so a RustSec failure still stops the draft.
- A workflow lint passes.
- On the next tag run, the canonical job's log shows no cargo-audit cache restore or install.

findings.title: The two no-network gates of the browser package keep separate pattern lists that already differ, and both miss other ways a script can load code or reach the network
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Gate completeness only: the shipped dist scripts contain none of the missing patterns, and the browser suite runs the package under connect-src 'none' and fails on any request that leaves the page.
findings.affected: scripts/remove-network-code.mjs:29-36 (NETWORK_CODE: fetch(, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, EventSource and sendBeacon). It runs only on the wasm-bindgen glue (scripts/build-wasm.sh:74) and on the Argon2 builds argon2-mt.js and argon2-st.js (scripts/build-argon2-wasm.sh:80). scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs:2720-2741 is the only static gate over every packaged script: runtime/runtime.js, runtime/worker.js, core/client.js, core/argon2-mt.js, core/argon2-st.js, wallet/wallet.js, repair/repair.js and passwords/passwords.js. Its list at :2733-2738 lacks sendBeacon. Build: the browser package (dist/).
findings.evidence:
- scripts/remove-network-code.mjs:29-36: `/** Code that could reach the network. None of it may remain. */ const NETWORK_CODE = [ /\bfetch\s*\(/u, /\bXMLHttpRequest\b/u, /\bWebSocket\b/u, /\bEventSource\b/u, /\bsendBeacon\b/u, ];`.
- scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs:2733-2738: `for (const pattern of [ /\bfetch\s*\(/u, /\bXMLHttpRequest\b/u, /\bWebSocket\b/u, /\bEventSource\b/u, ]) {`.

Probe output (rerun while writing this record):
- "navigator.sendBeacon(...)": build REFUSED, package passes.
- "importScripts(...)", "await import(...)", "new WebTransport(...)", "new RTCPeerConnection()" and "(new Image).src=...": build passes, package passes.
- "fetch(...)": build REFUSED, package REFUSED.

Current dist: `grep -cE 'importScripts\s*\(|\bimport\s*\(|WebTransport|RTCPeerConnection|sendBeacon|\.src\s*='` gives 0 for each of the eight scripts.

Callers of remove-network-code.mjs: only scripts/build-wasm.sh:74 and scripts/build-argon2-wasm.sh:80.

Prior audits: AUD-002 and AUD-005 grepped for importScripts by hand. AUD-010's harness docs/audits/AUD-010-harnesses/secrets-security/network-scan.mjs:4-5 describes its own scan as "wider than the build's own list in scripts/remove-network-code.mjs", but it is an audit harness, not a build gate, and no earlier finding raised the gap.

The skeptic noted that CHECK-SEC-003 (network egress) would also fit this finding.
findings.reproduction: Run the skeptic's probe: `node /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-network-gate/probe.mjs`. It reads both regex lists out of the two source files and tests these samples against each list: `navigator.sendBeacon("https://example.invalid", d)`, `importScripts("https://example.invalid/x.js")`, `await import("https://example.invalid/m.js")`, `new WebTransport("https://example.invalid")`, `new RTCPeerConnection()`, `(new Image).src="https://example.invalid/p.gif"`, and the control `fetch("https://example.invalid")`. Then grep the current dist scripts for the missing patterns.
findings.expected:
- The gate's own comment (verify-browser-package.mjs:2720-2721): "No script of the package contains code that could reach the network, not even code that never runs".
- SECURITY.md:238: "The package fetches nothing and needs no `connect-src`".
- docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:47: "Nothing is fetched at run time".
- Workspace AGENTS.md rule 6: every list has exactly one source, and a deliberate copy says so in a comment next to it, with the reason, while a test keeps both copies in step.
findings.observed:
The two lists differ: sendBeacon is only in the build list. No comment names the second list as a copy; the comment at :2720-2721 names scripts/remove-network-code.mjs only as the script that removes the loaders. No test keeps the lists in step.

Probe results:
- sendBeacon: refused by the build list, passes the package list.
- importScripts, dynamic import(, WebTransport, RTCPeerConnection and an Image src assignment: pass both lists.
- fetch( (control): refused by both.

The current dist scripts contain none of the missing patterns (count 0 in all eight).
findings.impact:
The static gates would not notice a future sendBeacon in runtime.js, client.js or a module class, or an importScripts, dynamic import(, WebTransport, RTCPeerConnection or image src in any packaged script.

The browser suite still catches network code that actually runs during the tests: verify-browsers.mjs:4434 sets `connect-src 'none'`, and checkPage fails on "a request left the page" (:4498-4523). A host's Content-Security-Policy remains the runtime barrier. Only code that never runs, or that the tests do not exercise, would slip through, which is exactly what the gate's comment promises to exclude.

No network code is present today. CHECK-SEC-003 itself warns that a pattern tripwire is no proof against arbitrary code.
findings.recommendedFix:
1. Keep one exported list, for example scripts/network-code.mjs, and import it in both remove-network-code.mjs and verify-browser-package.mjs.
2. Add to it at least importScripts(, dynamic import(, WebTransport and RTCPeerConnection, and consider assignments of a src to images or scripts and workers with non-blob URLs.
3. Give the gate a self-test with one sample per pattern that must be refused and a clean sample that must pass.
findings.requiredVerification:
- The new self-test fails if any sample is not refused.
- The repository's copy gate (scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs), or a test, shows that only one pattern list exists.
- `node scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs` still passes on the current dist.
- A scratch copy of a dist script with an added `importScripts("x")` is refused by the package gate.

findings.expected:
- Workspace AGENTS.md ("Self-tests and tests come with every coin and feature"): each check is built only with its feature, and "Extend the composition gates and the artifact checks accordingly".
- src/self_check/sets.rs:2-3: "a browser module's WebAssembly carries the checks and vectors of its own parts and no others".

- FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md CHECK-BLD-002: "Compiler success is insufficient for dynamic installer/function requirements and template pruning", and it asks for runtime sampling of independent modules.

findings.observed:
The only single-module gate is a type check: check.sh:38-42 runs `cargo clippy --locked --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-default-features --features "$module" -- -D warnings` under the comment "Each browser module builds alone, so that another program can take one part without the rest". Clippy neither generates code nor links.

No repository script or workflow builds, binds, scans or runs a single-module WebAssembly:
- The package checks look only at the full package's scripts.
- The Rust test compares id lists in a build where every set is compiled.

As a result, the passwords-only WebAssembly carries the core's formats vectors (AUD-023-BLD009) and no gate reports it. MhfeRepair's startup set misses the fingerprint parts (AUD-023-BLD010), which no single-module run would accept silently once a damaged-copy check exists.
findings.impact: The owner's isolation rules are enforced only at compile time. Those rules are that a module without a feature carries none of its checks or vectors, and that another program can take one part alone. A regression in what a single-module WebAssembly carries, or in whether it starts, would ship unnoticed to programs that build one module. AUD-023-BLD009 escaped for this reason. The shipped all-module package is covered by the existing checks.
findings.recommendedFix:
Add a step to check.sh. It costs about 6 s per module after the first build.
1. Link and bind each module alone.
2. Scan each for the vector literals of the parts outside its set, by generalising rustStrings and vectorTexts of verify-browser-package.mjs to a per-part attribution like the probe's scan2.py.
3. Run each module's startup self-check, and one damaged-copy refusal, through its class in Node, as Part 2 of verify-browser-package.mjs does for the full build.
findings.requiredVerification:
- The new step fails on the current tree because of AUD-023-BLD009, which shows that it can fail, and passes once that is fixed.
- A deliberately added foreign vector in one module makes it fail.
- Each single-module startup check passes, and a damaged copy is refused.
- CI runs the step through check.sh, within the fast-check budget.

findings.title: The browser client's early refusals of the PIM, memory level, word count and repair-word count use their own lower-case messages with API identifiers, differ from the library's sentences for the same codes, and call a rekey's newPim "pim".
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Only the shown text is affected; the error codes and the refusals themselves are correct.
findings.affected:
Browser package (web/), in every browser, for any page that shows MhfeError.message; working tree on e8dca53.
- web/client.js:1003-1005 requireSettings() passes the API names "pim" and "memoryLevel"; :1018-1022 requireSetting() builds the message; :1025-1032 requireWordCount(); :1034-1041 requireRepairWordCount().
- web/client.js:610 rekey() calls requireSettings(newPim, newMemoryLevel); :827 #begin() calls requireSettings(pim, memoryLevel) for the old settings.

- Tests comparing only the code: verify-browser-package.mjs:3359 `{ code: "INVALID_REPAIR_WORDS" }`, :3369 `{ code: "INVALID_PIM" }`, :3784 `{ code: "INVALID_PIM" }`; verify-browsers.mjs:1025-1031 expectRejection with codes only. verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs compares the CLI with direct WebAssembly calls, which the production client's early path never reaches for these codes.
Probe output (reviewer, early-refusals.out):
"encrypt pim 1024: MhfeError INVALID_PIM :: pim must be a whole number from 0 to 1023."
"encrypt memoryLevel 22: MhfeError INVALID_MEMORY_LEVEL :: memoryLevel must be a whole number from 0 to 21."
"decrypt words 13: MhfeError INVALID_WORD_COUNT :: words must be 0 (detect) or 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24."
"encrypt repairWordCount 3: MhfeError INVALID_REPAIR_WORDS :: repairWordCount must be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8."
"rekey newPim 5000: MhfeError INVALID_PIM :: pim must be a whole number from 0 to 1023."
Verifier probe (skeptic-early-refusals/probe.out) adds: "rekey pim 5000 (old): MhfeError INVALID_PIM :: pim must be a whole number from 0 to 1023."

Prior audits: no AUD-001 to AUD-022 finding covers this mismatch. AUD-015-ARC001 (word-count lists typed by hand in client.js) is a different defect in the same functions and is fixed (countsText(WORD_COUNTS)); AUD-015-UI005 is the precedent for rating a cosmetic message defect low.
findings.reproduction:
1. Run `node /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/browser-wasm/early-refusals.mjs` (local evidence, not committed). It loads web/client.js and web/runtime.js from the working tree with a stub WebAssembly and synthetic values, and calls encrypt({ pim: 1024 }), encrypt({ memoryLevel: 22 }), decrypt({ words: 13 }), encrypt({ repairWordCount: 3 }) and rekey({ newPim: 5000 }). The verifier's independent probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-early-refusals/probe.mjs adds rekey({ pim: 5000 }) for the old PIM.
2. Read the code and the message of each MhfeError.
3. Compare with the command-line tool: `NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe decrypt --stdin --pim 1024 < /dev/null`.
findings.expected: web/runtime.d.ts:156 says "`message` is an English sentence that a page can show as it is"; docs/API.md:949-950 and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:496-498 say the same of every MhfeError, and web/runtime.js:583-586 adds that a shown message starts with a capital letter, as the command-line tool's messages do. The package's own rule at scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs:1729-1730 says the classes give these early refusals of the library "with the library's code and in its words, as the command-line tool does". The workspace DRY rule (AGENTS.md, principle 6) requires the same message to be built in one place. The four refusals should therefore carry the library's sentence for their code (src/error.rs:184-188, 250-252, 265-276), with the refused value, and a rekey should say whether the new or the old setting was refused.
findings.observed:
The client refuses all four early, before any WebAssembly call, with its own text:
- encrypt pim 1024: INVALID_PIM "pim must be a whole number from 0 to 1023."
- encrypt memoryLevel 22: INVALID_MEMORY_LEVEL "memoryLevel must be a whole number from 0 to 21."
- decrypt words 13: INVALID_WORD_COUNT "words must be 0 (detect) or 12, 15, 18, 21 or 24."
- encrypt repairWordCount 3: INVALID_REPAIR_WORDS "repairWordCount must be 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8."
- rekey newPim 5000 and rekey pim 5000 (old): both INVALID_PIM "pim must be a whole number from 0 to 1023.", the same text, naming neither the side nor the value.
The library words the same codes differently: "the PIM must be a whole number from 0 to 1023, not {pim}", "the memory level must be a whole number from 0 to 21, not {level}", "the original seed phrase must have {counts} words, not {words}". The command-line tool prints "✗ Error: The PIM must be a whole number from 0 to 1023, not 1024" and exits 2. The WebAssembly path would give the library's sentence ("CODE: message" from src/wasm_api/mod.rs:89-91, capitalised by sentence() at web/runtime.js:587-589), so one code yields two texts in the browser package depending on where it is refused; the production client always refuses these four early, so a page only ever sees the API-style fragment. LIBRARY_MESSAGES (verify-browser-package.mjs:1731-1744) keeps four other early refusals word for word with the library (MEMORY_LEVEL_NOT_SUPPORTED_HERE, WALLET_CHECK_NEEDS_PASSPHRASE, PASSPHRASES_DIFFER, NO_BUILT_IN_CHECK_AT_24) but not these four, and the tests that reach them compare only the code.
findings.impact: A page that shows the message as documented displays a lower-case fragment with a camelCase API identifier and without the refused value, different from the command-line tool's sentence for the same refusal. For a rekey the user cannot tell from the text whether the new PIM or memory level, or the old one, was refused. Presentation only: the codes are correct, the refusal happens before any secret reaches a worker, and nothing is computed or disclosed. Limit of the evidence: the command-line side of the old/new PIM wording of rekey was not run (rekey has no --stdin script mode); the browser side was reproduced.

findings.title: mhfe rekey refuses an invalid --new-pim or --new-mem, or a new level this computer cannot hold, only after the old container's full recovery, and a --confirm way the length does not allow only after the old password and the old level's memory reservation.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The refusals come in the wrong order and work is wasted, but the result is never wrong and nothing is disclosed.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool, `mhfe rekey`, all platforms (reproduced on Linux with target/release/mhfe built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC, newer than rekey.rs and settings.rs); working tree on e8dca53.
- src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:46-51 (new_pim and new_memory_level, no range parser), :171-180 (confirmation match; `(Some(kind), _) => kind` at :177), :191 (settings::reserve_memory(old_work)), :195-212 (recover_state), :215-254 (confirmation loop), :279 (owner_confirms with --confirm show), :301-313 (passphrase prompt for the rehearsal fingerprint), :315-319 (new settings and settings::choose).
- src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:108-134 (choose; range check through work_factor() at :123, check_resources at :132).
- src/rehearsal.rs:503-504 (the --confirm refusal inside recover_for_rekey).
- README.md:477-478 and the --confirm help at rekey.rs:102-104.
findings.evidence:
Code (working tree; rekey.rs last changed 2026-10-10):
- rekey.rs:45-51: `/// PIM of the new container, 0 to 1023 (default 0)` `new_pim: Option<u32>` and `new_memory_level: Option<u32>`, with no range value_parser. A grep of src/ for new_pim and new_memory_level finds them used only at rekey.rs:316-317.
- rekey.rs:315-319: `let new_settings = Settings { pim: options.new_pim, memory_level: options.new_memory_level }; let new_work = settings::choose(new_settings, &mut input, Operation::RekeyNew)?;`
- settings.rs:123 `let defaults = settings.work_factor()?;` and :132 `check_resources(work)?;` (check_resources calls check_can_run, settings.rs:446-448).
- Order in rekey::run: old settings :146, container :153-157, --words :159, old password :161-164, confirmation match :171-180, passphrase question :185-188, reserve_memory :191, recover_state :200, confirmation loop :215-254, owner_confirms :279, rehearsal fingerprint :301-313, new settings :315-319.
- rekey.rs:171-177: `let kind = match (options.confirm, rekey.confirmation_needed()) { ... (Some(kind), _) => kind,`
- rehearsal.rs:503-504: `let facts = ContainerFacts::read(container)?; confirmation.refuse_for(facts.confirmation_needed(length)?)?;`, before `self.recover_state(...)`.
- README.md:477-478: "The 64-bit CLI supports every memory level and checks available memory before secrets are entered".
Probe, rerun by the verifier under the heavy-check lock and memory scope; output in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-rekey-late/rerun.out (local evidence):
"rekey --new-pim 5000: exit 4; reached the Argon2 memory reservation: True" / "Container 24 words, valid" / "Format MHFE-BIP39-256-EXPERIMENTAL-3" / "Password typed" / "✗ Error: The computer could not reserve 2 GiB of memory for Argon2"
"rekey --new-mem 99: exit 4; reached the Argon2 memory reservation: True"
"rekey --confirm check --words 24: exit 4; reached the Argon2 memory reservation: True"
"control: rekey --pim 5000: refused at start, exit 2"
Verifier's correction: the --confirm help's "refused before anything is computed" holds literally (the refusal precedes Argon2); the defect is that it follows secret entry. Prior audits: a search of docs/audits for new-pim, new-mem and "new settings" finds no earlier finding on this order.
findings.reproduction:
1. Run `python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/cli-ux/rekey_late_refusals.py` (local evidence, not committed). It drives target/release/mhfe in a pseudo-terminal with the public zero-12 container and a synthetic password, with the address space capped at 1 GiB (RLIMIT_AS) so that the 2 GiB reservation fails before any Argon2 round, and prints which option was refused at start.
2. Cases: `rekey --pim 0 --mem 0 --new-pim 5000 --new-mem 0 --words 12 --confirm check --passphrase-used no --repair-words 0 --new-password own`; the same with `--new-mem 99`; the same with `--words 24 --confirm check`; control `rekey --pim 5000`.
3. Without the cap, the code order (rekey.rs:191-319) shows that a given --new-pim or --new-mem is judged only after the old container's recovery (about 1-2 minutes at the defaults); this full-cost run was not executed.
findings.expected: README.md:477-478: "The 64-bit CLI supports every memory level and checks available memory before secrets are entered". The doc of settings::choose (settings.rs:108-113) says it "refuses at once settings that this computer cannot run ... Nothing secret has been asked yet." The --confirm help (rekey.rs:102-103) says "A way the length does not allow is refused before anything is computed". The same command already refuses --words before the password (rekey.rs:545-570, AUD-008-FUN002) and an invalid --pim at start, and the library offers Rekey::check_confirmation (src/rekey.rs:176-183) and ContainerFacts::confirmation_needed (src/container.rs:135) for an early check. Given new settings and a given --confirm should therefore be judged before the container and the old password are asked.
findings.observed:
With the capped probe all three cases end with exit 4 and "✗ Error: The computer could not reserve 2 GiB of memory for Argon2", after "Container 24 words, valid", "Format MHFE-BIP39-256-EXPERIMENTAL-3" and "Password typed"; the control `rekey --pim 5000` is refused at start with exit 2.
New settings: options.new_pim and options.new_memory_level are read only at rekey.rs:315-318, and settings::choose at :319 refuses them. That call comes after reserve_memory(old_work) (:191), the Argon2 recovery (:195-212), the confirmation loop (:215-254), with --confirm show the display of the recovered phrase (owner_confirms, :279), and with show and an unverified length the passphrase prompt for the rehearsal fingerprint (:301-313). When the new settings are not given, ask_own (settings.rs:220) asks again until the computer can run them; when they are given, `?` ends the run with exit 2 or 4.
--confirm: rekey.rs:177 `(Some(kind), _) => kind` ignores the confirmation_needed() value the same match computes. A built-in check where a wallet or the owner must confirm is refused (REFERENCE_REQUIRED) only in recover_for_rekey (rehearsal.rs:503-504), after the container, the old password, the passphrase question (when --passphrase-used is not given) and the reservation of the old level's memory, though still before any Argon2 round. The help's "refused before anything is computed" is therefore literally true; the defect is the order, and on a computer short of memory this refusal is masked by the memory error.
findings.impact: An out-of-range --new-pim or --new-mem, or a new level this computer cannot hold, is reported only after the old container's full recovery: 1-2 minutes at the defaults, many hours at a high old PIM or memory level (README.md: PIM 1023 takes roughly 17 to 34 hours per recovery). With --confirm show it comes after the original seed phrase has been displayed on the private screen. The run ends with exit 2 or 4 and must be repeated, with the old password typed again. A --confirm way the length does not allow is refused only after the old password has been typed, and on a computer short of memory it is reported as a memory error instead. The output is never wrong and no secret leaves the owner's private screen. Limit of the evidence: the late refusal of the new settings after the full recovery is established by the straight-line code order; a full-cost rekey (2 GiB) was not run under the audit's memory rules.
findings.recommendedFix: In rekey::run, check the new settings right after the old ones: when --new-pim or --new-mem is given, build the new work factor with WorkFactor::new(new_pim.unwrap_or(0), new_mem.unwrap_or(0)) and run the same resource check (check_can_run) before the container is asked. Judge a given --confirm with container.confirmation_needed(length) or Rekey::check_confirmation as soon as the length is known, before the old password is asked. Both rules are the library's, so the command line calls them instead of writing them again.
findings.requiredVerification: Add pseudo-terminal cases for `rekey --new-pim 5000`, `rekey --new-mem 99` and `rekey --words 24 --confirm check` that must end with exit 2 before the container and the old password are asked, and a case where --new-mem exceeds the memory available (capped address space) that is refused at start. Rerun rekey_late_refusals.py: all three cases must be refused at start, like the `rekey --pim 5000` control.

findings.title: Keys typed during startup or long work are taken by the next screen: result screens that show a secret once clear at once, and the first question with a default after the work is answered.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A UI timing defect that can be recovered from by repeating the step; no data is lost and no secret is exposed.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool at a Unix terminal (reproduced on Linux with the release binary built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC; the relevant code last changed 2026-10-09); the Windows console was not examined. Working tree on e8dca53.
- Cause: src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:642-659 (wait_to_leave, wait_to_leave_saying); src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:305-324 (TerminalKeys::next_byte takes bytes already queued), :676 and :762 (tcsetattr with TCSANOW, no flush); src/bin/mhfe/choice.rs:155-159 and :196-199 (TYPED_AHEAD only for questions without a default); terminal.rs:171-187 (Input::choose and choose_here with a default).
- Waits affected: decrypt.rs:193-194 (recovered phrase), new_wallet.rs:292-293 (new phrase, shown once), container_repair.rs:495-496 and :531-532 (container and repair card), made_password.rs:225-226 (made password; :219-220 at HEAD), diceware.rs:222-223, encrypt.rs:266-267 (encrypt check screen).
- Questions with a default after long work: decrypt.rs:181-182 then check.rs:951 ("Is a BIP39 passphrase used ...?", first answer "No"); check.rs:312-313 then phrase_length.rs:79-93 ("How many words ...?", first answer "12 words").
findings.evidence:
Code (working tree):
- terminal.rs:650-659: `hidden_input::with_keys(|next_key| loop { match next_key()? { hidden_input::Key::Enter | hidden_input::Key::Quit => return Ok(()), _ => continue, } })`; nothing ignores keys by time and nothing discards queued input.
- hidden_input.rs:305-324: next_byte takes whatever fill_buf() returns, including bytes already queued at the terminal.
- hidden_input.rs:676 and :762 switch modes with `libc::tcsetattr(..., libc::TCSANOW, ...)`. `grep -rn "tcflush|TCIFLUSH|TCSAFLUSH|FlushConsoleInputBuffer" src/bin/mhfe` returns nothing.
- choice.rs:157: `if start.is_none() && shown_at.elapsed() < TYPED_AHEAD && key != Key::Quit { continue; }`; choice.rs:199 `const TYPED_AHEAD: Duration = Duration::from_millis(200);`
- decrypt.rs:181-182 source_check_passphrase, then check.rs:943-952 "Is a BIP39 passphrase used with {whose}?" through input.choose with answer 0 "No".
- check.rs:312-313 ask_length_after_detection, then phrase_length.rs:79-93 ask_stated with WORD_COUNTS, whose first entry is 12 (src/phrase.rs:21).
Probe outputs (reviewer's scripts, rerun by the verifier under the heavy-check lock with MemoryMax=3G; copies and the verifier's new_enter_during_draw.py in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-typed-ahead/):
- typed_ahead_wait2.py: "exit 0 | tool ended 0.10 s after the card appeared"
- typed_ahead_wait.py: "ended by itself within 1 s: False; exit 130" (one Enter) and "ended by itself within 1 s: True; exit 0" (two Enters)
- typed_ahead_password.py: "ended by itself: False (2.00 s after the wait appeared); exit 130" without the early Enter; "ended by itself: True (0.10 s after the wait appeared); exit 0" with it
- new_enter_during_draw.py: control and Enter-during-draw lines as quoted under Observed.
Prior audits: AUD-010-UI001 and the AUD-018 TYPED_AHEAD fix cover only questions without a default; the PTY suite (check_new_check_question) tests typed-ahead keys for that one question. No AUD-001 to AUD-022 finding reports this.
findings.reproduction:
Probes (local evidence, not committed), each with target/release/mhfe in a pseudo-terminal, public data only:
1. `python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/cli-ux/typed_ahead_wait2.py`: `mhfe repair-words --count 4` given the public zero-12 container followed by two Enters.
2. `python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/cli-ux/typed_ahead_password.py`: `mhfe password` with one Enter typed during startup, while the terminal is in line mode; control without the Enter.
3. `python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-typed-ahead/new_enter_during_draw.py` (verifier): `mhfe new --pim 0` with the synthetic passphrase "synthetic" and the phrase + passphrase check chosen; one Enter is typed 0.5 s into "Drawing a phrase…"; the run is cancelled with Ctrl+C at the password prompt, before any Argon2 work; the phrase is never printed by the probe.
4. From the code only (a full-cost Argon2 run was not executed): run `mhfe check --words auto` on a container of a 24-word phrase and press Enter while "Recovering" runs; the queued Enter answers the length question with 12 and the run ends "✗ does not match" with exit 3.
findings.expected: A screen that shows a secret once (a recovered phrase, the new phrase of `mhfe new`, a repair card, a made password) should stay until the person, having read it, presses Enter or Escape: the doc of wait_to_leave (terminal.rs:642-644) says the person is asked to write down what the screen shows and that "a stray" key "cannot clear the screen too early". A question that follows long work should be answered only by keys pressed after it appeared. The project already treats keys typed ahead as a defect: choice.rs:155-158 ignores keys that arrive within TYPED_AHEAD (200 ms) of a question without a default (the AUD-018 fix, following AUD-010-UI001), but the rule covers neither these waits nor questions with a default.
findings.observed:
- Repair card: "exit 0 | tool ended 0.10 s after the card appeared"; the screen-clear and leave-alternate-screen sequences follow the card.
- `mhfe password`: with one Enter typed during startup, "ended by itself: True (0.10 s after the wait appeared); exit 0"; without it, still waiting after 2 s (exit 130 when stopped).
- typed_ahead_wait.py: container + Enter: "ended by itself within 1 s: False; exit 130"; container + Enter + Enter: "ended by itself within 1 s: True; exit 0".
- `mhfe new`: control "Enter during draw: False; draw took 0.8 s; phrase screen cleared within 2 s without a key: False; went on to the password: False; exit 130"; with the Enter "Enter during draw: True; draw took 3.9 s; phrase screen cleared within 2 s without a key: True; went on to the password: True; exit 130; terminal restored: True". The new phrase, shown only once, is cleared as soon as it appears and the command goes on to the password.
- By code: during Argon2 or other long work the terminal is in its usual line mode with echo, so an Enter typed then stays queued, survives the switch to single-key mode (tcsetattr TCSANOW, no flush) and is taken by wait_to_leave or by run_list with a default (Some(0)). The decrypt passphrase question would take "No"; the length question of check --words auto would take "12 words", after which the built-in check compares the 12-word reading that already failed.
findings.impact: A recovered phrase, the new phrase of `mhfe new` (shown only once), a repair card or a password made by MHFE can vanish about 0.1 s after it appears. A decrypt must then be rerun, about a minute at the defaults and up to hours at a high PIM or memory level. `mhfe new` goes on to encrypt a phrase the owner never saw, although Ctrl+C is still possible at the password prompt. A hurried Enter during `check --words auto` can produce a false "does not match" (exit 3) for a correct password. Nothing secret is disclosed, no data is lost, and the step can be repeated. Limits of the evidence: the decrypt passphrase question and the check length question after Progress were established by code reading only (a full-cost Argon2 run is outside the audit's memory rules); the repair-words case is a pasted double Enter, not long work; the doc line at terminal.rs:644 is about keys other than Enter and Escape, so it is not strictly contradicted.
findings.recommendedFix: Apply the typed-ahead rule to every wait and question that follows long work or a new screen, in one shared place: discard queued input when the screen or question appears (tcflush(TCIFLUSH) or TCSAFLUSH on Unix, FlushConsoleInputBuffer on Windows), or ignore keys that arrive within TYPED_AHEAD, in wait_to_leave and in run_list for questions with a default too.
findings.requiredVerification: Add pseudo-terminal cases that type Enter ahead of the repair card, a made password, the new phrase of `mhfe new` (during the draw) and the first question with a default after Progress, each asserting that the screen stays until a key pressed after it appeared and that the question is not answered by the queued key. Rerun typed_ahead_wait2.py, typed_ahead_password.py and new_enter_during_draw.py: the screen must not clear within 2 s without a new key.

findings.title: At TERM=dumb the container, repair-word and never-use word prompts still write cursor-control sequences and hint rows for their word hints.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A display defect in an uncommon terminal type; input is still read correctly and no secret is shown.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool on Unix (reproduced on Linux with the release binary built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC, newer than the relevant sources); on Windows control_sequences() asks the console for VT processing (hidden_input.rs:838-846) and TERM=dumb was not examined there. Working tree on e8dca53.
- src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:150-165 Input::visible_words (the hinted test at :154-157 has no TERM check).
- src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:697-700 control_sequences() returns true on Unix.
- src/bin/mhfe/typed_line.rs:114-150 remove() and hint() write ESC[nA, ESC[nG and ESC[J raw.
- Callers: terminal.rs:773 (container), container_repair.rs:372 (repair words), chosen_words.rs:169 (word never to use).
- For comparison, TERM=dumb is excluded at terminal.rs:634-640 (terminal_screen_possible) and choice.rs:86-91 (can_run).
findings.evidence:
Code (current tree):
- terminal.rs:154-157: `let hinted = matches!(self, Self::Terminal { .. }) && io::stdin().is_terminal() && io::stderr().is_terminal() && hidden_input::control_sequences();` with no TERM check.
- hidden_input.rs:697-700: `/// A Unix terminal carries out control sequences as they come.` `pub fn control_sequences() -> bool { true }`.
- choice.rs:88-91: can_run has `&& std::env::var_os("TERM").is_none_or(|term| term != "dumb")`.
- terminal.rs:634-640: terminal_screen_possible has `&& std::env::var("TERM").map_or(true, |term| term != "dumb")` (the uncommitted diff to terminal.rs only moves control_sequences() into this function and does not touch visible_words).
- typed_line.rs:126-129: remove() writes `\x1b[{rows_up}A` and `\x1b[{}G\x1b[J`; :138-147: hint() writes `\x1b[J` and `\x1b[{}A\x1b[{column}G`.
- Callers of visible_words: terminal.rs:773, container_repair.rs:372, chosen_words.rs:169 (the last not listed by the reviewer).
Verifier probe output: "TERM=dumb: exit 130; restored True", "ESC before prompt: False", then the three byte strings quoted under Observed; "TERM=xterm-256color: exit 130; restored True", "ESC before prompt: True", "after 'a' / 'b' / Backspace: byte-identical to TERM=dumb."
Prior audits: AUD-016's dumb-container probe (docs/audits/AUD-016-harnesses/native/boundary-probes.py:144-165) strips the hint rows and cursor codes and records only that the container is echoed (audit-16:349, audit-17:302). AUD-015-SEC002 concerns user-typed control characters reaching the terminal, a different issue. No AUD-015 to AUD-022 finding reports cursor control at TERM=dumb.
findings.reproduction: Run `timeout 60 python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-dumb-hints/probe.py` (verifier) or `python3 -B /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/cli-ux/dumb_container_prompt.py` (reviewer); local evidence, not committed. The probe uses the Session helper of scripts/verify-hidden-input.py with the release binary, sets TERM=dumb, runs `mhfe check --fingerprint --pim 0`, types "a", "b" and Backspace at the container prompt, and ends with Ctrl+C before any password or Argon2. It repeats the run with TERM=xterm-256color and compares the bytes written after each key.
findings.expected: The tool's own rule is that TERM=dumb cannot redraw: terminal_screen_possible (terminal.rs:634-640) and choice::can_run (choice.rs:86-91) exclude it, and the doc of Input::choose (terminal.rs:168-170) says that a script "or a terminal that cannot redraw lines" gets numbered answers. Everywhere else in the tool TERM=dumb gets plain sequential output. Word hints, which redraw lines, should therefore be turned on only where lines can redraw, with Input::visible as the fallback. (The workspace rule in AGENTS.md "Terminal output", "TERM=dumb and CLICOLOR=0 turn it off", is literally about colour; the stronger basis is this internal inconsistency.)
findings.observed:
At TERM=dumb the tool writes no ESC byte up to the container prompt. After it, each key and each Backspace writes cursor-control sequences and hint rows byte-identical to the TERM=xterm-256color output:
- after 'a': b'a\x1b[J\r\r\n  136 BIP39 words begin with this letter\x1b[1A\x1b[62G'
- after 'b': b'b\x1b[J\r\r\n  abandon   ability   able ... abuse\x1b[2A\x1b[63G'
- after Backspace: b'\x1b[62G\x1b[J\x1b[J\r\r\n  136 BIP39 words begin with this letter\x1b[1A\x1b[62G'
Both runs exit 130 with the terminal restored. The sequences are written raw through io::stderr(), which anstream does not filter, so NO_COLOR does not remove them either.
findings.impact: In a dumb terminal (Emacs shell-mode, some IDE or serial consoles) every key and Backspace at the container, repair-word or never-use word prompt prints escape codes and hint rows that are never erased, while everywhere else the tool gives TERM=dumb plain sequential output. Input is still read correctly. No secret is involved at the container and repair-word prompts: containers and repair words are public.
findings.recommendedFix: Write one shared "terminal can redraw" predicate (stdin and stderr are terminals, TERM is not dumb, control_sequences() holds) and use it in Input::visible_words, choice::can_run and terminal_screen_possible, falling back to Input::visible where it is false. This also removes the duplicated TERM=dumb test, now written once with std::env::var and once with std::env::var_os.
findings.requiredVerification: Add a TERM=dumb pseudo-terminal assertion that the container prompt, and the repair-word prompt, write no ESC byte after typing and Backspace, while the same input at TERM=xterm-256color still shows the hints. Rerun the dumb-hints probe: no ESC byte after the prompt at TERM=dumb.

findings.title: Without --stdin, a non-terminal standard input is read as answers to the list and container questions, so the advice to run in a terminal or pass --stdin is not reached.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A misleading refusal or loop in a misuse case; nothing is computed, saved or shown, and the exit code is the invalid-input code 2.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool, all platforms (reproduced on Linux with the release binary built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC); commands that read a secret and whose first question is a list or the container: decrypt, encrypt, check, rekey. Working tree on e8dca53.
- src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:63-71 (Input::new(false) builds Terminal whatever stdin is), :80-83 (can_ask_again true for every Terminal), :136-148 (visible reads a line from stdin and fails with "No answer was typed." at end of input), :177-187 (choose_here falls to choose_numbered when choice::can_run() is false), :216-255 (choose_numbered asks again after every refusal), :369-378 (the is_terminal check exists only in read_secret), :396-404 (no_terminal_advice), :759-782 (read_container asks again after every refusal).
- Callers: decrypt.rs:141-144, rekey.rs:141-147, check.rs:235; main.rs:224-251 has no early terminal check.
findings.evidence:
Code: terminal.rs:63-71 `pub fn new(from_standard_input: bool) -> Self { if from_standard_input { Self::Script(io::stdin().lock()) } else { Self::Terminal { command_reads_stdin: true } } }`; :80-83 `matches!(self, Self::Terminal { .. })`; :140-145 `match read_bounded_line(&mut io::stdin().lock())? { Some(line) => Ok(line), None => Err(Failure::invalid_input("No answer was typed.")) }`; :182-186 choose_here falls to choose_numbered; :240-254 the loop calls style::retry and asks again for a Terminal input; :374-378 `if !io::stdin().is_terminal() { return Err(Failure::invalid_input(no_terminal_advice(command_reads_stdin))); }` exists only in read_secret.
Probe outputs (skeptic-cli-ux-pipe/probe.out, probe2.out):
"== 1 decrypt piped two lines" / "Choice [1]: ! Type a number from 1 to 2." (twice) / "✗ Error: No answer was typed." / "exit=2"
"== 2 check --address --coin ETHEREUM </dev/null" / "Choice [1]:" / "✗ Error: No answer was typed." / "exit=2"
"== 3 yes | rekey --pim 0 --mem 0 --words 24 (3s)" / "exit=124" / "427441 err3.txt"
"== 11 encrypt --pim 0 </dev/null" / "✗ Error: There is no terminal to type secrets into. Run the command in a terminal, or pass --stdin and give one answer per line on standard input." / "exit=2"
"== 9 ..." / "! The container is not a valid English BIP39 phrase: it has 4 words, but a" / "exit=2"
"== 12 password </dev/null (no input needed)" / "exit=0"
Tests: scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:1777-1788 checks the advice only for `password --dice`, for `rekey --pim 0 --words 24` with "1\n" and the container piped in to answer the list questions, and for `encrypt --pim 0`; it depends on this behaviour and never covers a command whose first question is a list.
Prior audits: AUD-010-UI005 (audit-10-2026-10-07.md:589-606) fixed which options the advice names; its reproduction piped "1\n<container>\n1\n" into rekey, using this behaviour without reporting it. AUD-015-UI002 is a different loop (a refused --never-use value). AUD-020 to AUD-022 contain no finding on this.
findings.reproduction:
With NO_COLOR=1 and target/release/mhfe (scripts and outputs in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-cli-ux-pipe/ and cli-ux/piped.err, local evidence):
1. `printf 'zoo zoo zoo\nsynthetic-password\n' | mhfe decrypt`
2. `mhfe check --address --coin ETHEREUM </dev/null`
3. `yes | timeout 3 mhfe rekey --pim 0 --mem 0 --words 24`
4. `mhfe decrypt </dev/null`, `mhfe encrypt </dev/null`, `mhfe rekey </dev/null`
5. Compare `mhfe encrypt --pim 0 </dev/null`, whose first question is a secret.
6. `printf 'abandon abandon\nsyntheticpw horse battery staple\n' | mhfe decrypt --pim 0 --mem 0`
7. Control: `mhfe password </dev/null`.
findings.expected: Input::Terminal is documented as "A person at a terminal" (terminal.rs:48), and the tool's message for a missing terminal is the advice at terminal.rs:396-404 ("There is no terminal to type secrets into. Run the command in a terminal, or pass --stdin and give one answer per line on standard input.", or, for rekey, which has no --stdin, "... it has no form for scripts."). README.md (lines 505-552) documents only --stdin for scripts; no document says that piped answers without --stdin are supported. The same misuse should get the same advice whichever question a command asks first.
findings.observed:
- decrypt with two piped lines: both are taken as "Choice [1]:" answers ("! Type a number from 1 to 2." twice), then "✗ Error: No answer was typed.", exit 2.
- check --address --coin ETHEREUM </dev/null: the numbered settings question, then "No answer was typed.", exit 2.
- decrypt, encrypt and rekey </dev/null: "No answer was typed.", exit 2, with no --stdin advice.
- encrypt --pim 0 </dev/null: "There is no terminal to type secrets into. Run the command in a terminal, or pass --stdin and give one answer per line on standard input.", exit 2: the same misuse, a different message.
- yes | rekey --pim 0 --mem 0 --words 24: the container is asked again without end ("Container ...: ! The container is not a valid English BIP39 phrase: it has 1 words"), 427,441 stderr lines in 3 s, stopped by the timeout with exit 124 (the reviewer's run: 830,541 lines in 5 s).
- decrypt --pim 0 --mem 0 with a short container line and a password-like line: the second line is taken as a container answer and refused with "it has 4 words", without its text; exit 2.
- password </dev/null: exit 0.
findings.impact: Someone who forgets --stdin, or a launcher without a terminal, gets the misleading "No answer was typed." or, with a producer that never ends, an endless retry loop, instead of the advice to run in a terminal or pass --stdin that the same misuse gets when a secret is asked first. A password-like line can be consumed as a menu or container answer; it is not echoed, and the refusal reveals only how many words it has (unknown words are named only by position, src/phrase.rs:55), a negligible disclosure under this misuse. Limits: the endless loop needs a producer that never ends, such as `yes`; any finite pipe or /dev/null ends at end of input with exit 2, and "No answer was typed." is literally true for /dev/null.
findings.recommendedFix: For a command that reads a secret, refuse at the start with no_terminal_advice when standard input is not a terminal and --stdin is not given, before any question. Commands that read no secret, such as repair, and `mhfe password`, which needs no input, keep working.
findings.requiredVerification: Add pipe tests for commands whose first question is a list (decrypt, encrypt, check, rekey without --pim) and for one whose first question is the container (decrypt --pim 0 --mem 0), each with /dev/null and with piped lines, asserting exit 2 with the no-terminal advice and no question asked; keep `mhfe password </dev/null` exiting 0. Adjust verify-hidden-input.py:1777-1788 so that it no longer relies on answering list questions from a pipe.

findings.releaseBlockingReason: Presentation only; no secret is shown and no behaviour changes.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool, all platforms (release binary built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC; serve.rs and style.rs unchanged since 2026-10-09).

Running text wraps at 78 columns." Every other person-facing command of mhfe prints its title (new, encrypt, decrypt, check, rekey, wallets, repair, repair-words, password, self-test, the menu), and the other text helpers of style.rs (hint, warn, warn_now, alarm, retry, error_wrapped, fact_wrapped) wrap.
