findings.title: When a phrase also reads as another length, the command-line tool tells the owner to write down the word count but not to keep that note apart from the container, as the specification's creation step 2 recommends.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: SHOULD-level wording for an event of about one phrase in four billion; no container is wrong, no recovery fails and the format is unaffected.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool, all platforms: encrypt, new and rekey (release binary built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC; encrypt.rs has no uncommitted changes). Browser package guidance as documented.
- src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:388-409 (warn_if_detection_would_mislead; text at :400-406), called from encrypt.rs:150, new_wallet.rs:133-136 and rekey.rs:322-325.
- src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:304-320 (what_to_keep: RepairWords at :313 "apart from the container phrase", WordCount at :316 without it).
- src/operation.rs:128-133 (KeepItem::RepairWords documented as "kept apart from the container phrase"; WordCount only "to choose at recovery").
- Browser guidance: docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:863-867, web/client.d.ts:92-95, web/client.js:242-245.
- README.md:182 (password apart) and the encrypt section (README.md:219-221, 272-277).
- Specification: mhfe_spec/README.md:370-375 (creation step 2).
findings.evidence:
- mhfe_spec/README.md:372-375, quoted under Expected.
- encrypt.rs:400-406: `style::warn(&format!("Write down that your phrase has {words} words."), &format!("By rare chance it also reads as {} words: recover it with mhfe decrypt --words {words}.", others));` with no "apart" wording.
- encrypt.rs:313 `KeepItem::RepairWords => "the repair words apart from the container phrase".to_owned(),` and :316 `KeepItem::WordCount(words) => format!("the word count, {words}"),`; unit-test expectations at encrypt.rs:627 "the 24 words, the password and the word count, 15" and :651 "the 24 words, the password, PIM 1 and the word count, 24".
- src/operation.rs:128-133: `/// The repair words, kept apart from the container phrase.` `RepairWords,` ... `/// The original phrase's word count, to choose at recovery.` `WordCount(usize),`.
- docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:865-866: "tell the user to note the word count and choose it during recovery"; web/client.d.ts:94 "tell the user to note the word count and choose it then"; web/client.js:244 "the page tells the user to note the word count and choose it then".
- Verifier's run: release binary, public AMBIGUOUS_12_WORDS phrase, exit 2; output lines as quoted under Observed ("Phrase 12 words, valid" precedes the warning).
- Prior audits: a grep of mhfe docs/audits (*.md, *.json, including AUD-020 to AUD-022) for "note apart", "keep that note" and "word count" finds no earlier mhfe finding. The rule originates in the specification's AUD-006-SEC001 (mhfe_spec/docs/audits/audit-06-2026-10-09.md:186-200, medium: "The recovery plan advised recording the source length next to the backup"), verified in the specification but not carried into the CLI wording.
findings.reproduction: Read encrypt.rs:388-409 and :304-320. The case is reachable without Argon2 with the public phrase AMBIGUOUS_12_WORDS of scripts/public-test-data.mjs: `printf '%s\n' "<AMBIGUOUS_12_WORDS>" | NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe encrypt --stdin` with only the phrase on standard input prints the warning before it asks for the password and exits 2 when the input ends (as verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs:247-257 does). The verifier's output is in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-word-count-apart/encrypt-ambiguous.out (local evidence).
findings.expected: Specification creation step 2 (mhfe_spec/README.md:372-375, added in mhfe_spec bbd2974 for specification 0.6.0 as the fix of the specification's AUD-006-SEC001): the application "SHOULD tell the user to write down the word count of the original seed phrase and keep that note apart from the container, like the password: a note showing fewer than 24 words also shows that a 24-word reading is not the original seed phrase." mhfe v0.6.0 implements specification 0.6.0.
findings.observed:
The warning says only:
"! Write down that your phrase has 12 words."
"! By rare chance it also reads as 21 words: recover it with mhfe decrypt"
"! --words 12."
and the run then ends "✗ Error: Standard input ended before this answer: Container password" (exit 2). The output never says where to keep the note. The Keep summary renders the item as "the word count, 15", while the repair words get "the repair words apart from the container phrase". The browser guidance says only to "note the word count". README.md:182 tells the user to keep the password apart, but nothing tells them to keep the word-count note apart.
findings.impact: In about one phrase in four billion the owner is told to write the word count down but not where to keep it. A note reading, for example, "12 words" kept next to a 24-word container shows that any 24-word decoy reading is not the original seed phrase, which weakens the decoy disclosure that the deniability analysis relies on. The rarity of the trigger bounds the impact; no container or recovery is affected.
findings.recommendedFix: Add "keep the note apart from the container, like the password" to the warning, and render KeepItem::WordCount as "the word count, N, apart from the container phrase". Model the "apart" property on the library's KeepItem, as RepairWords already is in its documentation, so that the browser's keep list carries it too, and add the same advice to README.md's encrypt section, docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:865-866, web/client.d.ts:94 and web/client.js:244.
findings.requiredVerification: Update the what_to_keep unit tests (encrypt.rs:627 and :651) to the new wording; extend the CLI check in verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs:247-257 (AMBIGUOUS_12_WORDS through `mhfe encrypt --stdin`, input ending before the password, so no Argon2) to assert that the warning says to keep the note apart from the container; add a browser package check that the keep item for the word count carries the "apart" property.

findings.title: mhfe serve's refusal of a malformed checksum file shows the text-mode format with one space instead of the required two, because the message wrapper collapses runs of spaces.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Presentation of a safe refusal: nothing is served, the correct format is documented, and the binary-mode form shown beside it is correct.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool, `mhfe serve` and the menu's fast-mode entry, all platforms (release binary built 2026-10-13 00:21 UTC; serve.rs and style.rs unchanged since 2026-10-09). The Python launcher prints the message unwrapped and is not affected.
- src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:129-135 (the malformed-file message, two spaces at :131), :161-166 (split_checksum_line requires a second space or `*`), :693 (unit test lists one space as malformed).
- src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:384-404 (wrap; :389 drops empty words), :309-312 (error_lines), :361-371 (marked).
- src/bin/mhfe/main.rs:261 (style::error_wrapped) and src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:150-153 (style::warn "The fast mode is not offered.").
- packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:238-241 (the same text, printed unwrapped).
findings.evidence:
- serve.rs:130-132: `"{} must hold exactly one line, \"<SHA-256>  <page>.html\" or \"<SHA-256> \` `*<page>.html\"; nothing was served."`
- style.rs:389: `for word in paragraph.split(' ').filter(|word| !word.is_empty()) {`, which joins the words with `line.push(' ')`; a run of two spaces always becomes one space, or a line break where the wrap falls on it.
- Both screens wrap: main.rs:261 style::error_wrapped → error_lines (style.rs:309) → wrap; menu.rs:153 style::warn → marked (style.rs:361) → wrap.
- serve.rs:163-164: `let rest = line.get(SHA256_HEX_DIGITS..)?.strip_prefix(' ')?; let name = rest.strip_prefix(' ').or_else(|| rest.strip_prefix('*'))?;`, so one space is refused.
- serve.rs:693: the unit test lists `format!("{digest} tool.html\n")` among the malformed inputs.
- packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:238-241 prints the same text with two spaces, unwrapped.
- The existing test checks failure.message before wrapping, so it cannot catch the problem.
- Probe outputs as quoted under Observed (verifier: skeptic-serve-format; reviewer: probe-menu-malformed.txt, whose path line reads "! /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/fast-mode-serving/menu-malformed/mhfe-fast-mode.sha256").
- Prior audits: AUD-004-FUN002 fixed the binary-mode parsing and its remediation made "the refusal message ... name both forms"; no prior audit reports this message's rendering.
findings.reproduction:
1. In a scratch folder, put any index.html and a mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 holding "not a checksum line".
2. Run `target/release/mhfe serve <absolute path>/index.html 2>&1 | cat -A` and `target/release/mhfe serve a/index.html 2>&1 | cat -A` (exit 2 each), or start a copy of mhfe from that folder with no arguments to see the menu warning.
3. Write the checksum line as the message shows it (the digest, one space, index.html): it is refused again as malformed (serve.rs:161-166; unit test at :693).
The verifier's folder is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-serve-format/a/; the reviewer's menu output is in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/fast-mode-serving/probe-menu-malformed.txt (local evidence).
findings.expected: The on-screen format guidance should show the format the parser accepts: "<SHA-256>  <page>.html" with two spaces in text mode, as the source string at serve.rs:131 and the Python launcher (mhfe-fast-mode.py:239) hold, and as docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:726-728 describes ("the page's SHA-256, two spaces and its file name, or one space and * before the name").
findings.observed:
With the absolute path the refusal reads (cat -A, path anonymised):
"✗ Error: /home/user/.../skeptic-serve-format/a/mhfe-fast-mode.sha256$"
"         must hold exactly one line, \"<SHA-256> <page>.html\" or \"<SHA-256>$"
"         *<page>.html\"; nothing was served.$"
so the text-mode form shows one space. With the relative path the line break happens to fall on the double space: "✗ Error: a/mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 must hold exactly one line, \"<SHA-256>$" / "         <page>.html\" or \"<SHA-256> *<page>.html\"; nothing was served.$". The menu warning, which always shows the absolute path of the program's folder, reads "! must hold exactly one line, \"<SHA-256> <page>.html\" or \"<SHA-256>". A line written from the screen with one space is refused again.
findings.impact: The only format guidance on screen is wrong for the text-mode form, so a person who writes the checksum line by hand from it is refused again. The binary form shown beside it is correct, the help and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md describe the format correctly, the shipped checksum file has the right form, and a refusal never serves anything. No security or data impact.
findings.recommendedFix: Write the format without depending on a run of spaces, in both launchers, for example with the wording docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:726-728 already uses: "the page's SHA-256, two spaces and its file name, or one space and * before the name". The alternative is to make wrap() keep runs of spaces.
findings.requiredVerification: Add a test that renders the refusal through the style wrapping, as the screen shows it (error_lines and marked, at the 78-column width and with a long absolute path), and checks the format text; keep the Python launcher's text in step with it. Rerun the skeptic-serve-format probe with both paths and the menu probe: the shown format must describe two spaces.

findings.title: Both fast-mode launchers print the page's address only when the browser opener cannot be started, so an opener that starts but fails, or an unwanted browser, leaves no address on screen.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Usability of the launcher only; the opener usually prints the address itself and --no-browser is a documented workaround on the command line.
findings.affected:
Native `mhfe serve` and the menu's fast-mode entry, and the Python launcher packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py (byte-identical release copy dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py); serve.rs has no uncommitted edits (last commit 2026-10-09).
- src/bin/mhfe/serve.rs:231-233 (address printed only with --no-browser or when open_browser() returns Err), :274-286 (open_browser spawns `open`, `cmd /C start ""` or `xdg-open` and returns at once).
- packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:347-348 (the same with webbrowser.open()).
- src/bin/mhfe/menu.rs:146-150 (the menu entry runs `serve <page>` without --no-browser; :149); a double-click on mhfe-fast-mode.py likewise opens a browser.
- Platforms: on macOS (`open`) and Windows (`cmd.exe`) the opener always exists, so the Rust fallback can practically never run there; on Linux it runs only when xdg-open is missing entirely.
findings.evidence:
- serve.rs:231-233: `if options.no_browser || open_browser(&address).is_err() { eprintln!("Open {} in your browser.", paint(ACCENT, &address)); }`
- serve.rs:275-286: `Command::new("open")` on macOS, `Command::new("cmd")` with `["/C", "start", ""]` on Windows, `Command::new("xdg-open")` otherwise; then `command.arg(address).spawn().map(|_| ())`, which never waits for the opener.
- mhfe-fast-mode.py:347-348: `if options.no_browser or not webbrowser.open(address): print("Open {} in your browser.".format(address), file=sys.stderr)`; for xdg-open, Python's BackgroundBrowser returns `p.poll() is None` just after Popen, which is True while the opener is still starting.
- menu.rs:149: `entry.action = Action::Run(vec!["serve".into(), page.into_os_string()]);` with no --no-browser.
- Probe output (skeptic-serve-address/probe-launchers.txt), cases A to E as quoted under Observed; synthetic tool.html with SHA-256 dedd3907…2617 and its mhfe-fast-mode.sha256; stand-in failbin/xdg-open is `exit 3`.
- Mitigating evidence: /usr/bin/xdg-open prints "xdg-open: no method available for opening '<url>'" and exits 3 (exit_failure_operation_impossible).
- Prior audits: a grep of docs/audits for open_browser, webbrowser.open, opener, "in your browser" or a serve-address finding found nothing.
findings.reproduction: Put a script named xdg-open that exits 3 without printing first on PATH (for Python, with DISPLAY set; the reviewer also set BROWSER to that script). Run `mhfe serve page.html` and `python3 mhfe-fast-mode.py page.html` beside a valid checksum file, each stopped by `timeout -s INT 2`. No "Open http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ in your browser." line appears. Repeat with an empty PATH and with --no-browser: the address is printed. Verifier's files: /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-serve-address/ (probe-launchers.txt); reviewer's: probes/fast-mode-serving/probe-e-rust-opener-fails.txt and probe-e-python-opener-fails.txt (local evidence).
findings.expected: The launchers' own fallback (serve.rs:231, mhfe-fast-mode.py:347) is meant to print the address when the browser cannot be opened, and the person needs it whenever the page does not appear. No written contract promises the address in the default mode: the help of both launchers documents --no-browser as "Print the address instead of opening the browser" (serve.rs:87-92, mhfe-fast-mode.py:17 and :317). The defect is that the fallback is incomplete and that the menu and double-click routes cannot ask for the address.
findings.observed:
- A (mhfe serve, failing opener on PATH): "✓ SHA-256 of tool.html verified: dedd3907…2617" and "✓ Fast mode is running. Close this window or press Ctrl+C to stop."; no address.
- B (mhfe serve, empty PATH): "Open http://127.0.0.1:43079/ in your browser." is printed.
- C (Python, failing opener on PATH, DISPLAY set): "SHA-256 of tool.html verified: …" and "Fast mode is running. …"; no address.
- D (Python, empty PATH): "Open http://127.0.0.1:56471/ in your browser." is printed.
- E (mhfe serve --no-browser): the address is printed.
The reviewer's runs with index.html give the same result for both launchers.
findings.impact: The screen shows no address when the opener starts but cannot show the page (no default browser set, or Windows' "How do you want to open this?" dialog), or when the default browser is one the person does not want to use. The person must stop and rerun with --no-browser, which the menu route cannot pass. Limits: the real /usr/bin/xdg-open prints "xdg-open: no method available for opening '<url>'" to stderr, which the opener inherits, so the common Linux failure shows the URL in the opener's own message, though not as advice; with an unwanted default browser the address is in that browser's address bar. The Python launcher on Linux also depends on a race: if the opener exits before poll() runs, webbrowser tries the next registered browser instead of printing the address.
findings.recommendedFix: Always print the address in both launchers, as one line after opening, for example: "Opened http://127.0.0.1:PORT/ in your browser; if it did not open, open that address yourself." This keeps to the minimal-text rule for running commands.
findings.requiredVerification: Add a test for each launcher (serve.rs tests or the launcher suite, and scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py) that runs it with a stand-in opener exiting 3 and asserts that the address line is printed; rerun the verifier's probe-launchers cases A and C, which must now print the address, and keep B, D and E unchanged.

findings.title: The Python fast-mode launcher's terminal output and help do not follow the workspace's terminal-output rules, which mhfe serve follows.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Presentation only: the launcher works, refuses correctly and escapes control characters; only its look breaks the written rule.
findings.affected:
packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py (369 lines) and its byte-identical release copy dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py, on every platform (Python 3.8 or later; observed with Python 3.14.4).
- packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py:307-353 (main): Parser at :308-318 without an epilog; "Error: …" at :335; "SHA-256 of … verified" at :337-339, "Open … in your browser." at :348 and "Fast mode is running." at :349, all without marks.
- class Parser at :87-93 (argparse subclass).
findings.evidence:
- mhfe-fast-mode.py:335 `print("Error: {}".format(refusal), file=sys.stderr)`; :337-339 `print("SHA-256 of {} verified: {}".format(shown(os.path.basename(path)), digest), file=sys.stderr)`; :348 `print("Open {} in your browser.".format(address), file=sys.stderr)`; :349 `print("Fast mode is running. Close this window or press Ctrl+C to stop.", file=sys.stderr)`; :308-311 `Parser(prog="mhfe-fast-mode.py", description=...)` with no epilog.
- `cmp packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py dist/core/mhfe-fast-mode.py`: identical.
- mhfe serve uses style::ok, style::examples_with_note and style::option_help (serve.rs:77-97, 200-236); `mhfe serve --help` has "Usage:", "Arguments:", "Options:", "Examples:" and a closing safety paragraph; with CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 its mark is ESC[1mESC[31m"✗ Error:"ESC[0m.
- Coordinator evidence run-launchers.json: entries [0] and [3] (mhfe serve) launcherStderr "✓ SHA-256 of index.html verified: 58c7db41..." ... "✓ Fast mode is running. ..."; entries [1] and [4] (Python) the same lines without ✓.
- Verifier's probes (Python 3.14.4, scratch folder skeptic-python-launcher-ui): outputs as quoted under Observed.
- Prior audits: a grep of docs/audits finds no finding on the launcher's terminal style; AUD-004's CHECK-UI-003 passed "help and script output", probably before the rule existed or without comparing against it. No exemption is recorded in AGENTS.md, the mhfe docs or README.
findings.reproduction: Run `python3 packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py --help` and `python3 packaging/mhfe-fast-mode.py missing.html` in a terminal and compare with `target/release/mhfe serve --help` and `target/release/mhfe serve missing.html`. For colour, run the help through a pseudo-terminal (`script -qc`) with and without CLICOLOR=0, and with CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 into a pipe. The coordinator's recorded runs are in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/fast-mode-serving/run-launchers.json (local evidence).
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md, "Terminal output" (lines 114-121): "Every command-line tool here looks the same; mhfe (src/bin/mhfe/style.rs) is the model"; a bold green ✓ for success and a red "✗ Error:" for errors; running text wraps at 78 columns; "Help has an overview, then \"Usage:\", \"Commands:\", \"Options:\" and \"Examples:\" sections in the same colours, with grey notes and a yellow safety line at the end"; colour only on a terminal, with NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, TERM=dumb and CLICOLOR=0 honoured. Nothing exempts the script: the only recorded constraint is the owner's choice of "stdlib only, Python 3.8+", and the standard library can print ✓, ✗ and ANSI codes.
findings.observed:
- `--help` prints argparse's default "usage: mhfe-fast-mode.py [-h] [--no-browser] [file]", "positional arguments:", "options:", with no Examples section and no safety line (exit 0).
- `missing.html` prints "Error: There is no readable mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 in /home/user/...: No such file or directory. The fast mode serves a page ..." on a single line of about 260 characters, without ✗ or colour, exit 2; `mhfe serve missing.html` prints "✗ Error: There is no readable mhfe-fast-mode.sha256 in .: No such file or" wrapped with a hanging indent, exit 2.
- Success: mhfe serve prints "✓ SHA-256 of index.html verified: 58c7db41…" and "✓ Fast mode is running. …"; the Python launcher prints the same lines without marks.
- On Python 3.14.4 argparse colours the help on a TTY by default in its own scheme (ESC[1;34m "usage: ", ESC[1;35m program name, ESC[32m "-h", ESC[36m "--no-browser"), not mhfe's bold-cyan scheme; it honours NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb but stays coloured with CLICOLOR=0 on a TTY and uncoloured with CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 into a pipe. The refusal line has no colour or mark on a TTY.
findings.impact: Presentation only: the two launchers of the same feature look different, against a written workspace rule, in a shipped artifact; on Python 3.14 the help's colouring also ignores CLICOLOR=0 and CLICOLOR_FORCE. No secret, network or integrity effect; refusals, exit codes and control-character escaping (shown()) are correct.
findings.recommendedFix: Give the script a small standard-library style helper: ✓ for success, "✗ Error:" for errors, text wrapped at 78 columns, and the sixteen colours only on a TTY, honouring NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, TERM=dumb and CLICOLOR=0; pass color=False to the Parser (or apply the same environment rules) so that argparse 3.14 does not use its own colours; add a help epilog with Examples and the safety line. On Windows, where the script is meant to be double-clicked, Python 3.8-3.13 does not enable VT processing on a legacy console, so the ANSI codes need enabling (SetConsoleMode through ctypes) or must be left out there, and a redirected stream with a legacy code page may need errors="replace" for the marks. Otherwise, record an owner exemption for this stdlib-only script in AGENTS.md.
findings.requiredVerification: Extend scripts/verify-fast-mode-script.py to compare the launcher's success and refusal lines and its help sections with mhfe serve's (marks, "Usage:"/"Options:"/"Examples:" and the safety line, 78-column wrapping), and to check colour under NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR=0, CLICOLOR_FORCE=1 into a pipe and TERM=dumb through a pseudo-terminal; rerun run-launchers.mjs and confirm both launchers print the same marked lines.

findings.title: The AUD-020-SEC002 regression test passes without running its child test when the child's name filter matches nothing.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not blocking: in the reviewed tree the child runs and the refusal it guards holds, so the defect is a loss of test fidelity that only appears after a rename or move, with no runtime exposure.
findings.affected: mhfe working tree at HEAD e8dca53a5d17cb80f1f5ac1f5a40b351f939e7e7 plus uncommitted changes. Both tests below are part of the uncommitted change to src/bin/mhfe/made_password.rs. Files and lines: src/bin/mhfe/made_password.rs:239-260 (parent test a_generated_password_never_prints_without_a_private_screen, fn at 240, assertions at 251-259) and :262-276 (ignored child refuse_generated_password_child, with no environment guard). The production check it covers is made_password.rs:210-216 in show() (`if !screen.shows_privately()` refuses with 'No private screen to show the generated password on.'). For comparison: the G10 child pattern at src/bin/mhfe/protect.rs:1500-1511, 1547-1555 and 1566. Also src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:698-700 (Unix control_sequences(), constant true), :836-846 (Windows VT activation) and src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:634-640 (terminal_screen_possible). Build: the native command-line test binary (the cargo tests of the mhfe bin) on every platform. No platform has an automated test of the Windows VT-failure branch.
findings.evidence:
Code (working tree, HEAD e8dca53 plus uncommitted changes):
- made_password.rs:241-250 spawns current_exe() with the arguments `--exact`, `made_password::tests::refuse_generated_password_child`, `--ignored`, `--nocapture`, with stdin null.
- made_password.rs:259: `assert!(output.status.success(), "the private-screen refusal failed");`
- made_password.rs:262-264: `#[test] #[ignore = "isolated no-terminal child, executed by the parent regression"] fn refuse_generated_password_child()`, with no environment guard.
- protect.rs:1500-1501: 'Exit codes of the process that [`g10_isolated_command`] forks, which its test process passes on as its own. They are not 0 or 101, the codes of a test process that ran no such child.'
- protect.rs:1503-1511: `mod g10 { ISOLATED = 40, NO_NAMESPACE = 41, CHECKS_FAILED = 42, NOT_EMPTY = 43, NO_CHILD = 44, VARIABLE = "MHFE_TEST_G10_CHILD" }`.
- protect.rs:1554: `other => panic!("the test process ran no isolated command: {other:?}")`.
- protect.rs:1566: `if std::env::var_os(g10::VARIABLE).is_none() { return; }`.
- hidden_input.rs:698-700 (Unix): `pub fn control_sequences() -> bool { true }`.
- terminal.rs:634-640: terminal_screen_possible now includes hidden_input::control_sequences().

Runs of the existing test binary (sha256 above). Two independent verifier probes ran it under flock and systemd-run with MemoryMax=3G. Their local evidence is /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-made-password/probe2.log and /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-arc003-vacuous-child/run.log (sha256 39afb6c32feb97a367bea133843700ea84f45b016449d07b2918269783d44cc9). The reviewer's own log, vacuous-child/run.log, has sha256 4224e9be8a84b55ac72a0c4f304ec0a6c71e1feeb889009b0f1c63ae3a122b74.
- Parent as written: '1 passed ... 130 filtered out', exit 0.
- Child under its real name: 'test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 130 filtered out', exit 0, 0 bytes on stderr.
- Child renamed (made_password::tests::renamed_child, or ..._renamed): 'running 0 tests ... test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 131 filtered out', exit 0, 0 bytes on stderr. All three parent assertions hold.
- Child moved by a refactor (password::made::tests::refuse_generated_password_child): 'running 0 tests ... 131 filtered out', exit 0. All three assertions hold.
- Control: a G10-style name that does not exist also exits 0, a code the G10 parent rejects.

Nothing else runs the child:
- scripts/check.sh:44 is a plain `cargo test --locked`.
- .github/workflows/vectors.yml:35-36 runs --ignored only for suite3_vectors and suite4_vectors.
- grep finds no other reference to refuse_generated_password_child or PUBLIC_DISPLAY_SENTINEL outside made_password.rs and the AUD-020/AUD-021 records.

Other coverage: scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:1111-1118 expects the preflight refusal with --new-password words under TERM=dumb.

Prior records:
- docs/audits/AUD-021-2026-10-12.md:111 and :127 record the parent failing before the fix (exit 101, panic at made_password.rs:245:9).
- AUD-021-2026-10-12.md:74 lists the Windows VT failure as not executed.
- AUD-020-2026-10-12.md:161, the required verification of AUD-020-SEC002, asks for an injected console whose VT activation returns false. That verification is not yet met.

No earlier AUD-020/021/022 finding covers the vacuous child.

Hygiene note: one verifier probe briefly wrote two temporary capture files into the mhfe working directory and deleted them in the same command. git status was unchanged afterwards.
findings.reproduction:
1. In the mhfe working tree, build the command-line test binary as scripts/check.sh does (`cargo test --locked`). The baseline run produced target/debug/deps/mhfe-adeb1a8c5c5aa0cf (sha256 1947024caccfe7031334b0dbde9b3799d7aa1c49a5b6559e092445c7d3706315). Its `--list --ignored` output shows made_password::tests::refuse_generated_password_child, so it contains the uncommitted test.
2. Run `B=target/debug/deps/mhfe-adeb1a8c5c5aa0cf; $B --exact made_password::tests::refuse_generated_password_child --ignored --nocapture </dev/null; echo $?`. It prints '1 passed' and exits 0.
3. Run the same command with a name that matches nothing, as would happen after a rename or a module move: `$B --exact made_password::tests::renamed_child --ignored --nocapture </dev/null; echo $?`, or the moved path password::made::tests::refuse_generated_password_child. It prints 'running 0 tests ... test result: ok. 0 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 131 filtered out', writes nothing to stderr and exits 0.
4. Apply the parent's three assertions (made_password.rs:251-259) to both outputs: no sentinel on stderr, none on stdout, and a success exit. Both runs pass all three, so the parent cannot tell a child that ran from one that did not.
findings.expected:
A regression check must be able to fail (workspace AGENTS.md:66: 'The checks must be able to fail'). CHECK-ARC-003 requires that a test-only seam not give a false impression that the production path was exercised. The repository already uses a pattern for isolated child tests that meets this:
- protect.rs:1500-1501 gives the G10 child dedicated exit codes 40-44, which 'are not 0 or 101, the codes of a test process that ran no such child'.
- protect.rs:1554 panics on any other code.
- protect.rs:1566 makes the child return at once unless the parent has set MHFE_TEST_G10_CHILD.
The parent of the AUD-020-SEC002 regression should likewise prove that its child ran.
findings.observed:
The parent checks only three things: the sentinel is absent from stderr (made_password.rs:251-254), it is absent from stdout (255-258), and `output.status.success()` holds (259). A libtest filter that matches no test exits 0 with no output. The child's name is a string literal that neither the compiler nor clippy checks. A renamed, removed or moved child therefore leaves the parent green while it tests nothing.

The child (262-276) also has no environment guard. By reading only (not executed): a bare `cargo test --bins -- --ignored` at an interactive terminal would run it inside the main test process. There terminal_screen_possible (terminal.rs:634-640) is true, so the alternate screen is entered and wait_to_leave blocks for a key before the child panics. No documented command does this: the documented ignored run of the bin filters on every_part_passes_the_full_self_test.

On Unix, hidden_input::control_sequences() is a constant true (hidden_input.rs:698-700). The Windows VT-failure branch that the AUD-020-SEC002 fix is named for therefore has no automated test anywhere. AUD-020 and AUD-021 already record this as a known gap; it is not a new defect.
findings.impact:
The child is the only automated test of the refusal inside show() (made_password.rs:212-216), the check AUD-020-SEC002 asked for. After a rename or move of the child or its module, it silently stops testing that refusal while every check stays green, so a regression of the fix could go unnoticed.

Limits:
- Today the child runs and passes, and AUD-021 recorded the parent failing before the fix (exit 101, panic at made_password.rs:245), so the check currently has teeth.
- The reviewer's 'the only regression guard of the generated-password refusal' overstates the gap. scripts/verify-hidden-input.py:1111-1118 separately tests the earlier preflight refusal of `encrypt` and `rekey` with `--new-password words` under TERM=dumb.
- No secret is exposed and no runtime behaviour changes.
findings.recommendedFix:
- Make the child prove that it ran. Either have it exit with a dedicated code after the refusal, as g10_isolated_command does, or print a fixed marker, and have the parent require that code or marker. At the least, require '1 passed' in the child's stdout.
- Make the child return at once unless an environment variable set by the parent is present, as protect.rs:1566 does.
- Consider a small capability seam: a trait or parameter that answers whether the screen can be switched (workspace AGENTS.md principle 5, Depend on abstractions). The VT-failure branch could then be unit-tested on any host. That would also meet the still-open required verification of AUD-020-SEC002 (an injected console whose VT activation returns false).
findings.requiredVerification:
- Temporarily rename the child, or change the parent's filter string, and confirm that the parent test now fails. Restore it and confirm that the parent passes with the real child.
- Run `cargo test --bins -- --ignored` without the parent's variable and confirm that the child returns without entering a private screen.
- If a capability seam is added: a unit test in which VT activation reports false must show that show() refuses before the sentinel reaches stdout or stderr.
- Run the targeted test and the cargo test step of scripts/check.sh.

findings.reproduction:
1. Read GeneratorCheck::run (src/new_password/known_answers.rs:109-146). The startup path has no strength case; the only one sits inside `if tier == Tier::Full` (134-144).
2. Grep src/ and web/ for other self-check uses of Strength. There are none.
3. Measure the two inputs. A separate crate depending on mhfe by path (the verifier's probe at /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-strength-selfcheck/, run as `cargo +1.99.0 run --offline --release` under flock and systemd-run with MemoryMax=3G) gives:
   - Strength::of("password") = 12.925 bits, exactly one EFF dice word. 'password' is EFF word 43644 (vendor/eff-large-wordlist/eff_large_wordlist.txt:4522).
   - The check-word draw DRAWS[0].expected = 77.55 bits, six dice words.
   Both take the dice-word path (strength.rs:108-110), so no self-check at either tier reaches read_parts.

Not executed, because the repository is read-only for this audit: the reviewer's mutation (change YEAR_BITS or a dictionary entry and observe that every self-check still passes). It follows from the measured bits above, since read_parts is the only code that uses YEAR_BITS.
findings.observed:
The only self-check of the estimate (known_answers.rs:134-144) is:
`if tier == Tier::Full { findings.one(|| expect(Strength::of("password").is_weak() && !Strength::of(DRAWS[0].expected).is_weak(), "the strength estimate misjudges a password")) }`

It has three weaknesses:
- It runs at the full tier only.
- It compares two booleans, not exact output.
- Both of its inputs avoid read_parts.

No self-check at either tier therefore exercises the rest of the estimate: the COMMON list, the dictionary, substitutions, years (YEAR_BITS), runs, keyboard rows, character kinds or the 100-character limit. A change there (YEAR_BITS, SUBSTITUTIONS, continues, character_bits, the sort and dedup in WordList::new) leaves both verdicts unchanged.

The unit tests (known_answers.rs:153-172) damage only a draw, so no test shows that the strength case can fail.

The comment at known_answers.rs:135-136 ('The most common leaked password is weak') does not match what the case actually exercises.

docs/API.md:580-582 accurately says the estimate is checked only at the full tier, so this is a deviation from the rule, not a wrong document.
findings.impact:
A fault on the user's machine that shifts the read_parts rules or the COMMON list passes every self-check, for example a miscompilation or a broken WebAssembly build. At startup nothing checks the estimate whose rating decides the weak-password warning in both front ends.

- The estimate only drives a warning. It does not affect encryption or recovery.
- Unit tests (strength.rs:272-334) cover the rules during development.
- The reviewer's 'a damaged word list copy' is overstated. The dictionary is built from the EFF and BIP39 lists that other startup checks cover (bip39-words, password-check-word, word-hints). The surface no check covers is the read_parts rules and the COMMON list.

Use inputs that reach read_parts, and give the source of each value in a comment as AGENTS.md requires. Add the dice-word case 'abacus zoom yearbook zipfile' = 51.7, which strength.rs:309 already asserts. ('password' alone cannot serve as a read_parts known answer, because it is a dice word.)

findings.title: Time units, a time-range formatter, the 33-byte word-bits size, the GF(2^11) field size and the millibit divisor are written again instead of derived from their sources.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not blocking: nothing shown to the user is wrong or inconsistent today, and there is no security or correctness effect, only a drift risk.
findings.affected:
All lines are committed code (blame d52dff8b, 3a705db6 and e038fa31). The uncommitted changes do not touch them.

Time units and formatters (native CLI):
- src/bin/mhfe/settings.rs:495-510: time_range, with MINUTE, HOUR and DAY at 498-500.
- src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:941-945: duration, with MINUTE, HOUR and DAY at 943-945.
- src/bin/mhfe/self_test.rs:82-97: vectors_cost, with MINUTE at 85.
- Hand-typed estimates in help: src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs:74 and decrypt.rs:74.

Library (all builds):
- src/search.rs:445-449: `[u8; 33]`, against src/packing.rs:45-46 (`STATE_BYTES + 1`).
- src/repair.rs:56-57: FIELD_SIZE = 2048, with POLYNOMIAL at 61, against src/phrase.rs:31 (LIST_SIZE).
- src/strength.rs:110: a literal 1000.0, against src/new_password.rs:27 (MILLIBITS_PER_BIT).

Browser binding: src/wasm_api/passwords.rs:196.
findings.evidence:
Commands run in the mhfe repository (HEAD e8dca53 plus the working tree):
- `grep -rn -E 'const (MINUTE|HOUR|DAY)' src`, with the results above.
- self_test.rs:84-97: `pub fn vectors_cost() -> String { const MINUTE: u64 = 60; const OPERATIONS: u64 = 2; let work = WorkFactor::default(); let (low, high) = work.estimated_seconds(); format!("about {} to {} minutes, {}", (OPERATIONS * low).div_ceil(MINUTE), (OPERATIONS * high).div_ceil(MINUTE), work.memory_text()) }`.
- settings.rs:507-508: `let low = (low_seconds / unit_seconds).max(1); let high = (high_seconds / unit_seconds).max(low);`.
- suite.rs:92-93: `DEFAULT_SECONDS_LOW: u64 = 60`, `DEFAULT_SECONDS_HIGH: u64 = 120`.
- `NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe self-test --help` prints '2 to 4 minutes, 2 GiB.'
- search.rs:445-449: '/// The bits of up to 24 words of 11 bits: 33 bytes, 32 of entropy and one of checksum.' `type WordBits = [u8; 33];` ... `let mut bits = [0_u8; 33];`.
- packing.rs:45-46: `pub(crate) fn with_checksum(entropy: &State) -> [u8; STATE_BYTES + 1] { let mut bits = [0u8; STATE_BYTES + 1];`.
- repair.rs:56-61: '/// Elements of GF(2^11): 2,048, as many as the words of the BIP39 list.' `const FIELD_SIZE: usize = 2048;` ... `const POLYNOMIAL: usize = 0x805;`.
- phrase.rs:31: `pub(crate) const LIST_SIZE: u16 = 1 << WORD_BITS;`.
- strength.rs:110: `return (dice_words * MILLIBITS_PER_WORD) as f64 / 1000.0;`.
- new_password.rs:27: `pub const MILLIBITS_PER_BIT: u32 = 1_000;`.
- wasm_api/passwords.rs:196: `bits: recipe.millibits() as f64 / f64::from(MILLIBITS_PER_BIT),`.
- `git diff --stat` shows the uncommitted changes do not touch these lines.
- A grep of docs/audits/*.md and *.json finds no earlier finding on any of these items.
findings.reproduction:
1. Run `grep -rn -E 'const (MINUTE|HOUR|DAY)' src`. It finds self_test.rs:85, settings.rs:498-500 and terminal.rs:943-945.
2. Compare self_test::vectors_cost (`(OPERATIONS * low).div_ceil(MINUTE)`, which rounds up) with settings::time_range (`(low_seconds / unit_seconds).max(1)`, which rounds down).
   - For an estimate that is not a whole number of minutes, they differ. With low = 70 s, vectors_cost gives (2 x 70).div_ceil(60) = 3, while time_range(140, ...) gives 140 / 60 = 2.
   - With the current constants both give '2 to 4 minutes': `NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe self-test --help` prints '2 to 4 minutes, 2 GiB.'
3. Run `grep -n '33]' src/search.rs`, `grep -n FIELD_SIZE src/repair.rs` and `grep -rn MILLIBITS_PER_BIT src`.
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md rule 6 (lines 47 and 50): 'A value with a meaning ... is a named constant defined once, and one that follows from another is derived from it, never typed again'. AGENTS.md:111: 'Give every magic number, bit width, limit and fixed string a named constant or a comment that says where the value comes from.'
findings.observed:
- MINUTE, HOUR and DAY are defined three times.
- vectors_cost rounds up while time_range rounds down, so one estimate would be rounded two ways. They also differ in units: vectors_cost always writes 'minutes', while time_range switches to hours or days.
- The help texts type the estimate in words: encrypt.rs:74 'At the default settings this takes about two to four minutes.' and decrypt.rs:74 'one to two minutes at the default settings'. This is another hand-typed copy of what WorkFactor::estimated_seconds computes.
- search.rs:446 and 449 type `[u8; 33]`. A comment says where 33 comes from ('32 of entropy and one of checksum'), which meets the readability rule. Rule 6 is still broken, because packing.rs:45-46 and word_wishes/known_answers.rs:201 write `STATE_BYTES + 1` for the same value.
- repair.rs:57 defines `const FIELD_SIZE: usize = 2048`, with the doc 'as many as the words of the BIP39 list'. repair.rs does not import phrase::LIST_SIZE, and no assertion ties the two together.
- strength.rs:110 divides by the literal 1000.0, which is new_password::MILLIBITS_PER_BIT. The only user of that constant is the WebAssembly binding (wasm_api/passwords.rs:196), which converts millibits to bits itself because PasswordRecipe offers no bits().
findings.impact:
The risk is drift only.
- The 'one estimate rounded two ways' cannot happen today. vectors_cost only ever gets WorkFactor::default(), whose estimate is (60, 120) s (suite.rs:92-93, asserted at suite.rs:270). That gives 120 and 240 seconds, both whole minutes, so both formatters print '2 to 4 minutes'. The reviewer's 70 s example is not reachable with the current constants.
- The FIELD_SIZE item is only partly right. 2048 is the size of GF(2^11), fixed by the degree-11 POLYNOMIAL 0x805 as well as by the list size. Deriving FIELD_SIZE from LIST_SIZE alone would not keep POLYNOMIAL in step, and BIP39 fixes the list size, so drift there is unlikely.
- terminal::duration and settings::time_range do different jobs (an elapsed time against a range). Only the unit constants are copied; self_test::seconds already reuses terminal::duration.
- The millibit conversion in the binding is a small boundary conversion, a borderline point rather than a defect.
- Nothing shown to the user is wrong today.
findings.recommendedFix:
- Create one time-units module and one range formatter, used by settings, terminal and self_test. vectors_cost can call time_range on the operation estimate. Build the help sentences at encrypt.rs:74 and decrypt.rs:74 from WorkFactor::estimated_seconds.
- Write search.rs's array as [u8; STATE_BYTES + 1].
- Tie FIELD_SIZE to phrase::LIST_SIZE with a compile-time assertion (`const _: () = assert!(FIELD_SIZE == LIST_SIZE as usize);`) rather than deriving it alone, since POLYNOMIAL fixes the field too.
- Add PasswordRecipe::bits(), or a bits_of(millibits) helper based on MILLIBITS_PER_BIT, and use it in strength.rs and in the binding.
findings.requiredVerification:
- grep finds a single definition of the time units.
- A unit test feeds the shared formatter an estimate that is not a whole number of minutes, and checks that the help, the menu and the settings summary agree.
- The self-test help still prints '2 to 4 minutes, 2 GiB'.
- The compile-time assertion builds.
- The strength unit tests (strength.rs:272-334) and the browser results of passwordStrength and makePassword are unchanged.
- The copy gate and clippy of scripts/check.sh pass.

findings.title: The container fingerprint is recomputed from its rule in four browser bindings and in the command line instead of being asked of the type that owns it.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Not blocking: all paths compute the same fingerprint today, and there is no functional, security or output difference, only a maintainability defect.
findings.evidence:
Commands run in the mhfe repository (HEAD e8dca53 with the uncommitted tree).

1. `sed -n 154,159p src/container.rs`:
   '/// The master key fingerprint of the wallet that the container's own words open without a' / '/// BIP39 passphrase. ...' / `pub fn fingerprint(&self) -> Result<[u8; 4], MhfeError> { wallet::master_fingerprint(&self.words, "") }`.

2. `grep -rn 'master_fingerprint_text(.*"")' src/wasm_api`:
   - repair.rs:88: `let fingerprint = master_fingerprint_text(&repaired.container, "").map_err(js_error)?;`
   - core.rs:245: `container_fingerprint: master_fingerprint_text(sealed.container(), "").map_err(js_error)?,`
   - core.rs:399: fingerprint_without_passphrase for a candidate phrase; not a container, correctly excluded.
   - core.rs:611: `let fingerprint = master_fingerprint_text(&found.container, "").map_err(js_error)?;`
   - core.rs:808: fingerprint_without_passphrase for a recovered phrase; not a container.
   - core.rs:1560: `let fingerprint = master_fingerprint_text(container, "")?;`
   Only core.rs:175 uses the owner.

3. terminal.rs:494 and 498 as quoted above. The callers are encrypt.rs:357 and container_repair.rs:494 (`terminal::print_phrase(container, Wallet::Container, ...)`).

4. The git blame dates as above.

5. A grep of docs/audits/*.md finds no prior finding on this.
findings.reproduction:
1. Run `grep -rn 'master_fingerprint_text(.*"")' src/wasm_api` and compare the results with container.rs:157-158.
2. Read terminal.rs:485-498.

core.rs:399 and 808 also match the grep, but they compute fingerprint_without_passphrase for recovered or candidate phrases, not for containers, so they are correctly excluded.
findings.expected:
Workspace AGENTS.md:57, principle 10 (Delegation): 'Each question is answered by the type that owns the data: the facts of a container say what it allows ... Callers ask them instead of deciding again from word counts or literals.'

Workspace AGENTS.md:49: 'A rule of the library is never written again in the command line, the WASM bindings or the page.'

container.rs:154-156 states the rule: 'The master key fingerprint of the wallet that the container's own words open without a BIP39 passphrase.'
findings.observed:
Only describe_container (core.rs:175) asks the owner: `container_fingerprint: fingerprint_text(facts.fingerprint().map_err(js_error)?)`.

sealed_json (core.rs:245), search_json (core.rs:611), unverified (core.rs:1560) and repair_container (repair.rs:88) call master_fingerprint_text(container, "") themselves.

The CLI's print_fingerprint maps Wallet::Container to the empty passphrase (terminal.rs:494: `Wallet::Container => ("", "of the container itself, not your wallet")`), then calls `mhfe::wallet::master_fingerprint_text(phrase, passphrase)` (terminal.rs:498).

git blame shows the owner method came first: container.rs:154-159 is d52dff8b (2026-10-07). The four binding copies are 3a705db6 (2026-10-09), so they were written after the owner existed rather than being an older pattern.
findings.impact:
A change to what identifies a container would need five front-end edits besides the owner. Until all five were made, describeContainer could disagree with the encrypt, search and repair results.

Limits:
- The computation itself (wallet::master_fingerprint) has a single source.
- Every path passes canonical container words and "", so all copies give the same result today.
- The impact is maintainability only.
findings.recommendedFix: Add one library entry point that ContainerFacts::fingerprint also uses, for example container::fingerprint_of(&str), or add container_fingerprint() methods on Sealed, Found and Repaired that call it. Those three types hold only the container text, not ContainerFacts, so re-reading ContainerFacts in each binding would not be enough. Use the entry point in every binding and in the CLI's Wallet::Container case.
findings.requiredVerification:
- grep finds no master_fingerprint_text(..., "") on a container in src/wasm_api or src/bin.
- A unit test checks the new entry point against ContainerFacts::fingerprint for a published container.
- The browser suites (scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs, scripts/verify-browsers.mjs) and scripts/verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs still give the same containerFingerprint for encrypt, search, repair and describeContainer.

Static check of the current tree. mhfe is at HEAD e8dca53 with uncommitted changes, none of them in the cited files.

1. src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:301-312:
   `let rehearsal_fingerprint = if by_owner && !phrase.verified() { let passphrase = if wallet_passphrase { check::read_passphrase_named(&mut input, Operation::Rekey, check::ORIGINAL_SEED_PHRASE)? } else { LockedText::copy_of("") }; Some(fingerprint_text(master_fingerprint(phrase.phrase(), &passphrase)?)) } else { None };`
   The comment at 298-300 cites 'the specification's re-encryption rules'. Lines 359-372 print the rehearsal command with the fingerprint.

2. src/rekey.rs: the grep above finds no rehearsal-reference API.

3. src/wasm_api/core.rs:802-811: PhraseJson::of sets `fingerprint_without_passphrase: master_fingerprint_text(recovered.phrase(), "")`. It is sent only in ownerCheck (1186-1189). seal (1076-1104) returns sealed_json with no rehearsal reference.

4. docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:269-272: 'For a phrase without a built-in check (`words` 24, or a same-length container), keep a fingerprint of the confirmed phrase for the rehearsal of the new container before sealing: `fingerprintWithoutPassphrase`, or `MhfeWallet.fingerprint()` with the wallet's passphrase.'

5. Neither docs/API.md:286-341 nor web/client.js:527-586 mentions the rehearsal reference.

6. src/mhfe.rs:129-131: '/// Whether the phrase passed its check value. Never true for 24 words or for a same-length container, which have none.'

7. mhfe_spec/README.md:524-525: '...The rehearsal uses the source verifier where the replacement has one, and otherwise a wallet-identity reference, which the application MUST have before it creates the replacement.'

8. multi-chain-wallet-tools at c5b62c2, files untracked:
   - recovery-mhfe-rekey.ts:289 as quoted above;
   - recovery-mhfe-owner-check.ts:78: `if (matches) this.#confirmed = check.fingerprintWithoutPassphrase;`, reset only at line 43.

9. Prior audits: a grep of docs/audits/*.md finds only:
   - the AUD-013 optional note (audit-13-2026-10-08.md:285, 'Replacement rehearsal intentionally belongs to caller workflow'). It is about running the rehearsal, not about who supplies the reference, so it does not settle this finding.
   - AUD-017-API001, a comparable case where 'a page must decide the rule itself', rated Low and not blocking.

Nothing was built or run. The claim is architectural and rests on the code reads and greps above.
findings.reproduction:
1. Read rekey.rs:298-313.
2. Search the library and the binding for an equivalent. `grep -n -i -E "fingerprint|rehears" src/rekey.rs` matches only the import at line 12, doc comments at 111 and 213 about confirming by a fingerprint, and test fixtures (315 and 445-505).
3. Read src/wasm_api/core.rs's seal (1076-1104): it returns no rehearsal reference.
4. Read web/client.js:527-586 and docs/API.md:286-341: neither mentions the requirement.
findings.expected:
mhfe_spec/README.md:522-529 (re-encryption, 'Checking the replacement'): 'The rehearsal uses the source verifier where the replacement has one, and otherwise a wallet-identity reference, which the application MUST have before it creates the replacement.'

Workspace AGENTS.md:35: 'Put all logic in library modules ... no logic is copied from one front end to another'. Also principle 10 (Delegation, AGENTS.md:57), and 'Every feature in the browser too', under which the library, its bindings and the page call one rule.
findings.observed:
The CLI decides the rule itself. rekey.rs:301 reads `let rehearsal_fingerprint = if by_owner && !phrase.verified() {`. When the wallet has a passphrase, the CLI reads it again (check::read_passphrase_named), then calls `master_fingerprint(phrase.phrase(), &passphrase)`. Lines 359-372 print 'rehearse the new container phrase with mhfe check --fingerprint and fingerprint ...'.

The library does not help a caller do the same:
- ConfirmedPhrase (src/rekey.rs:24-55) holds only phrase, wallet_has_passphrase and awaits_owner.
- confirmed_by_owner() clears awaits_owner, so after confirmation the object no longer records that the owner confirmed it. A caller has to track by_owner itself, as the CLI does at rekey.rs:269.

The documents do not carry the rule either:
- docs/API.md's Rekey section (286-341) never mentions the requirement, so a native integrator who follows API.md does not learn of the MUST.
- In the browser the decision is left to page authors, in prose (docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:269-272).

Correction to the reviewer: the binding is not silent. PhraseJson::of (core.rs:802-811) gives every owner check fingerprintWithoutPassphrase, which the documents name as one acceptable rehearsal fingerprint. What is missing:
- the binding never identifies that value as the rehearsal reference;
- it never gives one that includes the wallet's passphrase, which is what the CLI derives;
- it puts nothing in the seal result.

The documents' condition ('words 24, or a same-length container') is equivalent today to the CLI's `!phrase.verified()`: src/mhfe.rs:129-131 says verified() is 'Never true for 24 words or for a same-length container'. Drift on that point is only a future risk.
findings.impact:
A page or native integrator that follows the API alone can seal a replacement without holding the reference its rehearsal needs, and the front ends can apply different rules.

Outside mhfe's scope, the front ends already differ (corroboration only, not executed). The Deriver in multi-chain-wallet-tools (commit c5b62c2; the files are untracked):
- apps/key-derivation/src/ui/recovery-mhfe-rekey.ts:289 uses `sealed.builtInCheck ? undefined : this.#ownerCheck.confirmedFingerprint`. That is always the fingerprint without the passphrase, while the CLI includes the passphrase.
- docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:825 tells pages that MHFE asks for the passphrase 'for the fingerprint to rehearse the new container', and the Deriver does not ask.
- recovery-mhfe-owner-check.ts resets #confirmed only in ask() (line 43), not in dispose() or in the rekey's #start(). A later rekey in the same page session, confirmed by an address and without a built-in check, could therefore show an earlier phrase's fingerprint.

Limits:
- The CLI meets the MUST.
- The browser exposes what a page needs (fingerprintWithoutPassphrase, MhfeWallet.fingerprint()).
- No secret is exposed and the re-encryption guard is not weakened.
findings.recommendedFix:
- Add a library answer, such as ConfirmedPhrase::replacement_rehearsal(). It should know how the phrase was confirmed (by the owner or by a reference) and whether the replacement has a verifier. It returns the source verifier, the reference given, or a reference derived from the confirmed phrase, with the wallet's passphrase where the wallet has one.
- Let the CLI use it.
- Have the binding return it, for example in the seal result.
- Document the MUST in docs/API.md's Rekey section and in the browser documents.
findings.requiredVerification:
- Unit tests of the new library answer for each case, comparing exact fingerprints with the CLI's current output for the same inputs:
  - a source with a built-in check;
  - a 24-word or same-length source confirmed by a reference;
  - a source confirmed by the owner, with and without a wallet passphrase.
- A browser regression in which the seal result of an owner-confirmed 24-word rekey carries the rehearsal reference.
- The CLI's 'Next' line shows the same fingerprint as before.
- docs/API.md and docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md are updated.

findings.reproduction:
1. In the mhfe checkout, extract the three code sets: the string literals returned by MhfeError::code() (src/error.rs:412-466), the first column of the table at docs/API.md:628-679, and the `| "CODE"` members of web/runtime.d.ts:5-147. Sort them in the C locale and compare with `comm -3`.

By reading the gates (no mutation was run; the audit was read-only): adding a code to MhfeError::code(), or renaming a native part's id, fails no step of scripts/check.sh, because the native tests use the constants (src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:198-200). findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md, Object-oriented design and no repetition, rule 6: every rule, constant, message and list of answers has exactly one source; 'A value with a meaning (24 words, a list of lengths, a limit, an error code) is a named constant defined once'; 'A rule of the library is never written again in the command line, the WASM bindings or the page'. The only exceptions, a fast path or a copy a build cannot avoid, each 'says so in a comment next to it, with the reason, and a test keeps both copies in step'. CHECK-ARC-002 asks for duplicated definitions to be recorded with the risk that they diverge.
findings.observed: The copies agree today, but nothing ties them to their source. MhfeError::code() has 50 codes; the API.md table has the same 50; the MhfeErrorCode union has those 50 plus the browser's own BUSY, CALLBACK_FAILED, INVALID_PASSWORD_TEXT, PACKAGE_MISMATCH, SESSION_CLOSED and WORKER_FAILED. The only scripts that name runtime.d.ts are scripts/build-wasm.sh:94 (a plain cp) and scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs:3033-3058, which checks only that exported class, const and function names exist in their modules, not type members. scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs says in its header that it does not find 'a constant written in many places', and scripts/verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs compares refusals for a few inputs only. web/worker-runtime.js:181-188 passes any 'CODE:' prefix through, so a new Rust code reaches pages without being in the union. web/client.js:90-121 types by hand the ids and labels of the native parts memory-locking/'Locked memory', core-dumps/'Core dumps', isolation/'Isolation' and hidden-input/'Hidden input', with no deliberate-copy marker; the tests compare the page's output with further hand copies (verify-browser-package.mjs:4785-4816, verify-browsers.mjs:3226-3229), never with the Rust constants. The memory-locking id and label could come from the library's LockProbe, which is built for wasm32. The bindings pass error codes to whole_number(value, code: &str, name) as string literals ('INVALID_PIM', 'INVALID_MEMORY_LEVEL', 'INVALID_WORD_COUNT', 'INVALID_REPAIR_WORDS', 'INVALID_PASSWORD_SIZE', 'INVALID_REQUEST'), with no comment marking them as copies and no test.
findings.impact: Maintainability only. Every copy agrees today, so no page, type or document is wrong now. A later change can let the TypeScript union, the documented table or the browser's list of parts a page cannot run drift from the library without any gate noticing: a page author would then meet a code missing from the type and the documentation, or the browser's full self-check report would name a part by an id or label the library no longer uses. No security or functional effect is shown. The self-test part of this record concerns the same web/client.js list as AUD-023-ARC005, which reports it from the side of the library's unused WebAssembly branch of LockProbe.
findings.recommendedFix: Following rule 6: (1) give the error codes one source that gates can read, for example a library list of every code() value, and add a gate run by scripts/check.sh (for example in scripts/verify-browser-package.mjs) that the code() set equals the docs/API.md table and equals the MhfeErrorCode union minus a named list of the browser's own codes; (2) take the ids and labels of the parts a page cannot run from the library (for example a list exported with the self-check plan, with LockProbe reporting memory-locking itself in the WebAssembly sets), or, if a copy is unavoidable, mark web/client.js's list as a deliberate copy with its reason and add a test against the Rust constants; fix this part together with AUD-023-ARC005; (3) derive the codes the bindings pass to whole_number() from MhfeError (for example `MhfeError::InvalidRepairWords(..).code()`) or from named constants instead of string literals.
findings.requiredVerification: A gate in scripts/check.sh fails when a code is added to or removed from MhfeError::code() without the same change to docs/API.md and web/runtime.d.ts, and when a native self-check part's id or label differs from the browser's not-run list; show both with a deliberately changed input. `grep -n 'whole_number(.*"[A-Z_]*"' src/wasm_api/*.rs` finds no literal code. scripts/check.sh and the browser package suite pass.

findings.title: .git-blame-ignore-revs names a commit hash that is not in the repository, so git blame does not skip the repository-wide Prettier reformat.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: It is repository tooling metadata only; builds, release artifacts and security are not affected.
findings.affected: .git-blame-ignore-revs:5, in the audited tree (HEAD e8dca53) and in the released v0.6.0 tree; docs/audits/AUD-005-decisions.md:75, which says the file lists f606731. Concerns local git blame with blame.ignoreRevsFile and GitHub's blame view; no build or platform.
findings.evidence:
`cat -n .git-blame-ignore-revs` prints line 4 '# Prettier: the workspace style, double quotes and 100 columns' and line 5 'ff8365c5ef3007525ec5f71f374465aa47c630fd'.
`git cat-file -t ff8365c5ef3007525ec5f71f374465aa47c630fd` prints 'fatal: git cat-file: could not get object info'.
`git branch -a --contains ff8365c5...` prints 'error: no such commit'.
`git log --format='%H %s' HEAD | grep -E 'Prettier|blame'` finds 4dad2bfc 'git blame skips the formatting commit' and f6067310e5acae95b02b5bc96d78007426c8d15a 'Prettier: the workspace style, double quotes and 100 columns'.
`git merge-base --is-ancestor f6067310... HEAD`, and the same against origin/main and v0.6.0, succeed.
`git show v0.6.0:.git-blame-ignore-revs | tail -1` prints ff8365c5....
`git config --get blame.ignoreRevsFile` prints '.git-blame-ignore-revs'; `git blame --ignore-revs-file .git-blame-ignore-revs -- web/client.js` runs with no error or warning.
Plain `git blame -- web/client.js` per-commit counts: 666 d52dff8b, 322 3a705db6, 83 22a1e369, 59 cc91b0ba, 52 f6067310. With `--ignore-rev f6067310...`: 666 d52dff8b, 322 3a705db6, 93 cc91b0ba, 83 22a1e369, 34 ^5ac08b2. So the correct hash would change the attribution, and the current file changes nothing.
docs/audits/AUD-005-decisions.md:75 names f606731 as the listed commit; its notes at :97 and :99 map ff8365c to f606731 (via 1980ab4). `git show f6067310 --stat` shows the added non-format files.
Earlier audits list the file only in source manifests (audit-08, 12, 13 and 14 JSON), and AUD-020-2026-10-12.json:1756 marks it explicitly excluded; no earlier finding covers it.
Verifier: real, reproduced, low, not release-blocking; it noted that a BLD category would fit slightly better than ARC.
findings.reproduction:
In the mhfe checkout (HEAD e8dca53, git 2.53.0):
1. `cat -n .git-blame-ignore-revs`
2. `git cat-file -t $(sed -n 5p .git-blame-ignore-revs)`
3. `git branch -a --contains ff8365c5ef3007525ec5f71f374465aa47c630fd`
4. `git log --format='%H %s' | grep 'Prettier: the workspace style'`
5. `git show v0.6.0:.git-blame-ignore-revs | tail -1`
6. Count lines per commit in `git blame --ignore-revs-file .git-blame-ignore-revs -- web/client.js` and in `git blame --ignore-rev f6067310e5acae95b02b5bc96d78007426c8d15a -- web/client.js`.
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md, Code readability: 'A commit that only reformats is listed in the repository's .git-blame-ignore-revs.' The file's own comment (line 4) names the commit 'Prettier: the workspace style, double quotes and 100 columns', and docs/audits/AUD-005-decisions.md:75 says the repository 'was reformatted once in f606731, which `.git-blame-ignore-revs` lists'.
findings.observed: Line 5 lists ff8365c5ef3007525ec5f71f374465aa47c630fd, which no ref contains (not HEAD, origin/main, the tags, or the backup and audit-snapshot refs). The commit with the subject named on line 4 is f6067310e5acae95b02b5bc96d78007426c8d15a, an ancestor of HEAD, origin/main and v0.6.0. The file was added in 4dad2bf ('git blame skips the formatting commit') and never updated, so v0.6.0 ships the same hash. git gives no warning: blame.ignoreRevsFile is set in the local configuration, git blame runs silently with the file, and it still credits f6067310 with 52 lines of web/client.js, exactly as plain blame does.
findings.impact: git blame with blame.ignoreRevsFile, and GitHub's blame view, do not skip the repository-wide reformat, so blame of reformatted lines points at it instead of the change that wrote them (52 lines of web/client.js alone). The statement at AUD-005-decisions.md:75 is no longer true. Builds, release artifacts and security are not affected. f6067310 is not purely a reformat: it also adds .prettierignore (+20 lines), a .gitignore line and the format CI; it is nevertheless the commit the file means to list.
findings.recommendedFix: Replace line 5 with f6067310e5acae95b02b5bc96d78007426c8d15a, and add a step to scripts/check.sh that checks every non-comment line of the file resolves to a commit (`git cat-file -e "$hash^{commit}"`). Word the commit message neutrally, for example 'the listed hash named a commit that is not in the history'. AUD-005-decisions.md:75 is then true again.
findings.requiredVerification: `git cat-file -t` prints 'commit' for every hash in the file; `git blame --ignore-revs-file .git-blame-ignore-revs -- web/client.js` no longer credits f6067310 and gives the --ignore-rev counts above; the new check.sh step fails when the file holds a hash that does not resolve.
