A provenance record states the values of the build it describes, read from their sources.
findings.observed: package-release.sh:68 writes `echo "Argon2: vendor/phc-winner-argon2 at f57e61e19229e23c4445b85494dbf7c07de721cb"` and :141 `echo "Emscripten 6.0.12" >> "$folder/BUILD-INFO.txt"`. Neither value is read from vendor/phc-winner-argon2.md or from the compiler, neither carries a deliberate-copy comment, and no gate compares them; check.sh:20-21 reads vendor/phc-winner-argon2.md only to check the vendored files' hashes. CITATION.cff:7 is compared with Cargo.toml by no repository gate (release.yml:30-31 compares only the tag with Cargo.toml; only the audit harness docs/audits/AUD-008-harnesses/devops-static.py:99-101 reads CITATION.cff). Nothing compares .node-version with the Dockerfile's NODE_VERSION. The reviewer's wider claim that no test keeps the Dockerfile's toolchain in step is overstated for three values: the Emscripten copies are checked by build-argon2-wasm.sh:14-19, which exits 1 on any other emcc version; the wasm-bindgen copies by Dockerfile.reproducible:71 and build-wasm.sh:38-43; and a Rust change in rust-toolchain.toml alone would pass the Dockerfile's assertion (line 70, run outside the project) but make rustup's cargo proxy install the new channel at `cargo fetch` (line 85) with only the wasm32 target, so the network-free stage would fail loudly at the aarch64 clippy run (lines 103-104) instead of building silently. Cargo.toml:5 rust-version is the minimum supported Rust version, a different meaning, not a copy. Every value matches today.
findings.impact: A bump of the vendored Argon2 commit or of Emscripten in their real sources would leave BUILD-INFO.txt, the provenance record in every archive (the Emscripten line in the browser archive), silently stale; a version bump in Cargo.toml would leave CITATION.cff stale; a Node bump in .node-version would leave the canonical Docker build on the old Node. No mismatch exists today, and the Emscripten, wasm-bindgen and Rust toolchain copies fail loudly on a drift.
findings.recommendedFix: Derive the two BUILD-INFO lines from their sources: read the commit from vendor/phc-winner-argon2.md (and let src/vectors.rs take it from the same source, or keep it equal by a test), and in the Emscripten stage write `emcc --version` to a file that package-release.sh copies. Pass the Node version, and if wanted the Rust version, to the Dockerfile as build arguments that scripts/build-reproducible.sh reads from .node-version and rust-toolchain.toml, or add a check that compares them. Compare CITATION.cff's version with Cargo.toml in release.yml's version step or in scripts/check.sh.
findings.requiredVerification: A check run by scripts/check.sh or the release workflow fails when CITATION.cff's version differs from Cargo.toml's, when .node-version differs from the Dockerfile's NODE_VERSION, and when the Argon2 commit in BUILD-INFO.txt or src/vectors.rs differs from vendor/phc-winner-argon2.md (shown with a deliberately changed copy); a canonical build's BUILD-INFO.txt shows the Argon2 commit and the Emscripten version taken from their sources.

findings.title: The command-line tool writes its 80-column fallback width, its row-count rule and its 78-column line width several times instead of once.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Maintainability only: no output, redraw or secret handling is wrong today.
findings.affected: src/bin/mhfe/style.rs:85-89 (style::rows), :380 (TEXT_WIDTH = 78) and :537 (HELP_WIDTH = 80, not reused); src/bin/mhfe/terminal.rs:314-320 (terminal::rows); src/bin/mhfe/choice.rs:31-33 (LINE_WIDTH = 78) and :244-255 (DrawnRows::rows_at, current_columns); src/bin/mhfe/hidden_input.rs:108-110. Build: the native CLI on every platform.
findings.evidence:
grep output on the audited tree: choice.rs:33 `pub const LINE_WIDTH: usize = 78;`; choice.rs:247 `.map(|width| width.div_ceil(columns.max(1)).max(1))`; choice.rs:254 `hidden_input::columns().unwrap_or(80).max(1)`; hidden_input.rs:110 `let columns = columns().unwrap_or(80);`; terminal.rs:318 `let columns = hidden_input::columns().unwrap_or(80);`; terminal.rs:319 `characters.div_ceil(columns).max(1)`; style.rs:87 `let columns = hidden_input::columns().unwrap_or(80).max(1);`; style.rs:88 `visible_width(line).div_ceil(columns).max(1)`; style.rs:380 `pub const TEXT_WIDTH: usize = 78;`. (Two self-test.rs hits use div_ceil(MINUTE) and are unrelated.)
LINE_WIDTH is used at choice.rs:317, 392, 412, 479, 500 and menu.rs:397, 448; no assert compares it with TEXT_WIDTH.
Zero width cannot occur: hidden_input.rs:726 `(read == 0 && columns > 0).then_some(usize::from(columns))` and :865 `(read != 0 && width > 0).then_some(width as usize)`.
git blame shows the copies came in separate changes: terminal.rs:315-320 and choice.rs:31-33 in 6d3c2b27 (2026-10-02), style.rs:85-88 in 83a5af00 (2026-10-06), choice.rs:252-255 in 9d27a35b (2026-10-06).
No earlier audit (AUD-001 to AUD-022) reports this duplication; the only TEXT_WIDTH and 80-column mentions are AUD-010 interface items about help width.
Verifier: real, reproduced, low, not release-blocking; it suggested placing the fallback in hidden_input, which already owns columns().
findings.reproduction: In the mhfe checkout: `grep -n "unwrap_or(80)\|= 78;\|div_ceil(col" src/bin/mhfe/*.rs`; then `grep -n LINE_WIDTH src/bin/mhfe/*.rs` to see that no test compares LINE_WIDTH with TEXT_WIDTH.
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md, rule 6: 'A value with a meaning ... is a named constant defined once, and one that follows from another is derived from it'; 'Two blocks that differ only in a value become one function with a parameter'; a deliberate copy carries a comment with its reason and a test that keeps both copies in step. CHECK-ARC-002 asks for inconsistent helper implementations to be recorded with the risk that they diverge.
findings.observed: The fallback `hidden_input::columns().unwrap_or(80)`, each time under the comment 'When the width cannot be read, the usual 80 columns', is typed four times: style.rs:87, terminal.rs:318, choice.rs:254 and hidden_input.rs:110. The row rule 'width.div_ceil(columns).max(1)' exists three times: style::rows (style.rs:88), terminal::rows (terminal.rs:319) and choice::DrawnRows::rows_at (choice.rs:247). choice.rs:33 declares `pub const LINE_WIDTH: usize = 78;` with the comment 'As style.rs: 78 columns', a hand copy of style.rs:380 `pub const TEXT_WIDTH: usize = 78`, and no test keeps them equal, so the documented exception does not apply. style.rs:537 `HELP_WIDTH: usize = 80` already names an 80-column terminal, but neither the fallback nor TEXT_WIDTH derives from it. The three row counters already measure width differently: style::rows uses visible_width (style.rs:411; colour codes removed, one cell per character), terminal::Step::visible uses `chars().count()` (terminal.rs:301), and hidden_input uses typed_line::text_cells (hidden_input.rs:108; wide characters count as two cells). The `.max(1)` guard on the columns is applied in two places and left out at terminal.rs:318.
findings.impact: Maintainability: a change of the fallback width or of the row rule would reach only some redraws, and a miscount would show as stale rows left on the screen after a redraw. No present defect is shown: hidden_input::columns() never returns Some(0) (hidden_input.rs:726 on Unix, :865 on Windows), so the missing .max(1) cannot divide by zero, and the copies give the same values today. The differing width measures show that the copies have already begun to diverge.
findings.recommendedFix: Put the fallback where the width is read: a named DEFAULT_COLUMNS (or HELP_WIDTH, if the same meaning is intended) and a hidden_input::columns_or_default() that returns at least 1. Add one rows(cells, columns) function, for example in style.rs, used by style.rs, terminal.rs, choice.rs and hidden_input.rs, and settle one width measure (cells, with wide characters counted as two and colour codes ignored) for all callers. Replace choice::LINE_WIDTH with style::TEXT_WIDTH.
findings.requiredVerification: The grep above finds one width fallback and one row rule in src/bin/mhfe and no second 78-column constant; a unit test of rows() covers an exact fill, a wrap, an empty line and wide characters; the terminal suite (scripts/verify-hidden-input.py and the redraw tests) passes, including in a narrow window.

findings.title: The rehearsal self-check gives the built-in check no case it must refuse and never runs the own-checks or wallet-check references.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: This is a coverage gap of a run-time self-check: the comparison logic is correct today and is covered by unit tests and browser regressions.
findings.affected: src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:59-109 (RehearsalCheck::run and its four cases); src/rehearsal.rs:373-384 (the compare_state arms for BuiltInCheck, WalletCheck and OwnChecks); src/detection.rs:90-101 (passes_own_checks); src/self_check/sets.rs:82 (RehearsalCheck, the only check of the rehearsal comparison). Reached by the CLI's `check --words auto` (src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:259) and by the browser's check with { words: 0 } and the walletCheck reference (src/mhfe.rs:71-76, src/rehearsal.rs:148, src/wasm_api/core.rs:462). Builds: every build with the core (native CLI and browser core module).
findings.evidence:
src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs: line 64 Fingerprint FINGERPRINT, expect matches; line 79 Address, expect the path; lines 92-96 `let outcome = Self::check(&Reference::BuiltInCheck { words })?; expect(outcome.matches(), "the built-in check is reported as not matching")`; lines 99-106 WRONG_FINGERPRINT, expect `outcome == CheckOutcome::DoesNotMatch`.
src/rehearsal.rs:373-384: `Reference::BuiltInCheck { .. } => Ok((CheckOutcome::of(!detection.short_lengths().is_empty()), None))`; `Reference::WalletCheck { passphrase } => Ok((CheckOutcome::of(detection.passes_wallet_check(passphrase)?), None))`; `Reference::OwnChecks { passphrase } => Ok((CheckOutcome::of(detection.passes_own_checks(*passphrase)?), None))`.
src/detection.rs:90-101: passes_own_checks returns true when a short length passes, otherwise the wallet check when a passphrase is given, and false without one.
The grep over every known_answers file finds rekey/known_answers.rs:104, 145, 173, 180 (Confirmation::BuiltInCheck), container/known_answers.rs:41, 42, 236 (ConfirmationNeeded::BuiltInCheck), mhfe/known_answers.rs:631 (short_lengths fixture cases) and rehearsal/known_answers.rs:92 (the one passing case); no Reference::OwnChecks or Reference::WalletCheck appears in any self-check.
Front-end reach: check.rs:259 `(_, _, Some(PhraseLength::Detect)) => Choice::OwnChecks`; mhfe.rs:73 `0 => Ok(Self::Detect)`; rehearsal.rs:148 `Self::Length(PhraseLength::Detect) => Reference::own_checks(passphrase)`; core.rs:462 `"walletCheck" => ReferenceTarget::WalletCheck`.
A refusal case is available from published data without Argon2: zero-24's container is 24 words, so refuse_impossible allows BuiltInCheck{12}, and its recovered state has no short length (the existing VERIFIER_MISMATCH refusal shows this), so compare_state returns DoesNotMatch using the published round keys.
Nothing was executed; the gap was confirmed by reading every known_answers file. No earlier audit (AUD-001 to AUD-022) reports it.
Verifier: real, not reproduced by execution, low, not release-blocking. It noted that the component strictly has one refusal case (the wrong fingerprint), but each reference kind is a separate comparison arm, and that the reviewer's `src/**/known_answers.rs` glob needs globstar, although its stated result is correct.
findings.reproduction:
1. Read src/rehearsal/known_answers.rs:59-109.
2. Search all 17 self-check files: `grep -rn "OwnChecks\|BuiltInCheck\|own_checks\|passes_own_checks\|short_lengths\|passes_wallet_check\|WalletCheck" $(find src -name 'known_answers*.rs')`.
3. By reasoning, not executed (a mutation run needs an edited source tree, which the read-only audit forbids): replace the arm at src/rehearsal.rs:373-376 with `CheckOutcome::of(true)`, or make passes_own_checks return Ok(true); RehearsalCheck::run would still return Passed at both tiers, because no case expects the built-in check or the own checks to refuse.
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md:66 (Self-tests and tests come with every coin and feature): 'The checks must be able to fail: a known answer compares exact output, and a verifier is also given a case it must refuse.' The same section says that a new feature brings its startup checks in the same change and that 'A feature without them is not finished'; the own-checks and wallet-check rehearsal references are live features of the CLI and the browser.
findings.observed: RehearsalCheck::run has four cases, all on zero-12: the matching fingerprint 73c5da0a (expect matches), the BIP84 address at m/84'/0'/0'/0/0 (expect the path), Reference::BuiltInCheck { words: 12 } (expect matches), and WRONG_FINGERPRINT (expect DoesNotMatch). No case gives BuiltInCheck a container on which it must refuse, and no case uses Reference::OwnChecks or Reference::WalletCheck. Nothing else covers these arms at startup or full tier: in the self-checks BuiltInCheck appears only as this one passing case, as rekey's Confirmation::BuiltInCheck and as the container facts' ConfirmationNeeded::BuiltInCheck; the rekey refusal (src/rekey/known_answers.rs:180) goes through RecoveredForRekey::confirm and recover() (src/rehearsal.rs:533-580), a different path from compare_state; ContainerSearchCheck uses only search_decoy with fingerprints. The CheckEvidence fields built_in_check and wallet_check (evidence_of, rehearsal.rs:319-355), which the front ends show, have no self-check either, since RehearsalCheck uses Mhfe::check, which returns only the outcome.
findings.impact: A fault in the rehearsal's built-in-check or own-checks comparison on a user's computer, the kind of fault the startup self-test exists to catch, would let a wrong password rehearse as 'matches' without the self-test noticing. Bounded: the detection primitive LengthDetection::short_lengths is checked at run time by the length-detection fixture cases (src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:618-634) and by the zero-24-as-12 VERIFIER_MISMATCH refusal (:431-434); the wallet-check digest and criterion have passing and failing vectors in WalletCheckProfile; the unit tests every_reference_matches_the_right_password_only (rehearsal.rs:1140) and the_own_checks_detect_the_length (rehearsal.rs:970) cover the logic with the reduced engine; the browser regressions (scripts/verify-browsers.mjs:1440, 1511-1537) cover { words: 0 }. Only the rehearsal's dispatch layer lacks a run-time check, and a fault would have to sit in one match arm. No production defect is shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Add to RehearsalCheck: a refusal case, zero-24's container with Reference::BuiltInCheck { words: 12 } expecting DoesNotMatch; zero-24 with OwnChecks { passphrase: None } expecting the non-matching outcome; a positive case, zero-12 with OwnChecks { passphrase: None } expecting matches with built_in_check 12; and, where a published vector allows it without Argon2, a WalletCheck case with a passphrase that must match and one that must not. Add a unit test that a damaged rehearsal comparison fails the self-check. When the missing 'not verified' outcome of AUD-023-FUN002 is added, extend these cases with it.
findings.requiredVerification: A unit test shows that a changed BuiltInCheck or OwnChecks result (through a test seam or a damaged case) makes RehearsalCheck fail with an exact detail; the new cases pass at startup and full tier and keep the startup suite within its time budget; `cargo test --locked --lib rehearsal` and the full self-test pass.

findings.title: The rekey warning about wallets that other passwords open, with its rule to name a PIM or memory level only when it is not 0, exists only in the CLI binary, so every browser host must write it again, and the existing wordings already differ.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: The CLI meets the specification's MUST and the browser package documents the duty for the host page, so the defect is maintainability and drift risk, not a wrong result; the owner may still apply the AGENTS.md rule that a change breaking these rules is not finished to the next release.
findings.affected: src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:428-447 (keep_until_funds_moved and its doc comment), :151 (the warning shown before the container is read), :134 (the help text) and :607-618 (the only test); src/operation.rs:159-164 (Keep::new, the library's not-0 rule); src/rekey.rs:66-72 ('a front end warns'); web/client.js:528-531 (JSDoc, shipped in dist/core/client.js:530 and dist/runtime/worker.js:277); src/wasm_api/core.rs:886-889 (RekeySession doc comment); docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:887-898 (host duties, shipped as dist/README.md); README.md:283 and :313-314; src/bin/mhfe/check.rs:422-457 (matched_lines). Specification: mhfe_spec/README.md:530-536. Builds: the browser package's core module and every host page that offers rekey (for example the multi-chain Deriver); the CLI meets the requirement.
findings.evidence:
src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:434-447: `fn keep_until_funds_moved(old_work: WorkFactor) -> String { let mut kept = vec!["the old container".to_owned(), "its passwords".to_owned()]; if old_work.pim() != 0 { kept.push(format!("PIM {}", old_work.pim())); } if old_work.memory_level() != 0 { kept.push(format!("memory level {}", old_work.memory_level())); } ...`.
src/operation.rs:159-164: `if work.pim() != 0 { items.push(KeepItem::Pim(work.pim())); } if work.memory_level() != 0 { items.push(KeepItem::MemoryLevel(work.memory_level())); }`.
`grep -rn "pim() != 0|memory_level() != 0" src`: only those four lines.
Built package: dist/README.md:892, dist/core/client.js:530 and dist/runtime/worker.js:277 hold the text only in comments or documentation; `grep -a -c "do not move" dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm` gives 0, and so does 'until you have moved'.
Probe output (exit 130 in both runs after cancelling at the container prompt): with `--pim 0 --mem 0` 'keep the old container and its passwords until you have moved their'; with `--pim 3 --mem 0` 'keep the old container, its passwords and PIM 3 until you have'.
Test rekey.rs:608 the_warning_names_settings_that_are_not_the_defaults asserts the CLI string only.
Earlier audits: a grep of docs/audits for keep_until, matched_lines and 'as the command-line tool does' finds only audit-17:315, which notes that the parity script does not cover rekey; no earlier finding.
Verifier: real, reproduced, low, not release-blocking; it judged the matched_lines half weaker, since the data and its meaning already live in CheckEvidence, and noted that the specification does not require the sentence about the owner's own addresses.
findings.reproduction:
1. `grep -rn 'do not move' src web docs README.md` lists the texts: src/bin/mhfe/rekey.rs:134, :430, :443, :612; src/wasm_api/core.rs:888; web/client.js:530; docs/BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:892; README.md:283.
2. `grep -a -c 'do not move' dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm` and `grep -a -c 'until you have moved' dist/runtime/mhfe.wasm` give 0, and no export of src/wasm_api/core.rs or method in web/client.d.ts returns the warning or its items.
3. Run `mhfe rekey` in a pseudo-terminal and cancel at the container prompt, so no Argon2 runs, once with `--pim 0 --mem 0` and once with `--pim 3 --mem 0` (probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/gap-parity/rekey_warning.py; the verifier's rerun is in probes/skeptic-rekey-warning/rekey_warning.out).
findings.expected: mhfe_spec/README.md:530-536: 'Before replacing a container, applications MUST show every user the same warning, whatever the container. ... Keep the old container, its passwords and its settings until the funds of those wallets have been moved.' Workspace AGENTS.md: 'Put all logic in library modules, never in a command-line or page module'; rule 6: 'A rule of the library is never written again in the command line, the WASM bindings or the page' and 'the same question, list of answers or message is built in one place'; Every feature in the browser too: the command line and the HTML page offer the same operations. The owner's 'nothing to store outside' rule: texts name a PIM or memory level only when it is not 0, as the library's Keep::new already does.
findings.observed: keep_until_funds_moved (rekey.rs:434-447) builds the warning in the binary and repeats the library's not-0 rule (`if old_work.pim() != 0` at :436, `if old_work.memory_level() != 0` at :439), the same rule as Keep::new at src/operation.rs:159-164; a grep finds these four lines as the only places in src that write it. The library only says that 'a front end warns' (src/rekey.rs:68-71). The browser package has no function, field or text for the warning: the built WebAssembly contains neither phrase, and the duty is passed to the host page in prose (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:891-898, client.js:528-531, core.rs:887-889). That differs from Keep, which the package exposes as structured items (core.rs:226-250, MhfeKeepItem in client.d.ts), and from the other-lengths warning, which comes from library data and is bound by scripts/verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs:245-261. The wordings differ: the CLI prints 'keep the old container and its passwords until you have moved their funds', naming PIM and memory level only when not 0; its doc comment (rekey.rs:432) adds 'Your own wallet's addresses do not change.', which the printed text lacks; BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:892-894 says 'its passwords, and a PIM or memory level that is not 0 ... Your own wallet's addresses do not change'; client.js:530-531 says 'its passwords and its settings' and core.rs:889 'its passwords and settings', unconditionally; README.md:313-314 says 'its passwords and changed settings until all decoy or hidden-wallet funds have been moved'; the CLI help at rekey.rs:134 says 'keep the old container until their funds are moved', without the passwords. The only test (rekey.rs:607-618) checks the CLI string alone. A weaker, secondary instance of the same pattern: matched_lines (check.rs:422-457) chooses which own checks to list beside a match (the built-in check only if it was not the reference, the wallet check only on a pass), and the browser asks the page to do it 'as the command-line tool does' (BROWSER-PACKAGE.md:887-890), although the data and its meaning already live in CheckEvidence (src/rehearsal.rs:58-72).
findings.impact: A specification MUST and its settings rule are logic outside the library. Each host (the multi-chain Deriver and any other program) must write the warning again, and nothing keeps the copies in step. A host that follows client.js tells every user to keep 'its settings' even at the defaults, against the owner's not-0 rule; a host that follows the CLI output leaves out the sentence about the owner's own addresses. The 'its settings' wording of client.js and core.rs copies the specification's own sentence, so it is not wrong against the specification, only out of step with the CLI. No secret is exposed and no wrong container is produced.
findings.recommendedFix: Model the warning in the library as Keep is modelled: a rekey method or type that returns the items to keep for the old container (OldContainer, Passwords, Pim(n), MemoryLevel(n)) from one shared 'settings that are not the default' helper, which Keep::new then uses too. Expose it through the WASM core, as a field of describeContainer/readContainer or as a client method that needs only pim and memoryLevel, since the warning must not depend on the container. Render it in the CLI from those items, settle one wording (including whether 'Your own wallet's addresses do not change' belongs to it, and the help text at rekey.rs:134), and replace the copies in client.js, core.rs, BROWSER-PACKAGE.md and README.md with a reference to it. Treat the check evidence the same way: give CheckEvidence a list of passed checks that both front ends render. The rule of AUD-023-ARC010 (the replacement's rehearsal reference after a rekey) also lives only in the CLI and can move to the library in the same change.
findings.requiredVerification: A test binds the CLI text to the library's items for (PIM, memory level) = (0,0), (3,0), (0,2) and (3,2); a browser package test gets the same items from the new client method or field; scripts/verify-cli-browser-parity.mjs, or the browser regression suite, compares the CLI and browser warning for a default and a non-default setting; `grep -rn 'pim() != 0' src/bin` finds nothing.

findings.releaseBlockingReason: This is maintainability and test fidelity only: the limits agree today and both mechanisms work in the probes.

findings.title: The test a_refusal_that_is_accepted_fails passes because a vector is missing, so no test shows that the cipher-rounds self-check's refusals can fail.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: This is a test-quality defect with bounded impact: the self-check's refusals are correct today and pass with the full table, and the library refusal has its own unit test.
findings.affected: src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:1141-1155 (the test, assertion at :1154), :425-473 (CipherRoundsCheck::refusals, three refusals in a local array at :428) and :549-572 (CipherRoundsCheck::run); src/self_check.rs:324-337 (Findings::each). Builds: the library's unit tests; the cipher-rounds startup and full self-check of every build with the core.
findings.evidence:
gdb on the library test binary built by `cargo test --locked --lib --no-run` under the flock and 3G memory-limit wrapper (records in /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/skeptic-cipher-rounds-refusal-meta/): gdb-outcome.log at :1154 prints `$1 = mhfe::self_check::ComponentOutcome::Failed("refusal 1 of 3 a built-in vector is missing")`, then 'test result: ok. 1 passed'; gdb-refusals.log hits only `refusals::{closure#0} (table=...(size=26)) at src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:432`, then 'test result: ok. 1 passed'.
Code: :1154 `assert!(outcome.is_failure(), "{outcome:?}");`; :432 `let result = find(table, "zero-24")?.recovery_at(table, 12)?;`; :438-439 `let vector = find(table, "zero-12")?; let other = find(table, "zero-24")?;`; :477-482 find returns "a built-in vector is missing"; src/self_check.rs:331-336 `if self.failure.is_some() { return; } if let Err(what) = check(item) { self.failure = Some(format!("{noun} {} of {} {what}", index + 1, items.len())); }`; :428 `let checks: [Refusal; 3] = [...]`.
Exact assertions in the same module at :1008-1013, :1032-1038, :1055-1061, :1074-1080 and :1093-1099.
No earlier report (audit-12 to AUD-022) mentions this test or a cipher-rounds refusal meta-test.
Verifier: real, reproduced, low, not release-blocking; it corrected the assertion line (:1154, not :1155) and the impact example.
findings.reproduction:
1. Trace CipherRoundsCheck::run with the table filtered as in the test (zero-24 removed).
2. Read-only execution: build the library tests with `cargo test --locked --lib --no-run`, run a_refusal_that_is_accepted_fails under gdb with a breakpoint at src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:1154 and print `outcome`; run it again with breakpoints at :432 (refusal 1), :438, :439, :450 (refusal 2) and :459 (refusal 3).
3. Scratch edit, not made in the repository: replace the assertion with an exact `assert_eq!(outcome, ComponentOutcome::Failed("refusal 2 of 3 ...".to_owned()))` and the test fails, showing 'refusal 1 of 3 a built-in vector is missing'; replace refusal 2's body with Ok(()) and the test stays green.
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md:66: 'The checks must be able to fail: a known answer compares exact output, and a verifier is also given a case it must refuse.' FULL_AUDIT_GUIDE.md CHECK-ARC-003: broad 'any error' assertions require explicit scrutiny. The test's own comment (:1143-1144) claims that 'the changed container's check cannot run its rounds and stops with another error than VERIFICATION_FAILED', that is, that the test shows refusal 2 can fail.
findings.observed: With zero-24 removed, 26 vectors remain; at startup tier the 9 remaining startup vectors replay with their own salts and pass, and both length rules use zero-12 only. Refusal 1 then fails at `find(table, "zero-24")?` with 'a built-in vector is missing'. Findings::each records the first failure and skips everything after it, so the outcome is Failed("refusal 1 of 3 a built-in vector is missing"), refusals 2 and 3 never run, and check_new_container is never reached. The test asserts only `outcome.is_failure()`, so it passes. Even without that ordering, refusal 2 itself starts with `find(table, "zero-24")?` (:439) and would stop with the same message before check_new_container, so the comment is wrong. No CipherRoundsCheck meta-test reaches any refusal's expect_refusal comparison, and refusal 3 (:458-469) has no meta-test. The refusals are a local array inside refusals(), not a field of CipherRoundsCheck, so a test cannot run one refusal alone. Every other CipherRoundsCheck meta-test (:1001-1100) asserts an exact Failed detail; this one is the only broad assertion.
findings.impact: A weakening of the self-check's own refusal code, for example a refusal body replaced by Ok(()) or a changed expected code, would leave every test green, and the startup self-check would silently lose the refusal case the workspace rule requires. The reviewer's original example was too broad: if check_new_container itself accepted a swapped container, refusal 2 and the_cipher_checks_pass (:956-962) would fail, as would the library's own unit test (src/mhfe.rs:1188-1206). expect_refusal is unit-tested for both failure branches (src/self_check.rs:672-684). No production defect is shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the refusals data of CipherRoundsCheck, like the cases of the other checks, so that a test can run one refusal against a chosen table and assert the exact detail. For refusal 2, give the swap a container that the check accepts: refusal 2 alone, with zero-24's container replaced by zero-12's, must fail with 'refusal 1 of 1 is accepted instead of refused with VERIFICATION_FAILED'. Add the same kind of test for refusal 3, and one that reaches refusal 1's comparison. Replace the broad is_failure() with an exact assert_eq! and correct the comment.
findings.requiredVerification: A meta-test per refusal asserts the exact Failed detail for a case the refusal wrongly accepts; replacing a refusal body with Ok(()) or changing its expected code makes a test fail; the_cipher_checks_pass and the startup self-check still pass; `cargo test --locked --lib known_answers` passes.

findings.title: src/validation_cases.rs runs the same fixtures through a second copy of the self-check runners, with the suite 4 refusal list and the suite-number conversion written twice, and the two copies already check different things.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Maintainability: both copies pass on the current fixtures, and no supported behaviour is wrong.
findings.affected: src/validation_cases.rs:24-281 (unit tests) against src/password/known_answers.rs:43-79 and src/mhfe/known_answers.rs:506-538 and 593-730 (self-check runners). Section pairs verified by reading both sides (listed under reproduction).
Duplicated list at validation_cases.rs:274-276 and known_answers.rs:722-724: `MhfeError::SameLengthNeedsShortPhrase | MhfeError::LengthChoiceNotApplicable { .. } | MhfeError::InvalidContainer(_)`.

Guards: validation_cases.rs:98 and :237 `Mhfe::with_engine(WorkFactor::default(), NoArgon2Calls)`; known_answers.rs:646 and :689 `Mhfe::with_engine(WorkFactor::default(), PublishedRoundKeys::none())`.
Both copies run under cargo test: docs/audits/AUD-023-evidence/baseline-check.log (local only) shows ok at line 146 password::known_answers::tests::the_password_encoding_passes, line 190 mhfe::known_answers::tests::the_cipher_checks_pass (which runs FormatsCheck at Tier::Full, known_answers.rs:956-962), line 202 password::known_answers::tests::the_full_tier_passes, and lines 262-269 all seven validation_cases tests.
History: validation_cases.rs first appears in cc91b0b (2026-09-29); FormatsCheck, PasswordUnicodeCheck and validation_fixtures.rs in d52dff8 (2026-10-07, 0.5.1), so the self-check was written as a second copy of runners that already existed.
No earlier finding reports this; docs/audits mention validation_cases only in test lists, manifests and the AUD-010 note about the three refusal kinds.
Verifier: real, reproduced, low, not release-blocking; it found drift claim 3 (the two Argon2 guards) overstated, added drift items 3 to 5 above, and corrected the second grep's count to three hits, the third unrelated.
findings.reproduction:
1. Read the paired ranges side by side: passwords validation_cases.rs:24-64 / password/known_answers.rs:43-79; settings :66-92 / mhfe/known_answers.rs:599-617; phrases :94-137 / :647-682; length detection :139-164 / :618-636; verifier :166-174 / :637-644; ent_separation :182-230 / :506-538; suite 4 refusals :232-281 / :686-730.
2. `grep -rn 'Some(Ok(4))\|Some(4) => Suite::SameLength' src` finds validation_cases.rs:259 and mhfe/known_answers.rs:712.
3. `grep -rn 'MhfeError::SameLengthNeedsShortPhrase$' src` finds validation_cases.rs:274, mhfe/known_answers.rs:722 and the unrelated exit-code mapping src/bin/mhfe/exit.rs:65.
4. `grep -i deliberate` over the three files finds nothing.
findings.expected: Workspace AGENTS.md, rule 6: every rule, check, validation, conversion and list of answers has exactly one source; a copy found while working is merged in the same change with its tests; the only exceptions, a fast path or a copy a build cannot avoid, are marked by a comment with the reason and kept in step by a test. CHECK-ARC-002 asks for duplicated logic to be recorded with the risk that it diverges.
findings.observed: Each of the seven fixture sections has two runners that read the same JSON (src/validation_fixtures.rs:19-23). The accepted suite 4 refusal list `MhfeError::SameLengthNeedsShortPhrase | MhfeError::LengthChoiceNotApplicable { .. } | MhfeError::InvalidContainer(_)` and the conversion of the fixture's suite numbers 3 and 4 to Suite are each written twice; no library function converts a suite number (Suite::of_container works from the word count, suite.rs:47). Neither runner carries a deliberate-copy comment, and the copy is avoidable: the self-check only needs an engine parameter so that the unit test can pass NoArgon2Calls. The copies already check different things: (1) with both expected_error and expected_nfkd_bytes (fixture cases nfkd-expansion-crosses-limit, PASSWORD_TOO_LONG 1056, and too-long-ascii, PASSWORD_TOO_LONG 1025), PasswordUnicodeCheck::case reads the code and then ignores it (password/known_answers.rs:53-62), while the unit test checks the code and the variant (validation_cases.rs:37-43); (2) mask_input_hex is checked only by the unit test (validation_cases.rs:218-223, against known_answers.rs:534); (3) verifier_hex is compared only by the unit test (validation_cases.rs:173); (4) the suite 3 suite_id is checked only by the self-check (known_answers.rs:595-598); (5) the unit test repeats the fixture-reading helpers in its own form (validation_cases.rs:16-22). 'Before Argon2' is enforced by a panicking NoArgon2Calls in the unit tests and by PublishedRoundKeys::none() returning INTERNAL_ERROR in the self-check; these are different mechanisms but equivalent in practice, since no case expects INTERNAL_ERROR and it is not in the accepted list.
findings.impact: A change to the fixture schema or to the refusal rules has to be made in two runners, and the existing drift shows that one copy can tighten or loosen without the other; the fixture coverage of `cargo test` and of the self-check that users run could then differ. The copy gate cannot see this duplication, since the copies are worded differently (scripts/verify-no-copies.mjs:11-12). Maintenance impact only; no wrong result today. It is the same class of defect as AUD-015-ARC002, a unit test that kept its own copy of a self-check table.
findings.recommendedFix: Make the self-check runners the single source. Give each section runner an engine parameter (impl Argon2Engine), so that the unit test can pass NoArgon2Calls and keep its 'panic if Argon2 is reached' guarantee. Move the stricter checks (the password code alongside expected_nfkd_bytes, mask_input_hex, verifier_hex) into the runners. Then reduce validation_cases.rs to calls of those runners, or delete the tests that the_cipher_checks_pass and the_password_encoding_passes already cover. Name the accepted suite 4 refusal set once, in the library next to the length rules, and the fixture's suite-number conversion once.
findings.requiredVerification: The two greps above each find a single site (apart from the unrelated exit-code mapping); a meta-test shows that the self-check runner now fails on a fixture case with a wrong expected_error code next to expected_nfkd_bytes and on a wrong mask_input_hex or verifier_hex; `cargo test --locked --lib` passes, with the unit tests still panicking if Argon2 is reached; the startup self-check stays within its time budget.

  ECHO WHILE TYPING: b'35142'
  alt screen entered: True

Origin: `git log -S "holds the container alone" -- src/bin/mhfe/encrypt.rs` gives da41728 (2026-10-01); the repair-words feature came in 4242e53. A grep of docs/audits/*.md for "container alone", "holds the container" and "second line" finds no earlier report of either text.
findings.reproduction:
1. `NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe encrypt --help` and read the --stdin paragraph: "Output: the container on one line, printed only after its check has passed. Messages go to standard error, so standard output holds the container alone."
2. Follow the script path in the source: with --stdin, input.is_script() is true, so `person_reads_output` is false (encrypt.rs:223), `screen` stays None, and the branch at encrypt.rs:247-253 prints the container and then, when `sealed.repair_words()` is Some, the card. With `--repair-words N` (N > 0), RepairWordsOption::choose (container_repair.rs:613-619) returns Some(N) also for a script. The labelled facts (Format, Keep, Next) go to standard error through style::fact_as (style.rs:98-103), so the card is the only extra standard-output line.
3. `NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe decrypt --help` and `check --help`: the --stdin paragraphs list the input lines without the card line; with --repair, container_repair.rs:301 reads the card straight after the container, so the decrypt passphrase is then on the fourth line, not the third.
4. Run `target/release/mhfe password --dice` in a pseudo-terminal (local probe /home/user/Documents/bip_tools/tmp/claude/aud023/probes/docs-claims-skeptic/dice_pty.py, not committed) and type the synthetic rolls 35142 one key at a time: the alternate screen is entered, the prompt has no "(hidden)" marker, and the digits are echoed.
Not run: a full-cost `encrypt --stdin --repair-words 4` (2 GiB Argon2; forbidden by the audit's memory rules, and the binary has no low-cost mode). The two-line output follows from the unconditional code path above and from README.md:507-509.
findings.expected: Under CHECK-DOC-001, tool help must match actual behaviour. README.md:507-509 states that "with `--repair-words N` its repair words follow it on a second line of the output"; the encrypt --stdin help should say the same. The decrypt and check --stdin helps should give the full line order with --repair, as README.md:513-515 does ("with `--repair`, the repair words follow the container on their own line"). The dice help should match the program's own prompt rule (terminal.rs:379-385): input is shown on the private screen where one exists and hidden, with the "(hidden)" marker, only where none exists.
findings.observed: encrypt --stdin help says standard output holds the container alone, but with --repair-words N > 0 standard output carries two lines: the container, then the repair words. The decrypt help puts the passphrase "on a third line" and the check help gives its order without the card line, although --repair inserts the card after the container. The --dice help says the five digits are typed "at a hidden prompt", but password --dice runs its steps on the alternate (private) screen, where read_secret uses the prompt without "(hidden)" and echoes the digits. The help text "holds the container alone" dates from da41728 and is older than the repair-words feature (4242e53, v0.5.0), so it is stale rather than intended.
findings.impact: A script written from --help, for example `mhfe encrypt --stdin --repair-words 4 > container.txt` or `container=$(...)`, gets the repair words in the same file or variable and may reject the second line or pass it on as the next standard-input answer. The repair words are not a secret on their own; the risk is a broken script or a confusing backup record, and only when the user explicitly asked for repair words. For decrypt and check, a careful reader of the whole help can work out the order from --repair's own help. The dice wording misdescribes what is visible on screen; the digits appear only on the alternate screen, which is cleared afterwards. No secret leaks and no output is wrong.
findings.recommendedFix: In encrypt.rs stdin_help, say that with --repair-words N the repair words follow the container on a second line of standard output, as README.md:507-509 does, and optionally add a script example. In the decrypt and check stdin_help texts, say that with --repair the repair words come on the line right after the container, so the later answers move down one line. In diceware.rs:99 replace "at a hidden prompt" with the actual behaviour, for example "on the private screen, or hidden where there is none", and correct the doc comments at diceware.rs:243 and 253.
findings.requiredVerification: A command-line unit test (at the test suite's reduced Argon2 cost, or on the function that writes the script output) that asserts standard output of `encrypt --stdin --repair-words 4` is exactly two lines, the container and then the card, and one line without --repair-words. A help-text assertion that the encrypt, decrypt and check --stdin paragraphs name the card line. A pseudo-terminal check, as in scripts/verify-hidden-input.py, that the --dice prompt behaviour (echo on the private screen, "(hidden)" without one) matches the wording of the --dice help.

findings.title: The documents say the startup self-checks take a few hundredths of a second, but in the native tool they take about a quarter of a second, 0.2 s of it a fixed sleep in the container-search check.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A documentation and performance inaccuracy with no effect on correctness, secrets or offline protections.
findings.affected:
Native command-line tool on all platforms: every secret-handling command and the start menu run the startup set. The WebAssembly build is not affected (src/search.rs:345-359 compares the candidates in turn without sleeping).
- Claims: README.md:431-435 ("a few hundredths of a second", line 434); docs/API.md:452 ("tens of milliseconds") and 456 ("milliseconds per part"); src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:5 ("a few tens of milliseconds"); src/self_check/sets.rs:245-246 ("where it takes a few tens of milliseconds"; the comment also sits on the wrong function, `timed`); published notes docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:22 ("in a few hundredths of a second"; to stay unchanged).
- Cause: src/search.rs:265-339 (native compare_candidates; the wait loop at 321-329 sleeps before it checks), src/search.rs:343 (PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS = 100), src/search.rs:147 (search_decoy calls it), src/search/known_answers.rs:101-127 (two search_decoy calls, at 107-109 and 119-121) and 139-143 (run does not depend on the tier), src/self_check/sets.rs:76 (the check is in core() and so in native()).
- Test: src/self_check/sets.rs:274-284 allows 500 ms in a release build (line 279), so it passes at about 240 ms.
findings.evidence:
Code:
- src/search.rs:321-322: `while finished.load(Ordering::Acquire) < workers { std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS));`
- src/search.rs:343: `const PROGRESS_INTERVAL_MS: u64 = 100;`
- src/search/known_answers.rs:107-108 and 119-120: two `search.search_decoy(&reference, super::DECOY_SCAN_GAP, &mut |_, _| Ok(()))` calls in decoy(), which run(_: Tier) calls unconditionally (139-143).
- src/self_check/sets.rs:76: `.with(crate::search::known_answers::ContainerSearchCheck::new())` in core().
- src/self_check/sets.rs:276-280: release budget `Duration::from_millis(500)`.
Documents:
- README.md:434: "They take a few hundredths of a second and are silent when they pass."
- docs/API.md:452: `let report = checks.run_quietly(Tier::Startup); // tens of milliseconds, no live randomness`; 456: "`Tier::Startup` is the check of every start: milliseconds per part".
- src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:5: "The checks take a few tens of milliseconds and a few MiB".
- src/self_check/sets.rs:245-246: "well under half a second in a release build, where it takes a few tens of milliseconds".
- docs/releases/v0.6.0.md:22: "in a few hundredths of a second".
Measurements (release binary; src/search.rs unchanged since 3a705db, so the binary matches the tree for this code):
- Verifier, 5 runs of `/usr/bin/time -f '%e s %U user %M KB' env NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 3 < /dev/null`: 0.25 s / 0.09 user, 0.23 / 0.08, 0.24 / 0.09, 0.24 / 0.08, 0.25 / 0.11.
- Reviewer strace: `clock_nanosleep(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, ...) = 0 <0.100302>` and `<0.100126>`; verifier strace: `<0.100161>` and `<0.100219>`.
- Verifier timeline with -tt (seconds within one run): execve at .1715, first sleep .2233 to .3236, second sleep .3266 to .4267, `read(0, "", 8192)` at .4680, then exit_group(2).
Prior record: audit-15-2026-10-09.md:729 notes, as an informational observation without an ID, "The startup set takes about 246 ms in a release build, 201 ms of it the container-search part"; the documents were not corrected afterwards. AUD-020 to AUD-022 do not mention it.
Not run: the per-check release timing `cargo test --release --locked --lib the_startup_set_stays_within_its_budget -- --nocapture` (the shared heavy-job lock was held by the canonical build); the AUD-015 measurement and the strace timeline cover what it would show.
findings.reproduction:
From the repository root, with the release binary:
  for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do /usr/bin/time -f '%e s %U user' env NO_COLOR=1 target/release/mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 3 < /dev/null 2>&1 >/dev/null | tail -1; done
  /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' target/release/mhfe --version
  strace -f -T -e trace=clock_nanosleep,nanosleep target/release/mhfe repair-words --stdin --count 4 < /dev/null 2>&1 | grep resumed
Add `-tt` to strace for the timeline. Compare the elapsed time with README.md:434, docs/API.md:452/456 and src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:5.
findings.expected: The documents state the measured startup cost. The workspace rule (workspace AGENTS.md:67, "Self-tests and tests come with every coin and feature") asks to "Keep the startup suite fast (milliseconds per check, about a second for all)".
findings.observed: On a nearly idle machine (load average 1.5 on 16 threads) the startup takes 0.23-0.25 s with 0.08-0.11 s user CPU over five runs (7.5 MB peak); with --count 4, which reaches the standard-input read after the checks, 0.24 s three times. The reviewer measured 0.24-0.25 s at load average 6-8 and 0.30-0.38 s at load average 13. `mhfe --version` (and `serve`, hash checks only) take 0.00 s. strace shows the main thread sleeping exactly twice during startup, about 100 ms each; about 40 ms is real work. The container-search part alone takes at least 200 ms, because the native wait loop sleeps 100 ms before it checks whether the workers have finished, and the check calls search_decoy twice although the 8 candidates finish within milliseconds.
findings.impact: Users and integrators are told the start costs a few hundredths of a second; in fact every secret-handling command and the menu wait at least 0.2 s, mostly idle, independent of processor speed. The container-search part strains the workspace rule of milliseconds per check, while the whole suite stays within about a second. The release budget test cannot catch the wrong figure. No security or correctness impact.
findings.recommendedFix: Preferably remove the idle wait: have the waiting thread wake when the workers end (for example a Condvar or park/unpark with wait_timeout for the progress interval), or skip polling for small candidate counts. Then measure on an idle machine and state that figure in README.md:434, docs/API.md:452 and 456, src/bin/mhfe/startup.rs:5 and src/self_check/sets.rs:245-246 (moving that comment onto the budget test). Otherwise correct those places to the real figure, about a quarter of a second. Leave the published v0.6.0 notes unchanged.
findings.requiredVerification: Re-run the timing loop and strace above: no 100 ms sleep remains in the startup path (or the documented figure matches the measurement). Run `cargo test --release --locked --lib the_startup_set_stays_within_its_budget -- --nocapture` and confirm container-search takes milliseconds; consider lowering the release budget at sets.rs:279 so that a regression of this size fails. Confirm the five document locations state the same measured figure.

findings.title: The audit index does not list AUD-022 as a table row, does not link the AUD-020 and AUD-021 JSON companions, and names the replaced base commit 0155c951 (row 29 as "Clean current HEAD") without the replacement note that the records themselves carry.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Audit-record bookkeeping in uncommitted drafts with no product effect; it should be fixed before the records are committed.
findings.affected:
Audit records only, no build.
- docs/audits/README.md (uncommitted modification): rows 29-30 (AUD-020 and AUD-021), the companion list at lines 32-62 (stops at AUD-019), and the separate section at lines 74-76 ("## AUD-022 current-source security review").
- docs/audits/AUD-020-2026-10-12.{md,json}, AUD-021-2026-10-12.{md,json}, AUD-022-2026-10-12.{md,json} (untracked): line 7 of each .md carries the replacement note; the JSON commit maps carry it at AUD-020-2026-10-12.json:5561/5567, AUD-021-2026-10-12.json:1194/1200 and AUD-022-2026-10-12.json:380/386.
findings.evidence:
- `git status --short`: docs/audits/README.md modified; AUD-020/021/022-2026-10-12.{md,json} and their harness folders untracked.
- docs/audits/README.md:29: "| [AUD-020](AUD-020-2026-10-12.md) | 2026-10-12 | Clean current HEAD `0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7`; ..."; line 30: "HEAD `0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7` plus uncommitted host-protection fixes".
- docs/audits/README.md:74-76: "## AUD-022 current-source security review" followed by "[AUD-022](AUD-022-2026-10-12.md) and [JSON](AUD-022-2026-10-12.json), completed 2026-10-12 UTC at `0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7` plus pre-existing dirty changes."
- `grep -n -o 'AUD-02[0-2]-2026-10-12\.json' docs/audits/README.md` prints only `76:AUD-022-2026-10-12.json`.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7 HEAD` returns 1; HEAD is e8dca53a5d17cb80f1f5ac1f5a40b351f939e7e7.
- `git reflog show refs/remotes/origin/main`: 0155c95 was pushed to origin/main on 2026-10-12 and replaced by e8dca53 on 2026-10-13.
- `git ls-remote origin` (non-tag refs): HEAD and refs/heads/main = e8dca53a5d17..., plus refs/pull/1..12/head; no audit-snapshot ref. `git for-each-ref refs/audit-snapshots` (local): AUD-020-reviewed-base -> 0155c951.
- AUD-020/021/022-2026-10-12.md line 7: "original reviewed base `0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7` is retained under a local audit-snapshot ref and was replaced on main by `e8dca53a5d17cb80f1f5ac1f5a40b351f939e7e7`. ... product files outside `docs/audits/` are byte-for-byte unchanged between these commits."
- docs/audits/README.md:68 and 72: earlier documentation-only amendments map replaced commits to their replacements in the index (line 68 names AUD-015-DOC001).
- Naming conflict: multi-chain-wallet-tools/docs/audits/AUDIT_STANDARD.md:11 "Filenames keep the existing convention: `audit-18-2026-09-18.md`"; workspace AGENTS.md:156 makes AUDIT_STANDARD the model for "numbering, finding IDs, severity, status, required content" and names the wallet-full-audit skill as the entry point; SKILL.md:20 "Reports: `<repository>/docs/audits/AUD-NNN-<date>.md` and `.json` ... (multi-chain-wallet-tools uses its own sequence and filename convention ...)". mhfe's AUD-023 harness README says its assembler writes `docs/audits/audit-23-<date>.md`, so mhfe already mixes both forms.
findings.reproduction:
From the repository root:
  git status --short docs/audits
  sed -n 26,31p docs/audits/README.md
  sed -n 74,76p docs/audits/README.md
  grep -n -o 'AUD-02[0-2]-2026-10-12\.json' docs/audits/README.md      # prints only 76:AUD-022-2026-10-12.json
  git merge-base --is-ancestor 0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7 HEAD; echo $?   # prints 1
  git ls-remote origin                                                   # refs/heads/main = e8dca53..., no audit-snapshot ref
  git for-each-ref refs/audit-snapshots                                  # local ref only
  sed -n 7p docs/audits/AUD-020-2026-10-12.md
findings.expected: The workspace audit skill (.github/skills/wallet-full-audit/SKILL.md:23) says "Index: append a row to `<repository>/docs/audits/README.md`". The index's own pattern links the JSON companion of every record (lines 32-62 for AUD-001 to AUD-019). The workspace rules (AGENTS.md, Commits) say a commit that an audit record names by its hash is rewritten only together with that record, whose hashes are then updated; earlier amendments in this index mapped replaced commits to their replacements in the index itself (README.md:68 and 72; AUD-015-DOC001).
findings.observed:
AUD-020 and AUD-021 are table rows 29-30, but AUD-022 is a separate section after "Privacy metadata" (lines 74-76), not a row. The JSON companions of AUD-020 and AUD-021 are linked nowhere; only AUD-022's JSON is linked (line 76). Rows 29-30 and line 76 name 0155c951ab9deee0301b7e37b42ebc994cbd28b7, and row 29 calls it "Clean current HEAD". That commit is not an ancestor of HEAD e8dca53, origin's main is e8dca53, and the only remaining ref to 0155c951 is the local refs/audit-snapshots/AUD-020-reviewed-base. The three records note that the base "was replaced on main by `e8dca53a5d17cb80f1f5ac1f5a40b351f939e7e7`" and that product files outside docs/audits/ are byte-for-byte unchanged; the index does not.
The reviewer also reported the AUD-NNN-<date> filenames as a breach of multi-chain-wallet-tools/docs/audits/AUDIT_STANDARD.md:11. The verifier refuted that part: the workspace skill (SKILL.md:20) prescribes `<repository>/docs/audits/AUD-NNN-<date>.md` and describes the audit-NN form as multi-chain-wallet-tools' own convention, mnemocode names every record AUD-NNN-<date>, and mhfe_spec's newest record is AUD-008-2026-10-12.md. What remains is a conflict between two procedure documents, which leaves mixed names in mhfe; it is not a defect of these records, and the rename advice is dropped.
findings.impact: A reader following the index reaches a reviewed base that no branch contains and is told it is the current HEAD; GitHub may still serve it by hash, but a later garbage collection may not, and only a local ref keeps it. The AUD-020 and AUD-021 JSON companions cannot be found from the index, and AUD-022 is missed by anyone reading the table. All of this is in uncommitted drafts: nothing is published and product behaviour is unaffected.
findings.recommendedFix: Before committing the records: make AUD-022 a row of the table; add the AUD-020, AUD-021 and AUD-022 JSON companions to the companion list; in the AUD-020, AUD-021 and AUD-022 entries name e8dca53 beside 0155c951 with the note the records already carry (product files outside docs/audits/ byte-for-byte unchanged); remove "current" from row 29. Do not rename the files to audit-NN form on the strength of AUDIT_STANDARD.md:11 alone; resolve the filename conflict between AUDIT_STANDARD.md:11 and SKILL.md:20 in the procedure documents and then apply one convention in mhfe.
findings.requiredVerification: `grep -n 'AUD-02[0-2]-2026-10-12.json' docs/audits/README.md` lists all three companions; AUD-022 appears as a table row; for every 40-hex commit named in docs/audits/README.md, either `git merge-base --is-ancestor <hash> origin/main` succeeds or the index states its replacement; the Markdown and JSON of each record still agree after the edit.

findings.title: CITATION.cff and Cargo.toml label the dual-licensed working tree as version 0.6.0, although the project states that 0.6.0 was released under the MIT license alone.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A metadata inconsistency in the unreleased tree; the release workflow refuses a tag that does not match the Cargo version, so the next release must set a new version anyway.
findings.affected:
Every build of the tree from e8dca53 on (native tool, browser package, canonical archives).
- CITATION.cff:7-10 (`version: 0.6.0` with `license: [MIT, Apache-2.0]`).
- Cargo.toml:3 (`version = "0.6.0"`) and 9 (`license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`), and so Cargo.lock's package entry, `mhfe --version`, dist/modules.json:2 (through scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:12-13) and the canonical archive version tag (scripts/build-reproducible.sh:7-13).
- Contradicted by README.md:644-647 ("Releases up to 0.6.0 were published under the MIT license alone", lines 645-646) and docs/releases/unreleased.md:11-13 (the dual licence listed as a change after 0.6.0).
findings.evidence:
- `cat CITATION.cff`: lines 7-10 `version: 0.6.0`, `license:`, `- MIT`, `- Apache-2.0`.
- `grep -n '^version\|^license' Cargo.toml`: `3:version = "0.6.0"`, `9:license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`.
- `git diff v0.6.0 HEAD -- CITATION.cff Cargo.toml`: only the licence lines change (`-license: MIT` to the MIT and Apache-2.0 list; `-license = "MIT"` to `+license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"`); the version stays 0.6.0.
- README.md:645-646: "Releases up to 0.6.0 were published under the MIT license alone and remain available under it." docs/releases/unreleased.md:11-12 under "Changed": "MHFE is licensed under the MIT license or the Apache License 2.0, at your option ... releases up to 0.6.0 remain available under the MIT license."
- `git ls-tree --name-only v0.6.0 | grep -i licen` prints `LICENSE`; at HEAD `LICENSE-APACHE` and `LICENSE-MIT`.
- `target/release/mhfe --version` prints `mhfe 0.6.0`; dist/modules.json:2 `"version": "0.6.0"`.
- scripts/write-package-manifest.mjs:12-13 reads the version from Cargo.toml; scripts/build-reproducible.sh:7-13 builds the archive version as "v" + the Cargo version.
- `git log -p -- CITATION.cff`: 1ab48aa 0.3.0 to 0.3.1; cc91b0b 0.3.1 to 0.4.0; aedd4ce to 0.5.0; d52dff8 0.5.0 to 0.5.1; 3a705db 0.5.1 to 0.6.0; e8dca53 no version change. Cargo.toml line 3 has the same history. Tags exist only for v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.5.0 and v0.6.0.
- .github/workflows/release.yml:30-31: `test "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" = "v$package_version"`, so a release forces a Cargo bump. A grep for CITATION in scripts/, tests/ and .github/ finds nothing.
- AUD-019 to AUD-022 report nothing on CITATION or the version; AUD-020 excluded fresh licence and release claims.
findings.reproduction:
From the repository root:
  cat CITATION.cff
  grep -n '^version\|^license' Cargo.toml
  git diff v0.6.0 HEAD -- CITATION.cff Cargo.toml
  sed -n 642-647p README.md
  sed -n 9,13p docs/releases/unreleased.md
  git ls-tree --name-only v0.6.0 | grep -i licen; ls LICENSE*
  target/release/mhfe --version
  sed -n 2p dist/modules.json
findings.expected: Version and licence metadata agree with the project's own statements (CHECK-DOC-002, metadata and legal materials); CHECK-DOC-001 notes that a source version is not proof of a published release. The project's history bumps CITATION.cff and Cargo.toml together in the first substantive commit after a release (1ab48aa 0.3.0 to 0.3.1; d52dff8 0.5.0 to 0.5.1).
findings.observed: e8dca53 changed the licence from MIT to MIT OR Apache-2.0 in CITATION.cff and Cargo.toml but left the version at 0.6.0. The tagged v0.6.0 tree carries only `LICENSE`; HEAD carries `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE`. Builds of this tree report `mhfe 0.6.0` and dist/modules.json reports `"version": "0.6.0"`, although they differ from the v0.6.0 release in licence and in unreleased fixes. A canonical build of this tree would produce archives labelled v0.6.0 that differ from the published v0.6.0 archives. No script or test compares the CITATION.cff version with Cargo.toml.
findings.impact: A citation or package-metadata consumer records version 0.6.0 as MIT OR Apache-2.0, contradicting the README and the published 0.6.0 artefacts. Bug reports from main-branch builds cannot be told apart from the 0.6.0 release by version string; the browser buildId still distinguishes builds. No security or functional effect.
findings.recommendedFix: Bump the unreleased tree to the next version (for example 0.6.1, following the 0.5.1 precedent) in Cargo.toml (and so Cargo.lock), CITATION.cff and the package manifest, or keep CITATION.cff describing the latest release (version 0.6.0, license MIT) until the next release changes both together. Add a check that the CITATION.cff version equals the Cargo.toml version.
findings.requiredVerification: `grep -n '^version' Cargo.toml` and `grep -n '^version' CITATION.cff` agree and no longer pair 0.6.0 with the dual licence; `mhfe --version` and dist/modules.json report the new version after a rebuild; the new consistency check fails on a deliberately mismatched CITATION.cff version and passes on the fixed tree.

findings.title: docs/DEVELOPMENT.md sends readers to AGENTS.md for the wasm-bindgen and Emscripten toolchains, but AGENTS.md does not mention wasm-bindgen and describes Emscripten only as a path in the maintainer's workspace.
findings.releaseBlockingReason: A developer-documentation gap with no build, security or format consequence; the build scripts refuse a wrong toolchain version with a clear message.
findings.affected:
Browser-package builds from source by a contributor who follows the public developer guide.
- docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:3-4 ("Use the toolchains and workspace rules in AGENTS.md") and 16-17 ("Browser builds also need wasm-bindgen and Emscripten, as AGENTS.md describes."); the file is new in e8dca53.
